11:1: Abu Ja`far said: We have mentioned the differences of opinion among the people of interpretation regarding the interpretation of His statement: Alif Lam Ra, and the correct statement regarding that, according to us, is based on its evidence, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. His saying: A Book whose verses are perfected, means: This is the Book that God revealed to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is the Qur’an. He raised his saying: Book, with the intention: (This is a book). As for the statement of those who claim that his saying: Alif Lam Ra, refers to all the letters of the alphabet with which the Qur’an was revealed, and these letters were made an indication of all of them, and that the meaning of the statement is: These letters are a Book whose verses are perfected, then the Book, according to his statement, should be raised by his saying: Alif Lam Ra. As for his saying: His verses are perfected and then explained in detail, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of it. Some of them said: Its interpretation is that its verses are perfected with commands and prohibitions, then they are detailed with reward and punishment. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abu Muhammad Al-Thaqafi told me, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: A Book whose verses are perfected and then detailed, he said: It is perfected in the command and prohibition, and detailed in the reward and punishment. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Abdul Karim bin Muhammad Al-Jurjani told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali, on the authority of Al-Hasan: “Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book whose verses are perfected.” He said: It is perfect in commands and prohibitions, and detailed in threats. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Hasan: “Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book whose verses are perfected,” he said: with commands and prohibitions, then explained in detail, he said: with reward and punishment. It was narrated from Al-Hasan that he said something contrary to this, and that is: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said, and Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: I have made it clear, with reward and punishment, then I have made it clear, with command and prohibition. Others said: The meaning of this is: His verses are perfected, from falsehood, then they are explained in detail, so He made clear from them what is permissible and what is forbidden. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: “Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book whose verses are perfected and then presented in detail from One Who is Wise and Acquainted.” God perfected it from falsehood, then presented it in detail with His knowledge, so He made clear what is lawful and what is unlawful, and what is obedience to Him and what is disobedience to Him. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: His verses are perfected and then explained in detail, he said: God perfected them from falsehood, then explained them in detail. Abu Jaafar said: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said: Its meaning is: God made His verses perfect from interference, error, and falsehood, then separated them with commands and prohibitions. This is because perfecting something means correcting and perfecting it, and perfecting the verses of the Qur’an means perfecting them from any defect in them or falsehood that might lead a deviant to attack them. As for the details of its verses, it is distinguishing some of them from others, by clarifying what is in them of what is permissible and what is forbidden, and what is commanded and forbidden. Some commentators interpreted his statement, I have explained as meaning: I have interpreted, and this is similar to what we have said about it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, he said, Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: Then it was explained, he said: It was explained. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: It was explained, he said: It was interpreted.... He said, Muhammad bin Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, it reached me on the authority of Mujahid: Then it was explained, he said: it was interpreted. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Qatada said: Its meaning is: I made it clear. We mentioned the narration of that before, and it is similar in meaning to what Mujahid said. As for his saying, From the side of the Wise, the All-Knowing, its meaning is: Wise, in managing and estimating things, All-Knowing, in what their consequences will lead to. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: From the side of the Wise, the All-Knowing, he said: From the side of the Wise, the All-Knowing.
11:2: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: Then He detailed that you should worship none but God alone, with no partner for Him, and that you should renounce all gods and rivals. Then God Almighty said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the al-Nas 114:I am to you, from God, a warner, warning you of His punishment for your disobedience and worship of idols, and a bearer of good tidings, giving you good tidings of the abundant reward for obeying Him and sincerely worshipping and devoting oneself to Him.
11:3: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: Then He detailed His verses, that you worship none but God, and that you seek forgiveness from your Lord. What He means by His statement: And that you seek forgiveness from your Lord is that you should do, O people, deeds that will please your Lord, so that He will cover for you the great sins that you committed by worshipping idols and statues, and associating other gods and rivals with Him in His worship. And His statement: Then repent to Him, means: Then return to your Lord with sincere worship of Him, without anything else that you worship besides Him, after you have renounced rivals and declared your innocence from worshipping them. That is why it was said: And seek forgiveness from your Lord, then repent to Him, and He did not say: And repent to Him, because repentance means returning to working in obedience to God, and seeking forgiveness is seeking forgiveness for the polytheism that they were residing in. And working for God is not working for Him except after abandoning polytheism with Him. As for polytheism, its work is only for Satan, so that is why the Most High commanded them to repent to Him after seeking forgiveness for polytheism, because the polytheists thought that they were obeying God with many of their actions, while they were residing in their polytheism. And His statement: He will grant you good enjoyment for a specified term, the Almighty says to the polytheists whom He addressed with these verses: Seek forgiveness from your Lord and then repent to Him, for if you do that, He will expand for you the world, provide for you from its adornments, and prolong your lifespans until the time when He decrees death for you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: He will grant you good enjoyment for a specified term, so you are in that enjoyment, so obey God and know His right, for God is a benefactor who loves those who are grateful, and those who are grateful will have more from God, and that is His decree that He has decreed. His saying: for a specified term, means death. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Until a specified term, he said: death. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: for a specified term, which is death. Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: Until a specified term, he said: death. As for his saying: And He will give every possessor of virtue his virtue, it means: He will reward everyone who bestows the virtue of his wealth, strength, or kindness upon another, seeking reward for that and intending thereby the face of God, with the most generous reward and virtue in the Hereafter, as: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And every possessor of virtue will be given his virtue, he said: what he counted from his wealth or the work with his hand or foot or word, or what he volunteered from his entire affair. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said -...And Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, in a similar manner, except that he said: Or he worked with his hands or feet and his speech, and whatever he prolonged of his entire affair. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, in a similar manner, except that he said: And what he spoke of his entire affair. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And every possessor of virtue will be given his virtue, meaning: in the Hereafter. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he used to say in interpretation of that: It was narrated to me on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Sharik, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, regarding his statement: And every possessor of virtue will be given his virtue, he said: Whoever does a bad deed, a bad deed will be recorded against him, and whoever does a good deed, ten good deeds will be recorded for him. If he is punished for the bad deed he did in this world, ten good deeds will remain for him. If he is not punished for it in this world, one of the ten good deeds will be taken, and nine good deeds will remain for him. Then he says: He is doomed whose ones outweigh his tenths! And His statement: But if they turn away, then indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great Day, God Almighty says: And if they turn away from what I have called them to, of sincere worship of God and abandoning the worship of deities, and refrain from seeking forgiveness from God and repenting to Him, and turn away from that, then indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great Day, the affair of which is great in its terror, and that is the Day when every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged. And He, the Most High, said: But if you turn away, then I fear for you the punishment of a great Day, but it is something that may be preceded by a statement, and when the Arabs precede a statement with a statement, they address, then return to reporting on the absent, then return to addressing. We have explained this in more than one place, so there is no need to repeat it here.
11:4: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: To God, O people, is your return and destiny, so beware of His punishment if you turn away from what I call you to, which is repentance to Him from your worship of gods and idols, for He will make you abide in the fire of Hell if you perish in your polytheism before repenting to Him. And He is over all things competent, meaning: He is able to revive you after your death, and punish you for associating idols with Him, and other things that He intended for you and others.
11:5: Abu Jaafar said: The readings differed in the reading of His statement: Behold, they are bending their chests. The majority of the readers of the regions read it as: Behold, they are bending their chests, on the basis of (yaf'alun) from (thanayt), and (al-sudur) is in the accusative case. Readers of this also differed in their interpretation of it. Some of them said: This was the action of some hypocrites. Whenever they passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they would cover their faces and bend their backs. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad, regarding his statement: “Behold, they turn their breasts away to hide themselves from Him. Behold, when they cover themselves with their garments,” he said: When one of them passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would throw his garment over his face and turn his back. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham told us, Hisin told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad bin Al-Had, regarding his statement: Indeed, they turn their chests away to hide themselves from Him, he said: from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: When the hypocrites passed by him, one of them would bend his chest and lower his head. So God said: Indeed, they bend their chests, the verse. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, he said: I heard Abdullah bin Shaddad say regarding His statement: They fold their chests, he said: When one of them passed by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would fold his chest and cover himself with his garment, so that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not see him. Others said: Rather, they did that out of ignorance of God, and thinking that God was unaware of what their hearts concealed if they did that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: They turn their chests away, he said: doubt and distrust of the truth, to hide from God if they are able. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: They turn their chests away, doubting and disputing the truth, to hide from Him, he said: from God if they are able. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: They fold their chests, he said: They become narrow with doubt. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: They turn their chests away, he said: They become narrow with doubt and skepticism about the truth. He said: To hide from Him, he said: From God if they are able. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Hudha told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement: “Indeed, they turn away their breasts to conceal themselves from Him. Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments,” he said: Out of their ignorance of Him, God said: Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, in the darkness of the night, in the interior of their homes, He knows, at that hour, “what they conceal and what they declare. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.” Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin: “Behold, they turn their chests to hide themselves from Him. Behold, when they cover themselves with their garments.” He said: One of them would bend his back and cover himself with his garment. Others said: They only did that so that they would not hear the Book of God. Who said that? Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, they bend their chests, the verse. He said: They were bending their chests so that they would not hear the Book of God. God Almighty said: Indeed, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they declare, and that is the most hidden thing that the son of Adam can be, when he bends his chest, covers himself with his garment, and conceals his concern in himself, for God does not hide that from Him. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: They cover themselves with their garments, he said: The most hidden thing a person can be is when he conceals something in his soul and covers himself with his garment, then that is the most hidden thing he can be, and God knows what is in their souls, and God knows what they conceal and what they declare. Others said: This is only an announcement from God to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the hypocrites who harbored enmity and hatred towards him, and showed him love and affection, that they were with him and of his religion. God, the Most High, says: But they conceal their hearts in disbelief in order to hide themselves from God. Then God, the Most High, informs that their secrets and their open actions are not hidden from Him. Others said: They used to do that when they talked to each other. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: Behold, they turn their breasts aside to hide themselves from Him, he said: This is when some of them are conversing with one another. And he recited: Behold, when they cover themselves with their garments, the verse. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite this: Indeed, their breasts turn me away, on the example of: The fruit is thawuli, “Tafa’u’l.” He told us... He said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas recite: Behold, they turn their breasts away from Me. He said: They would not come to women or to the toilet except after covering themselves with their clothes, out of dislike of exposing their private parts to the sky. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, I heard Muhammad Ibn Abbad Ibn Ja`far say, I heard Ibn Abbas recite it: Indeed, their breasts turn away from Me. He said: I asked him about it and he said: There were people who were ashamed to relieve themselves and go to the sky, and to get a wound and go to the sky. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the interpretation of this, which is: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said, I was told on the authority of Ikrimah: Ibn Abbas recited: (Indeed, their breasts turn Me aside), and Ibn Abbas said: (their breasts turn Me aside), doubting God, and doing evil deeds covering themselves with their garments, he is arrogant or hides himself from God, and God sees him, He knows what they conceal and what they declare. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he recited: Indeed, their breasts turn Me away. Ikrimah said: Their breasts turn Me away. He said: Doubting God and doing evil deeds, so he covers himself with his garments and seeks refuge from God, while God sees him and knows what they conceal and what they declare. Abu Ja`far said: The correct reading of this, according to us, is what the countries read, which is: Alas, they bend their chests, on the example of they do, and the chests, in the accusative case, meaning: they bend their chests and conceal them, as in: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: They turn their chests away, meaning: they use a metaphor. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Behold, they turn away their breasts, he says: they conceal what is in their hearts, Behold, when they cover themselves with their garments, he knows what they did by night and by day. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Indeed, they turn their breasts away, meaning: They turn their breasts away. Abu Jaafar said: This interpretation, which Al-Dahhak interpreted according to the method of Ibn Abbas’s reading, except that the one who told us this is how he mentioned the reading in the narration. Abu Ja`far said: If the reading we mentioned is the more correct of the two readings in this regard, due to the consensus of the proof from the readings on it, then the most correct of the interpretations is the interpretation of the one who said: They were doing this out of ignorance of God, that He is unaware of what their souls conceal, or what they whisper to Him among themselves. We said that this is the most appropriate interpretation of the verse, because His statement, that they may hide from Him, means: that they may hide from God, and that the ha in His statement, from Him, refers to the name God, and Muhammad was not mentioned before, so it would be more appropriate to mention him, peace and blessings be upon him, while it is in the context of reporting on God. So since that is the case, it would be more appropriate to mention God. And if it is true that this is the case, then it is known that they did not think to themselves that they were hiding from God, except out of their ignorance of Him. So God, the Most High, informed them that the secret of their affairs and their openness is not hidden from Him, regardless of their condition, whether they cover themselves with clothing or appear in defecation, so He said: Except when they cover themselves with their garments, meaning: they cover themselves with their garments, cover themselves with them and wear them. It is said: He covered himself with his garment, he covered himself with it. God said: And they covered themselves with their garments, (Nuh 71:7), and Al-Khansa’ said: I watch the stars, but I am not burdened with watching them, and sometimes I am covered with the excess of my treasures He knows what they conceal, says the Most High: He knows what these ignorant people conceal about their Lord, who think that God is unaware of what their hearts conceal when they bend them over what is in them and fold them, and what they whisper among themselves and conceal it, and what they declare, the secrets of His servants and their public affairs are the same to Him. He is Knowing of what is in the breasts, says the Most High: God is the One with knowledge of everything that the breasts of His creation conceal, of faith and disbelief, truth and falsehood, good and evil, and what you conceal of what you have not yet committed, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Not when they cover themselves with their garments, he said: they cover their heads. Abu Ja`far said: Beware lest your Lord looks upon you while you are harboring doubt in your hearts about something related to His Oneness, or His command or prohibition, or about what He has obligated you to believe in and confirm, and you perish because of your belief in that. Part eleven of volume six is done Followed, God willing, by the twelfth part of the seventh volume. The first: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision. Hud 11:6
11:6: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty meant by His saying: And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, and no creature creeps on the earth. The active animal, from daba, so he crawls, and he is daba, and she is a beast. Except that her provision is from God, meaning: except that her provision is from God, which reaches her, and He is responsible for it, and that is her strength, her food, and what sustains her. Some of the interpreters said something similar to what we said about this. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Mujahid said regarding His statement: And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, he said: Whatever provision comes to us is from God, and perhaps He does not provide for it until it dies of hunger, but whatever provision there is is from God. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, he said: Every creature. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Dahhak say regarding His statement: And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, meaning every creature, and people are among them. Some of the scholars of the Arabic language from Basra claimed that all money is a beast, and that the meaning of the statement is: and what is a beast on the earth, and that min is redundant. His saying: And He knows its resting place, where it settles, and that is its shelter to which it takes refuge at night or during the day, and its depository, the place where it is deposited, either by its death in it, or by burying it. A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about this. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Its resting place is where it takes refuge, and its repository is where it dies. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And He knows its resting place, meaning where it takes refuge, and its depository, meaning when it dies. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And He knows its place of rest and its place of storage. He said: The place of rest is where it takes refuge, and the place of storage is where it dies. Others said: Its resting place is in the womb, and its repository is in the loins. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And He knows its place of rest, in the womb, and its place of deposit, in the loins, like that of livestock. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And He knows its place of rest and its place of deposit. So the place of rest is what is in the womb, and the place of deposit is what is in the loins. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And He knows its place of rest, meaning: in the womb, and and its depository, meaning: in the loins. Others said that the stable place is in the womb, and the warehouse is where you die. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father, Ya’la, and Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah: And He knows its place of rest and its place of deposit. He said: Its place of rest is the wombs, and its place of deposit is the land in which it dies. He said: Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah: And He knows its place of rest and its place of storage. The place of rest is the womb, and the place of storage is the place where it dies. Others said: Her resting place is the days of her life, and her warehouse is where she dies. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa`d told us, he said, Abu Ja`far told us, on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas, regarding his statement: And He knows its place of rest and its place of deposit. He said, its place of rest means the days of its life, and its place of deposit means where it dies and from where it will be resurrected. Abu Ja`far said: We chose the statement that we chose about it because God, may He be glorified and exalted, informed us that whatever sustenance the animals are provided with is from Him, so it is more appropriate to follow that He knows their resting place and their resting place, rather than the statement about His knowledge of what the loins and wombs contain. What he means by his saying: All is in a clear book, is the number of each creature, the amount of its provisions, the amount of its resting place, and the duration of its stay in its storehouse. All of that is in a book with God, established and written, clear, making clear to whoever reads it that it is established and written before He created it and brought it into existence. This is a message from God, the Most High, to those who were turning their hearts away to belittle Him, that He knew things for them and recorded them in a book with Him before He created them and brought them into existence. God Almighty says to them: If someone knew that about them before He created them, how could He be unaware of what their souls conceal when they turn their chests to Him and cover themselves with their garments?
11:7: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: God, to whom you will return, O people, all together, He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days. He says: Is He who created that from nothing unable to bring you back to life after He has caused you to die? It was said: God Almighty created the heavens and the earth and what is in them in six days, so in this place it was sufficient to mention the creation of the heavens and the earth, instead of mentioning the creation of what is in them. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ismail bin Umayya informed me, on the authority of Ayoub bin Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi’, the freed slave of Umm Salamah, “on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took my hand and said: God created the soil on Saturday, and created the mountains in it on Sunday, and created the trees in it on Monday, and created the detestable on Tuesday, and created the light on Wednesday, and spread in it every kind of creature on Thursday, and created Adam after the afternoon of Friday at the end of creation, in the last hours of Friday, between the afternoon and the night.” Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: in six days, he said: He began the creation of the earth in two days, and measured its sustenance in two days. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ka’b, who said: God began the creation of the heavens and the earth on Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, and finished them on Friday. Then He created Adam in the last hour of Friday. He said: Then He made a thousand years in place of each day. And it was narrated on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Sharik, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, he said: Of the days of the Hereafter, each day is equivalent to a thousand years. He began creation on Sunday, and concluded creation on Friday, so it was called Friday, and Saturday was Saturday, so He created nothing. And his saying: And His Throne was over the water, means: And His Throne was over the water before He created the heavens and the earth and what is in them, as: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding God’s statement: And His Throne was over the water, before He created anything. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And His Throne was over the water. Your Lord, blessed and exalted be He, informs you of how the beginning of His creation was before He created the heavens and the earth. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And His Throne was over the water, he said: This is the beginning of His creation before He created the heavens and the earth. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ya`la ibn Ata`, on the authority of Wakee` ibn Hadas, on the authority of his uncle Abu Razeen al-`Uqayli, he said: I said: O Messenger of God, where was our Lord before He created the heavens and the earth? He said: In the clouds, above which was air, and below which was air, then He created His Throne upon the water. Khallad bin Aslam narrated to us, he said: An-Nadr bin Shumayl narrated to us, he said: Al-Mas’udi narrated to us, he said: Jami’ bin Shaddad narrated to us, on the authority of Safwan bin Mahraz, on the authority of Ibn Husayn, who was one of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “Some people came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they entered upon him. He began to give them good report and they said: ‘Give us,’ until that upset the Messenger of God, then they left him. Other people came and entered upon him and they said: ‘We have come to greet the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to learn about the religion and to ask him about the beginning of this matter.’ He said: ‘Then accept the good report, since those who left did not accept it.’ They said: ‘We accept it.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God was and there was nothing else besides Him, and His Throne was over the water, and He wrote in the Remembrance before all things, then He created seven heavens.’ Then someone came and said: ‘Your she-camel has gone.’ So she left, and the mirage was cut off before her. I wish I had left her. Muhammad ibn Mansur narrated, Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated, Amr ibn Abi Qays narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abi Layla, on the authority of Al-Munhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “And His Throne was over the water,” he said: The Throne of God was over the water, then He created for Himself a garden, then He created another beneath it, then He covered them with a single pearl. He said: And beneath them are two gardens. He said: And they are the ones so no soul knows - or he said: And they are the ones that no soul knows - what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do, he said: And they are the ones that the creation does not know what is in it - or: what is in them - and every day a gift comes to them from it - or from them. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: Ibn Abbas was asked about the statement of God: And His Throne was over the water, he said: On what was the water? He said: On the back of the wind. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, he said: Ibn Abbas was asked about his statement: And His Throne was over the water, on what was the water? He said: On the back of the wind. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. He said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Mubashar Al-Halabi told us, on the authority of Artah bin Al-Mundhir, he said: I heard Damrah say: God’s throne was over the water, and He created the heavens and the earth in truth, and He created the pen and wrote with it what He created and what would be of His creation, then that book glorified and praised God for a thousand years before He created anything of creation. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, he said, Abdul Samad bin Maqal told me, he said: I heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: The Throne existed before God created the heavens and the earth, then He took a handful of pure water, then He opened the handful and it rose as smoke, then He completed them as seven heavens in two days. Then He took clay from the water and placed it in the place of the House, then He spread out the earth from it, then He created sustenance in two days, and the heavens in two days, and He created the earth in two days, then He finished the last of the creation on the seventh day. And His statement: To test you, which of you is best in deed, the Most High says: And He is the One who created the heavens and the earth, O people, and He created you in six days, To test you, meaning: To test you, which of you is best in deed, meaning: Which of you is best in obedience to Him, as: He told us on the authority of Dawud bin Al-Muhabbir, who said: Abd Al-Wahid bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Kulayb bin Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he recited this verse: ‘To test you as to which of you is best in deed.’ He said: Which of you has the best intellect, is most pious in avoiding God’s prohibitions, and is quickest to obey God!” Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: To test you as to which of you is best in deed, meaning the two heavy burdens. And His statement: And if you were to say, ‘You will be resurrected after death,’ those who disbelieve would surely say, ‘This is not but obvious magic,’ God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And if you were to say to these polytheists among your people, You will be resurrected alive after your death, and I recited to them My revelation and revelation, those who disbelieve would surely say, ‘This is not but obvious magic,’ meaning: What you are reciting to us of what you are saying is nothing but obvious magic, clear to its listener about its true nature as magic. This is according to the interpretation of the one who reads it: This is nothing but obvious magic. As for the one who reads: This is nothing but an obvious magician, then the report about them is directed to the fact that they described the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as being, in what he brought to them, an obvious magician. Abu Jaafar said: We have already explained the correct reading of this in similar texts, previously, so there is no need to repeat it here.
11:8: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And if We delay the punishment for these polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, then We do not hasten it for them, and We extend their terms, for a limited term, a limited time, and known years. The origin of the word ummah is what we have explained previously in this book of ours, that it is a group of people who come together on a doctrine and religion, then it is used in many meanings that go back to the meaning of the origin that I mentioned. And the only thing that is said about the numbered years and the time, in this place and similar to it, is: ummah, because in it the nation is formed. The meaning of the words is: If We delay the punishment from them until the coming of a nation and the extinction of another nation before it. And in a manner similar to what we said, that the meaning of the nation, in this context, is the term and the time, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us - and al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told me, he said, Sufyan al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And if We delay the punishment from them for a limited term, he said: for a limited term. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razeen, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: To a limited nation, he said: a limited term. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said: For a specified term. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: To a limited nation, he said: For a time. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And if We delay the punishment from them for a limited time, he says: We withhold the punishment from them, for a limited time, Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: for a time. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And if We delay the punishment from them for a limited term, he says: for a known term. And His statement: He will surely say, ‘What is holding him back?’ He says: He will surely say, these polytheists, What is holding him back? What is it that prevents him from hastening the punishment with which he threatens us? As a denial from them of it, and as they think that this only delays the lie that was threatened from them, as: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, his statement: He will say, ‘What is holding him back?’ He said: To deny it, or that it is nothing. And His statement: Behold, the Day when it comes to them, it will not be averted from them, the Most High says, fulfilling His threat and correcting His report: Behold, the Day when it comes to them, the torment that they deny, will not be averted from them, meaning that no one will avert it from them, nor will anyone repel it from them, but it will come upon them and destroy them, and that which they used to ridicule will overtake them, meaning: And that which they used to ridicule of the torment of God will descend upon them and befall them. And their mockery of it that God mentioned was their saying before it descended: What is holding it back, and why don’t you bring it to us? Some of the interpreters said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And that which they used to ridicule overtook them, he said: What their prophets brought of the truth.
11:9: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And if We let a man taste from Us ease and abundance in provision and living, and We spread out for him from the world - which is the mercy that God Almighty mentioned in this place - then We take it away from him, meaning: Then We take it away from him, and calamities befall him that make him miserable and take him away, indeed, he is despairing and ungrateful, meaning: He remains hopeless of God’s mercy, hopeless of goodness. His saying: He despairs, is a noun derived from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so despaired of such-and-such, so he is he despairs, if that is a description of him. His saying: ungrateful, means: He is ungrateful to those who bestowed blessings upon him, and he is not thankful to his Lord who has bestowed blessings upon him for what He has bestowed upon him of His blessings. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And if We let a man taste mercy from Us and then take it away from him, indeed, he is despairing and ungrateful. He said: O son of Adam, if you have a blessing from God of abundance, security and well-being, then you are ungrateful for it. But if it is taken away from you, seeking your strength and your mind, then you despair of God’s mercy, despairing of His mercy. That is how the hypocrite and the disbeliever are.
11:10: God Almighty said: And if We let him taste a blessing after hardship had befallen him, he will surely say, ‘The bad times have gone away from me.’ Indeed, he is exultant and boastful.
11:11: Abu Ja`far said: The Almighty says: And if We make things easy for man in his worldly life, and provide him with ease in his life, and expand his provision for him, and these are the blessings of which God Almighty said: And if We let him taste [some] blessings, and His saying: after a hardship has befallen him, means: after a hardship he was in, and a difficulty he was dealing with, he will surely say, ‘The evils have departed from me,’ the Almighty says: He will say at that time: The hardship and difficulty have departed from me, and the difficulties and misfortunes have gone away, He is indeed joyful and boastful, the Almighty says: Man is joyful with the blessings he is given, delighted by them, proud, means: and he abandons seeking the bliss that remains, and the joy that lasts and does not go away. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his saying: The evil deeds have gone away from me, is a deception of God and an audacity towards Him, He is indeed joyful, and God does not love those who are joyful, proud, after what he has been given, and he does not thank God. Then He, the Most High, made an exception from the human being whom He described with these two attributes: Those who are patient and do righteous deeds. It is only permissible to exclude them from Him because the human being has the meaning of a species and a meaning of a group, and it is like His saying: By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds. So He, the Most High, said: Except for those who are patient and do righteous deeds. For if hardship and difficulty befall them in this world, that does not deter them from obeying God, but they are patient for His command and decree. If they attain ease and plenty in it, they thank Him and fulfill His rights with what He has given them from it. God says: For those is forgiveness, which He forgives them, and He does not disgrace them for it in their afterlife, and a great reward, meaning: And for them from God, along with the forgiveness of their sins, is a reward for the righteous deeds that they did in this world, a great reward and a tremendous recompense. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Except for those who are patient in the face of affliction, and do righteous deeds in the face of blessing, for them is forgiveness for their sins, and a great reward he said: Paradise.
11:12: Abu Ja'far said: The Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Perhaps, O Muhammad, you are abandoning some of what your Lord has revealed to you to convey from your command to convey it, and your heart is constrained by what is revealed to you, so you do not convey it to them, for fear that they will say: Why was not a treasure sent down to him or an angel come with him?, to him believing that he is a Messenger of God! The Almighty says: So convey to them what I have revealed to you, for you are only a warner warning them of My punishment, and warning them of My wrath for their disbelief in Me. The verses that they ask of you are with Me and under My authority. I will send them down if You wish. You are not required to do anything but convey the warning. And God is the Guardian over all things, meaning: God is the Guardian of all things, and in His hand is its management, so carry out what I have commanded you to do, and do not let their asking you for verses prevent you from conveying My revelation to them and carrying out My command. In the same way that we said about that, some of the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: God said to His Prophet: Perhaps you are abandoning some of what is revealed to you, so that you may do what you have been commanded to do, and call to it as you were sent. They said: Why was a treasure not sent down to him? We do not see any money with him! Where is the money? Or an angel came with him to warn with him! You are only a warner, so convey what you have been commanded.
11:13: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: This Qur’an is sufficient proof for you of the truth of what you have brought them, and evidence of the truth of your prophethood, from all other verses, since verses are only for those who are given them as evidence of their truthfulness, because all creation is incapable of producing anything like it. And this Qur’an, all creation is incapable of producing anything like it, so if they say you have fabricated it, that is, you have invented it and denied it. And it is indicated that the meaning of the statement is what we mentioned, His statement: Or do they say, ‘He invented it’ to the end of the verse. And what the Most High means by His statement: Or do they say, ‘He invented it’ is: Do they say, ‘He invented it’? We have shown the reason for the Arabs inserting umm in such a situation. So tell them to bring ten surahs like this Qur’an, fabricated, meaning: fabricated and different, if what I have brought you from this Qur’an is fabricated, and not a miraculous sign like the rest of the signs that you asked me about, like the treasure that you said, Why was it not sent down to him? or the angel about whom you said, Why did not a warner come with him to confirm him? For you are my people, and you are from the people of my language, and I am a man from among you, and it is impossible for me to be able to create by myself one hundred and fourteen surahs, and you cannot all be able to fabricate and invent ten secrets like them, especially if you seek help in that from whomever you wish from among the creation. God, the Most High, says: Say to them: And call upon whomever you are able to call upon besides God - meaning other than God - to fabricate and invent that from the gods. If you are not able to fabricate ten chapters like it, then it has become clear to you that you are lying in your saying: He fabricated it, and the truth of what I have brought to you that it is from God has become clear to you. But you may choose the signs from your Lord, and there has come to you from the proof that what you are denying is from God, like the proof that you ask for, and you desire that you believe in its coming. His saying: If you are truthful, is because he said: Then bring ten surahs like it, but it is: Say: Then bring ten surahs like it that are fabricated, if you are truthful that this Qur’an was fabricated by Muhammad, and call upon whomever you can besides God to do so, from among the gods and rivals. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Or do they say, ‘He has fabricated it,’ they have said it. Say, ‘Then bring ten fabricated surahs like it,’ and call your witnesses. He said: They testify that it is like it. This is what Al-Qasim said in his hadith.
11:14: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet, Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: If those whom you call upon besides God do not respond to you until they produce ten fabricated surahs like this Qur’an, and you and they are not able to produce that, then know and be certain that it was only sent down from the heaven to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the knowledge and permission of God, and that Muhammad did not fabricate it, nor is he able to fabricate it, and that there is no god but Him, meaning: And be certain also that there is no deity worthy of divinity over creation except God, to whom belongs creation and command, so renounce rivals and gods, and devote worship to Him alone. It has been said that his statement, If they do not respond to you, is an address from God to His Prophet, as if He said: If these infidels do not respond to you, O Muhammad, then know, O polytheists, that it was revealed with the knowledge of God. This is an interpretation far from the concept. And his saying: Are you Muslims? means: Are you obedient to God and sincere in your worship of Him, after the proof has been established against you? Mujahid used to say: What he meant by this statement were the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: So are you Muslims? He said: To the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: And Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And that there is no god but He, so are you Muslims? He said to the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. It was said: If they do not respond to you, and the address at the beginning of the speech was to one person, and that is his saying: Say, ‘Come,’ and he did not say: If they do not respond to you, in the manner that we have explained before in addressing the leader of the people and the one in charge of their affairs, that the Arabs sometimes address him as a group address, since his address was an address to his followers and soldiers, and sometimes as an address to one person, since he was one in himself.
11:15: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Whoever desires through his work the life of this world, and seeks it and its adornments, We will fully pay them the wages of their deeds therein and their recompense, and they will therein, meaning: while they are in this world, will not be deprived, meaning: their reward will not be diminished, but they will be fully paid therein. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments, the verse, which is what God gives them of this world in return for their good deeds, and that is because they will not be wronged, even as much as a speck on a date seed. He says: Whoever does righteous deeds seeking this world, fasting, praying, or praying at night, and does not do them except seeking this world, God says: I will give him what he sought in this world of reward, and his deeds which he did seeking this world will be in vain, and he will be among the losers in the Hereafter. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments - We fully repay them for their deeds therein. He said: The reward for the good they did in this world will be given to them in this world, and in the Hereafter they will have nothing but the Fire, and what they did therein will be in vain. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments - We fully repay them for their deeds therein, he said: The weight of what they did of good they were given in this world, and in the Hereafter they will have nothing but the Fire, and what they did therein will be in vain. He said: It is like the verse in al-Rum 30:And whatever you give in interest that it may increase within the wealth of people - it does not increase with God. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments, he said: Whoever works for the world, and has in it in the world. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, he said: Whoever does an action that God has commanded, such as prayer or charity, not seeking thereby the face of God, God will give him in this world the reward for that like what he spent, so that is His statement: We will fully repay them for their deeds therein, in this world, and therein they will not be deprived, the reward for what they did therein, Those are the ones who will have nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire, and what they did therein will be worthless, the verse. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Isa - meaning Ibn Maymun - on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments, he said: from someone from whom it is not accepted, he will be rewarded for it, he will be given its reward. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Isa Al-Jarashi, on the authority of Mujahid: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments, We fully repay them for their deeds therein, he said: From those from whom it is not accepted, it is hastened for them in this world. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments - We fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived, meaning: they will not be wronged. He says: Whoever’s concern and obsession, his desire and his intention is the world, God will reward him for his good deeds in this world, then he will go to the Hereafter, and he will not have a good deed for which he will be given a reward. As for the believer, he will be rewarded for his good deeds in this world, and he will be recompensed for them in the Hereafter, and they therein will not be deprived, meaning: in the Hereafter they will not be wronged. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, and al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, all on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments - We fully repay them for their deeds therein, the verse. He said: Whoever desires only the world, seeking it, God will give him wealth, and give him in it what he can live on, and that will be recompense for his deeds. And therein they will not be deprived, he said: They will not be wronged. He said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Laith bin Abi Salim, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does good to a doer of good, his reward is with God in this world and the hereafter. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj who said, I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about the words of God, Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments - We fully repay them for their deeds therein, the verse, he said: Whoever does a righteous deed without piety - meaning: from the people of polytheism - will be given a reward for that in this world: he will maintain ties of kinship, give to one who asks, show mercy to one in need, in similar acts of righteousness. God will hasten for him the reward for his work in this world, expand his livelihood and provision, and make his eyes content with what He has given him, and ward off from him the hardships of this world, in similar ways, but he will have no share in the Hereafter. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Hafs bin Omar Abu Omar Al-Dharee’ told us, he said, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, regarding his statement: We will fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived therein, he said: It refers to the Jews and Christians. He said, Hafs bin Omar told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’ al-Azdi, on the authority of al-Hasan: We will repay them for their deeds therein, he said: their good deeds. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, similarly. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, similarly. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Wahib: It reached him that Mujahid used to say about this verse: They are the people of hypocrisy, they are the people of hypocrisy. He said: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Haywah bin Shuraih, who said: Al-Walid bin Abi Al-Walid Abu Uthman told me: Uqbah bin Muslim told him: Shafi bin Mati’ Al-Asbahi told him: He entered Madinah and saw a man around whom the people had gathered, so he said: Who is this? They said: Abu Hurairah! So I approached him and sat in front of him, and he was talking to the people. When he was silent and alone, I said: I ask you by right and by right, when you told me a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I understood it and learned it. He said: Abu Hurairah said: I will do it, I will tell you a hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told me! Then he was distracted, then he came to and said: I will tell you a hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told me in this house, and there is no one in it except me and him! Then Abu Hurairah was overcome with a violent sigh, then he fell on his face, and he remained in a severe state for a long time, then he regained consciousness and said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) told me: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God, the Blessed and Exalted, will descend to the Resurrection to judge between them, and every nation will be kneeling. The first to be called will be a man who collected the Qur’an, a man who was killed in the way of God, and a man with great wealth. God will say to the reciter: Did I not teach you what I revealed to My Messenger? He will say: Yes, O Lord! He will say: What did you do with what you learned? He will say: I used to stand during the night and during the day! God will say to him: You lie! The angels will say to him: You lie! God will say to him: Rather, you wanted it to be said: So-and-so is a reciter, and that has been said! The owner of the wealth will be brought and God will say to him: Did I not provide for you so generously that I did not leave you in need of anyone? He will say: Yes, O Lord! He will say: What did you do with what I gave you? He will say: I used to maintain family ties and give charity. God will say to him: You lie! The angels will say to him: You lie! And God will say to him: Rather, you wanted it to be said: You were commanded to fight, so you fought until you were killed. God will say to him: You lied! And the angels will say to him: You lied! And God will say to him: Rather, you wanted it to be said: So-and-so is brave, and that has been said! Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, struck my knee and said: O Abu Hurairah, those three are the first of God’s creation to be set on fire by the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Walid Abu Uthman said: Uqba informed me that Shafi’ was the one who entered upon Mu’awiyah and informed him of this. Abu Uthman said: Al-Ala’ bin Abi Hakim told me that he was a guide for Muawiyah. He said: A man entered upon him and told him this on the authority of Abu Hurairah. Abu Hurairah said: He did this to these people, so what about those who remain among the people?! Then Muawiyah wept intensely until we thought he had perished, and we said: This man has brought us evil! Then Muawiyah came to, wiped his face and said: God and His Messenger spoke the truth: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments, We fully repay them for their deeds therein, and he recited until: And in vain is what they used to do. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Isa bin Maimun, on the authority of Mujahid: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments, the verse, he said: from those from whom it is not accepted, he fasts and prays, seeking thereby the world, and to ward off the worries of the Hereafter, and therein they will not be deprived, they will not be diminished.
11:16: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: These are the ones whom I mentioned, I will give them the reward for their deeds in this world. They will have nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire, which they will enter, and what they did therein will be in vain, meaning: what they did in this world will be gone, and what they used to do will be in vain, because they were working for other than God, so God made it null and void the reward of the one who did it. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Is he who has a clear proof from his Lord? He has made his religion clear to him, so he understands it, and a witness from Him recites it. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said: What he means by his saying: Is he who has clear evidence from his Lord? is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Khalaf told me, he said, Husayn ibn Muhammad told us, he said, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, he said: I said to my father: O my father, are you the one who recites in: And a witness from Him follows him? He said: No, by God, my son, I wish that I was him, but it is his tongue. Yaqub and Ibn Wakee’ told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And a witness from Him recites it, he said: His tongue. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And a witness from Him follows him, he said: His tongue. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Al-Hakam bin Abdullah Abu Al-Nu’man Al-Ajli told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. Ali bin Al-Hassan Al-Azdi told me, he said, Al-Mu’afa bin Imran told us, on the authority of Qura bin Khalid, on the authority of Al-Hassan, similarly. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Is he who has a clear proof from his Lord? - and he is Muhammad - he has a clear proof from his Lord. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And a witness from Him follows him, he said: His tongue. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And a witness from Him recites it, he said: His tongue is the witness. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ghundar told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. Others said: What he means by his saying: And a witness from Him follows him is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Sulayman al-Alaaf, on the authority of al-Hasan bin Ali, regarding his statement: And a witness from Him follows him, he said: The witness is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ghundar told us, on the authority of Awf, he said, Sulayman Al-Alaaf told me, he said: It reached me that Al-Hasan bin Ali said: And a witness from Him follows him, he said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said, Abu Osama told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Sulayman al-Alaaf, who heard al-Hasan ibn Ali: And a witness from Him follows him, saying: Muhammad, he is the witness from God. Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: Is he who has a clear proof from his Lord and a witness from Him recites it? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a clear proof from his Lord, and the Qur’an was also recited by a witness from God, that he is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: Is he who has a clear proof from his Lord? He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Nadr ibn Arabi, on the authority of Ikrimah, the same. He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Al-Harith told us, he said, Abu Khalid told us, I heard Sufyan say: Is he who has a clear proof from his Lord? He said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Others said: He is Ali bin Abi Talib. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me, Raziq bin Marzouq told us, Sabah Al-Farra told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abdullah bin Naji, who said, Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: There is no man from Quraysh about whom this or that verse was not revealed. A man said to him: What was revealed about you? Ali said: Do you not read the verse that was revealed about Hud 11:And a witness from Him follows him. Others said: It is Gabriel. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And a witness from Him follows him, that he used to say: Gabriel. Abu Kuraib and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan Ibn Ubaid God, on the authority of Ibrahim: And a witness from Him recites it, he said: Gabriel. Abu Kuraib told us about it again, with his chain of transmission on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: He said: They say: Ali, but it is Gabriel. Abu Kuraib and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: He is Gabriel, he recited the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur’an, and he is the witness from God. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us - and Muhammad ibn Abd God al-Mukhrami told us, he said, Ja`far ibn `Awn told us, he said, Sufyan told us, and al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, and al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Na`im told us, he said, Sufyan told us - on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: And a witness from Him recites it, he said: Gabriel. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. He said, Sahl bin Yusuf told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. He said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Gabriel. He said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Saleh: And a witness from Him recites it, he said: Gabriel. He said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: And a witness from Him recites it, he said: Gabriel. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak, saying regarding His statement: Is he who has a clear proof from his Lord, meaning Muhammad, who has a clear proof from God, and a witness from Him recites to him, Gabriel, a witness from God, recites to Muhammad what he was sent with. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, he said: He is Gabriel. He said, my father told us, on the authority of Nadr bin Arabi, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: He is Gabriel. He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Gabriel. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement: Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord, meaning Muhammad, on a clear proof from his Lord, and a witness from Him recites it, he is Gabriel, a witness from God regarding what he recites from the Book of God that was revealed to Muhammad. He said: And it is said: and a witness from Him recites it, meaning: the angel who is with him preserves it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Al-Nu’man A’rim told us, he said, Hammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Ayoub, he said, Mujahid used to say regarding His statement: Is he who has a clear proof from his Lord, he said: meaning Muhammad, and a witness from Him recites it, he said: Gabriel. Others said: He is a king who protects him. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And a witness from Him recites it, he said: With him is a guardian from God, an angel. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun and Suwaid bin Amr told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Mujahid: And a witness from Him recites it, he said: An angel who memorizes it. He said, Muhammad bin Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of someone who heard Mujahid: And a witness from Him recites it, he said: The angel. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And a witness from Him follows him, he is followed by a guardian from God, an angel. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Mujahid: And a witness from Him recites it, he said: The angel preserves it: They recite it as it should be recited, he said: They follow it as it should be followed. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And a witness from Him recites it, he said: A guardian from God, an angel. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these statements that we have mentioned in interpreting His statement: And a witness from Him recites it, is the statement of the one who said: It is Gabriel, because His statement: And before him was the Book of Moses as a guide and a mercy, indicates the correctness of that. That is because the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not recite the Book of Moses before the Qur’an, so that is evidence for the correctness of the statement of the one who said: It meant the tongue of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, or: Muhammad himself, or Ali, according to the statement of the one who said: It meant Ali. And it is not known that anyone recited that before the Qur’an or brought it, from those who the people of interpretation mentioned that he meant by His statement: And a witness from Him recites it, other than Gabriel, peace be upon him.
