If someone says: If that is your evidence that what is meant by it is Gabriel, then the reading of His statement, And before it was the book of Moses, must be in the accusative case, because the meaning of the statement, according to what you have interpreted, must be: And a witness from God recites the Qur’an, and before the Qur’an was the book of Moses? It was said: The reading in the countries has agreed to read it in the nominative case, so no one disagreed with it. If the reading had come in the accusative case, it would have been a correct reading and a correct meaning. If he said: Then what is the reason for their raising the book, according to what you claimed of interpretation? It was said: The reason for their raising this is that they began the report about the coming of the book of Moses before our book revealed to Muhammad, so they raised it, with from and from it, and the reading is like that, and the meaning that I mentioned of the meaning of Gabriel’s recitation of that before the Qur’an, and that what is meant by its meaning is that, even though the report is resumed as I described, sufficing with the indication of the speech to its meaning. As for his saying: an Imam, it is in the accusative case as a break from the Book of Moses, and his saying: and a mercy, is in apposition to the Imam, as if it was said: And before it was the Book of Moses as an Imam for the Children of Israel to follow, and a mercy from God that he recited to Moses as: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement: And before it was the Book of Moses, he said: Before it came the Book to Moses. There is an omission in the speech, and it was left out because what was mentioned about it was sufficient, which is: Is he who is upon clear evidence from his Lord and recites it a witness from Him, and before him the Scripture of Moses as an imam and a mercy, like one who is in misguidance, wavering, not guided to the right path, does not know truth from falsehood, and does not seek by his work anything but the life of this world and its adornment. This is similar to His statement: “Or is he who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord? Say, Are those who know equal to those who do not know?” The evidence for the truth of what we have said about this is that it follows His statement: He who desires the life of this world, the verse, then it was said: Is this better, he who is upon clear evidence from his Lord? The Arabs often do this if what is mentioned indicates what they mean by what was omitted, such as the saying of the poet: I swear that if anything came to us from his messenger other than you, we would not have found a defense for you. And his saying: Those believe in it, he says: These are the ones I mentioned, they believe in it and acknowledge it, even though these polytheists who say: Muhammad invented it disbelieve in it.
11:17: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And whoever disbelieves in this Qur’an, and denies that it is from God, of the parties, and they are the parties of their religions, the Fire is his promised destination, that he will go to it in the Hereafter because of his denial of it. God says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So be not in doubt about it, meaning: So be not in doubt about it, that whoever disbelieves in the Qur’an from the parties will be promised the Fire, and that this Qur’an that We have sent down to you is from God. Then He, may His praise be glorified, began the story about the Qur’an and said: This Qur’an that We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, is the truth from your Lord, there is no doubt about it, but most people do not believe that it is so. If someone says: Was the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in doubt that the Qur’an was from God and that it was true, so much so that it was said to him: So do not be in doubt about it? It was said: This is similar to his saying: If you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, and we have explained that there. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, Ayoub told us: I was informed that Saeed bin Jubair said: I have not heard a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in its entirety, except that I found its confirmation in the Book of God Almighty, until he said: And no one from this nation, neither Jew nor Christian, hears of me and does not believe in what I have been sent with, except that he will enter the Fire. Saeed said: So I said: Where is this in the Book of God? Until I came upon this verse: “And before it was the Book of Moses as a guide and a mercy. Those believe in him. But whoever disbelieves in him from the parties - the Fire is his promised destination.” He said: From the people of all religions. Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Mukhrami and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Ja’far bin Awn told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: And whoever disbelieves in it from the parties, he said: from all religions. Yaqub and Ibn Wakee’ told me, they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ayoub told us, “On the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: I would not hear a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as it was, except that I would find its confirmation - or he said: its verification - in the Qur’an. Then it reached me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one from this nation, neither Jew nor Christian, hears of me and does not believe in what I was sent with, except that he will enter the Fire.” So I began to say: Where is its confirmation? Until I came to this: Then is he who is upon a clear proof from his Lord to His saying: Then the Fire is his promised destination. He said: So the parties, all the religions. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said, Ayoub told me, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no one from this nation who hears of me, neither Jew nor Christian, and does not believe in me, but he will enter the Fire. So I began to say: Where is its proof in the Book of God? He said: I rarely heard a hadith from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but I found proof for it in the Qur'an, until I found these verses, And whoever disbelieves in it from the parties - the Fire is his promised destination, all religions. He said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And whoever disbelieves in it from the parties, the Fire is his promised destination. He said, the disbelievers are parties, all of them disbelievers. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And among the parties are those who deny part of it, meaning they disbelieve in part of it, and they are the Jews and Christians. He said: It has reached us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: No one from this nation hears of me, neither Jew nor Christian, and then dies before believing in me, except that he will enter the Fire. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Yusuf bin Adi Al-Basri told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever hears about me from my nation, or a Jew or a Christian, and does not believe in me, will not enter Paradise.
11:18: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And which people will be more severely punished than he who fabricates a lie against God and then lies about Him? Those will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, ‘These are the ones who lied about their Lord.’ They will be presented before their Lord on the Day of Resurrection, and He will ask them about what they did in this world, as: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God? He said: The disbeliever and the hypocrite. Those will be presented before their Lord, and He will ask them about their deeds. And His statement: And the witnesses will say, meaning the angels and prophets who witnessed them and recorded for them what they were doing, and they are the plural of witness, like companions, which is the plural of companion, These are the ones who lied about their Lord, meaning: These witnesses will testify in the Hereafter against these slanderers against God in this world, and they will say: These are the ones who lied about their Lord in this world. God says: Unquestionably, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers, meaning: Unquestionably, the wrath of God is upon the transgressors who disbelieved in their Lord. And similar to what we said about his statement: And the witnesses say, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And the witnesses say, he said: the angels. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The angels. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the witnesses will say, and the witnesses are the angels, they testify about the deeds of the children of Adam. Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told me, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: The witnesses, he said: the creatures, or he said: the angels. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, something similar. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hasan told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, And the witnesses will say, those who record their deeds against them in this world, These are the ones who lied about their Lord, they recorded it and testified about it against them on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: The witnesses are the angels. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said: I asked Al-A’mash about his statement: And the witnesses say, he said: The angels. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Al-Faraj who said: I heard Abu Muadh who said: Ubaid bin Sulayman narrated to us who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And the witnesses will say, meaning the prophets and messengers, which is His statement: And the Day We will raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves, and We will bring you as a witness over these, he said: And His statement: And the witnesses will say, ‘These are the ones who lied about their Lord,’ they say: O our Lord, we brought them the truth and they lied, so we bear witness against them that they lied about You, O our Lord. Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday narrated to us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Qatada, “On the authority of Safwan ibn Muhriz al-Mazini, he said: While we were in the House with Abdullah ibn Umar, and he was performing the Tawaf, a man came to him and said: O Ibn Umar, what did you hear the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say about the secret conversation? He said: I heard the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The believer draws near to his Lord until He places His cloak over him and confesses his sins to him, and says: Do you know such and such? He says: O Lord, I know! Twice, until when he has reached what God willed for him to reach, He says: I concealed it from you in this world, and I forgive you for it today. He said: Then he is given his scroll of good deeds - or: his book - in his right hand. As for the disbelievers and hypocrites, they will be called out before all witnesses: “These are the ones who lied about their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers.” Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Safwan ibn Mahraz, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: We used to say that no one is disgraced when he is in front of God, and his disgrace is hidden from anyone whom God created - or: the creation.
11:19: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: May the curse of God be upon the oppressors who prevent people from believing in Him, and acknowledging His worship, and sincerely worshipping Him instead of the gods and rivals, from the polytheists of Quraysh, and they were the ones who tempted those who entered Islam from it, and seek to make it crooked, meaning: and they seek the path of God, which is the Islam to which Muhammad called people, meaning: deviation and inclination from the straight path, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter, meaning: and they are disbelievers in the resurrection after death, along with their preventing people from the path of God, and their seeking to make it crooked, disbelievers, meaning: they deny that and reject it.
11:20: Abu Ja'far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: Those were not able to escape on earth, are those whom He, the Most High, described as turning people away from the path of God. He, the Most High, says: They were not those who could escape their Lord by fleeing from Him on earth if He wanted to punish them and take revenge on them, but they are in His grip and dominion, they cannot escape from Him if He wants them, and they cannot escape Him if He seeks them. And they had no protectors besides God, meaning: And these polytheists had no supporters to aid them from God if He wanted to punish them besides God, and to stand between them and Him if He punished them, and they had in this world a means of protection by which they could protect themselves from those among the people who wanted to harm them. And His statement: The punishment will be doubled for them, the Most High says: Their punishment will be increased, so He made for them two in place of one. His saying: They could not hear, nor could they see, there is a difference of opinion regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: This is how God described these polytheists, that He has sealed their hearing and their sight, and that they do not hear the truth, nor do they see God’s proofs, with beneficial hearing, nor guided sight. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: They were not able to hear, nor did they see, deaf to the truth, so they did not hear it, dumb, so they did not speak it, blind, so they did not see it, nor did they benefit from it. Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: They were not able to hear, nor were they able to see. He said: They were not able to hear good and benefit from it, nor see good and take it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God Almighty informed us that He stood between the people of polytheism and their obedience to Him in this world and the Hereafter. As for this world, He said: They were not able to hear, which is His obedience, nor were they able to see. As for the Hereafter, He said: They were not able * humbled. Others said: What he meant by his statement: And they had no protectors besides God, are the gods who hinder people from the path of God. They said: The meaning of the statement is: Those and their gods, they were not able to defeat God on earth, the punishment would be doubled for them, they were not able to hear, nor could they see, meaning the gods, that they had neither hearing nor sight. This is a statement narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas from a source that I disliked mentioning due to the weakness of its chain of transmission. Abu Ja`far said: The meaning of this is that the punishment will be doubled for them because they were able to hear but did not hear, and because they saw but did not contemplate God’s proofs with their eyes and take heed from them. They said: The preposition ba should have been inserted, because He said: And for them is a painful punishment because they used to lie, because of their lie, in more than one place in the revelation where the preposition ba was inserted, and its omission is permissible in speech, like saying in speech: I will surely reward you for what you did, and for what you did. This is a statement made by some of the Arabists. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement regarding this, according to us, is what Ibn Abbas and Qatada said, that God Almighty described them as being unable to hear the truth with beneficial hearing, nor to see it with guided sight, because they were too busy with the disbelief in which they were established to use their limbs in obedience to God, even though they had hearing and sight.
11:21: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: These people who have this description are the ones who have cheated themselves of their share of God’s mercy, and what they used to invent has gone astray from them, and their lies, slander, and falsehood against God have been invalidated by their claiming that He has partners. So those who were gods besides God took a path other than theirs, and took a path other than theirs, and went astray from them, because it led them to Hell, and their gods became nothingness, nothing, because they were stones, wood, or copper in this world, or God had a friend who led him to Paradise. This is also not their path, and this is also a deviation from them.
11:22: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Indeed, these people who have this description in this world and in the Hereafter are the greatest losers, who have sold their homes in Paradise for the homes of the people of Paradise in Hell, and that is the clear loss. We have already explained that the meaning of their saying: You have committed a sin is you have earned the sin and you have committed it. The Arabs used it frequently in places of oaths and in places of there is no escape, like their saying: It is certain that you are going, meaning there is no escape, until they used it in places of confirmation, so they said: It is certain that you will stand, meaning it is certain that you will stand. So the meaning of the statement is: There is no prevention from them, and no turning away from them.
11:23: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: Those who believed in God and His Messenger, and worked in this world in obedience to God, and humbled themselves before their Lord. The interpreters differed about the meaning of humility. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: And they turned to their Lord. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds and humbled themselves before their Lord, he said: Humility is turning back. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: His statement: And they humbled themselves before their Lord, he said: And they turned to their Lord. Others said: The meaning of this is: And they feared. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And they humbled themselves before their Lord, he said: They feared. Others said: It means: Be reassured. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And they humbled themselves before their Lord, he said: They were reassured. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Others said: The meaning of this is: they were humble. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And they humbled themselves before their Lord, humility, reverence and modesty. Abu Jaafar said: These sayings are close in meaning, even if their wording differs, because turning to God comes from fear of God, and from humility and submission to God through obedience, and reassurance with Him comes from submission to Him. However, the very essence of submission, among the Arabs, is humility and submission. He said, To their Lord, meaning: And they humbled themselves before their Lord. This is because the Arabs often place the letter lam in place of ila and ila in place of the letter lam, as God Almighty said: That your Lord inspired her, meaning: inspired her. It may be possible that it was said thus, because they were described as having deliberately humbled themselves before God. And His statement: Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally, means: Those who have this description are the inhabitants of Paradise who will not leave it, nor will they die in it, but will remain in it forever.
11:24: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: The example of the two groups of disbelief and faith is like the example of the blind man who sees nothing with his eye, and the deaf man who hears nothing. Likewise, the group of disbelief does not see the truth and follow it and act upon it, because it is preoccupied with its disbelief in God, and the overwhelming defeat of God upon it. It does not hear God's caller to guidance, so it responds to him and is guided by it, so it persists in its misguidance, wavering in its confusion. As for the All-Hearing and All-Seeing, that is the group of faith. It saw God's proofs and acknowledged what they indicated of the Oneness of God, and innocence from deities and rivals, and the prophethood of the prophets, peace be upon them. It heard God's caller and responded to him, and acted in obedience to God, as: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said: The example of the two groups is like that of the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing. He said: The blind and the deaf are the disbelievers, and the seeing and the hearing are the believers. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: The parable of the two groups is like that of the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing. The two groups are the disbelievers and the believers. As for the blind and the deaf, they are the disbelievers, and as for the seeing and the hearing, they are the believers. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: The parable of the two parties is like that of the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing, the verse. This is a parable that God has given for the disbeliever and the believer. As for the disbeliever, he is deaf to the truth and does not hear it, and blind to it and does not see it. As for the believer, he hears the truth and benefits from it, and sees it and comprehends it, memorizes it, and acts upon it. God Almighty says: Are they equal in comparison? He says: Are these two groups equal in their different states in themselves before you, O people? They are not equal before you, just as the state of the disbeliever and the believer are not equal before God. Do you not remember? He, the Most High, says: Do you not consider, O people, and reflect, and learn the truth of the difference between their two states, so that you may be deterred from what you are upon of misguidance and guidance, and from disbelief and faith? The blind and the deaf, the seeing and the hearing, are four in wording, but two in meaning. Therefore it was said: Are they equal in example? It was said: Like the blind and the deaf, meaning: like the blind and the deaf. It was also said: and the seeing and the hearing, meaning: the seeing and the hearing, like the saying of the speaker: the elegant and the intelligent, and he is describing one person with that.
11:25: God Almighty says: And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, [saying], ‘Indeed, I am to you a clear warner.’
11:26: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: We sent Noah to his al-Nas 114:I am to you, O people, a warner from God, warning you of His punishment for your disbelief in Him, so believe in him and obey his command. What he means by his saying: clear is that he explains to you what he was sent with of God’s commands and prohibitions. The readings of his saying: I differed. The majority of the Kufan reciters and some of the Medinans read it with a kasra on the letter in as a beginning, since it was in the sending, meaning: the saying. Some of the people of Medina, Kufa, and Basra read it with the fat-ha on the an, based on the use of the sending in it, as if the meaning of the speech according to them was: We sent Noah to his people, saying, I am a clear warner to you. Abu Jaafar said: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two readings that agree in meaning. A group of people have read each of them, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct in that. And his saying: That you worship none but God, whoever breaks the alif in his saying: I, makes his saying: We sent, an agent for the that in his saying: That you worship none but God, and the meaning then becomes: And We sent Noah to his people that you worship none but God, and say to them: I am to you a clear warner. And whoever opens it, returns the that in his saying: That you worship none, to it. So the meaning then becomes: We sent Noah to his people that I am to you a clear warner, that you worship none but God. His saying: That you worship none but God, O people, means worshipping gods and idols, and associating them with Him in His worship. And single out God in monotheism, and devote worship to Him, for He has no partner in His creation. And His saying: Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful Day, means: O people, if you do not single out God for worship, and single Him out for monotheism, and abandon all rivals and idols besides Him, then I fear for you from God the punishment of a painful Day, the punishment and torment of whomever is tormented on it. And He made the painful a description of the day, which is a description of the torment, since the torment was in it, as it was said: And He made the night a place of rest, and rest is a description of what is rested in, not the night.
11:27: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: The great ones of Noah’s people and their nobles - who are the elites - who disbelieved in God and denied the prophethood of their prophet Noah, peace be upon him, said, We do not see you, O Noah, except as a human being like us, meaning by that: that he is a human being like them in creation, form, and kind, as if they were denying that God would send a messenger from among humans to His creation. And his saying: And we do not see you followed except by those who are our lowest in appearance, means: And we do not see you followed except by those who are our lowest among the people, not the great and noble, as we see and what appears to us. His saying: The first opinion, the reading of it differed. The majority of the readers of Medina and Iraq read it as Badī al-Ra’y without the hamza of al-Bādī and with the hamza of al-Ra’y, meaning: apparent opinion, from their saying: the thing appeared, if it appeared, as the rajaz poet said: My uncle has become like me, my body is like my body, and my tongue and hand are like the stallion Badi Badi, without a hamza, and another said: The height of my body has risen above me Some people of Basra read it as: badī’ al-ra’y, also with a hamza, meaning: the initiator of opinion, from their saying: I started with this matter, if you started with it before something else. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in our view, is the reading of the one who reads: Badī al-ra’ī, without the hamza of al-badī, and with the hamza of al-ra’ī, because the meaning of that statement is: except for those who are our lowest, in apparent opinion, and in what appears to us. And His statement: And we do not see that you have any superiority over us, means: And we do not see that you have any superiority over us that you attain by opposing us in worshipping idols, to worshipping God and sincerely devoting your servitude to Him, so we follow you seeking that superiority and seeking what you have attained by opposing us, but we think you are liars. This is a speech from them to Noah, peace be upon him, because they only denied Noah and not his followers, because his followers were not messengers. The speech, which is one, was presented in the same way as the speech of all, as it was said: (O Prophet, when you divorce women). Abu Jaafar said: The interpretation of the statement is: Rather, we think that you, O Noah, in your claim that God sent you to us as a messenger, are lying. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of his saying: at the beginning of the opinion, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And we do not see that you are followed except by those who are the lowest of us in appearance, he said: according to what appeared to us.
11:28: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says, informing about what Noah said to his people when they denied him and rejected the advice he brought them from God: O my people, have you considered, if I am on clear evidence from my Lord, on knowledge, understanding, and clarification from God to me of what is required of me for Him, and what is required of me in terms of sincere worship of Him and abandoning associating idols with Him in it, and He has given me mercy from Him, meaning: and He has granted me success, prophethood, and wisdom from Him, so I believed in Him and obeyed Him in what He commanded me and forbade me, then it has become blind to you. There are different readings of this. The people of Medina and some of the people of Basra and Kufa read it as: Fa’amit, with the ‘ayn open and the mim softened, meaning: The mercy was blinded to you, so you were not guided to it, so you acknowledged it and gave your Messenger charity on it. The majority of the Kufi reciters read it as: Fa’maitu alaykum, with a damma on the ‘ayn and a shaddah on the meem, considering it to be Abdullah’s recitation, as it is mentioned in Abdullah’s recitation: Fa’maitu alaykum. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who read it: So it was made blind to you, with a damma on the `ayn and a shaddah on the meem, because of what they mentioned as a reason for the one who read it with it, and because of its proximity to His statement: Have you considered, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Himself, so He attributed mercy to God, so likewise his blinding others to Him, with the addition to Him, is more appropriate. This word is one of the words that the Arabs have changed the verb from its place. This is because man is the one who is blind to seeing the truth, since he is blind to seeing it. The truth is not described as blind except in the usage that has been used in speech. It is permissible for the Arabs to use it, similar to their saying: The ring entered my hand, and the shoe entered my foot. It is known that the foot is what enters the shoe, and the finger into the ring, but they used it in this way because what was intended by it was known. And his saying: Shall we force it upon you while you are averse to it? He says: Shall we force you to enter Islam, while God has blinded you to it? While you are averse to it? He says: And you are averse to our forcing it upon you. Hate it. He says: We will not do that, but we will entrust your affair to God, so that He may be the one who decides regarding your affair as He sees and wills. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Noah said: O my people, have you considered if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, he said: I have known it, and I have known through it His command, and that there is no god but Him, and He has given me mercy from Himself, Islam, guidance, faith, wisdom, and prophethood. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Have you considered, if I am on clear evidence from my Lord, the verse, but by God, if the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been able to do so, he would have made his people do it, but he was not able to do so and did not possess it. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, he said: In my father’s reading: Shall we force it upon you from among ourselves while you are averse to it? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, he said, Amr bin Dinar told us, he said, Ibn Abbas read, We will force you to do it from within ourselves, Abdullah said: From within ourselves, from our own volition. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, on the authority of Abi bin Kaab: We force you to do it with half of our hearts while you are averse to it.
11:29: Abu Ja`far said: This is also report from God about what Noah said to his people, that he said to them: O my people, I do not ask you for any reward for my advice to you and my calling you to the Oneness of God and the sincerity of worship to Him, so you accuse me of my advice and think that my action is seeking worldly gain. My reward is only from God, meaning: What is the reward for my advice to you and my calling you to what I call you to, except from God, for He is the One who will reward me and recompense me for it. And I will not drive away those who believe, and I will not drive away those who believe in God, and acknowledge His Oneness, and abandon the idols and disavow them, since they are not from your elite and nobles. Indeed, they will meet their Lord, meaning: These people whom you ask me to drive away will go to God, and God will ask them about what they did in this world, not about their honor and lineage. Noah was told this to his people, because his people said to him, as: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: “And I will not drive away those who have believed. Indeed, they will meet their Lord.” He said: They said to him: O Noah, if you wish for us to follow you, then drive them away, otherwise we will not be satisfied for us and them to be equal in this matter. So he said: “I will not drive away those who have believed. Indeed, they will meet their Lord.” So He will ask them about their deeds. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, and Muhammad Ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, all on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: My reward is only from God, he said: My recompense. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. And his saying: But I see you are a people who are ignorant, means: But I, O people, see you are a people who are ignorant of what is due to you from the right of God, and what is required of you from His obligations. And therefore, out of your ignorance, you asked me to expel those who believed in God.
11:30: Abu Jaafar said: He says: O people, who will support me and protect me from God, if He punishes me for expelling the believers who believe in God’s Oneness, if I expel them? Do you not remember? He says: Do you not think about what you are saying, so that you know its error, and then stop it?
11:31: Abu Jaafar said: His saying: And I do not say to you that I have the treasures of God, is connected to his saying: And O my people, I do not ask you for any wealth for it. The meaning of the words: O my people, I do not ask you for any money for it, “nor do I tell you that I have the treasures of God,” which nothing can exhaust, so I call you to follow me in them. Nor do I know the unseen - meaning: what is hidden from the secrets of the servants, for no one knows that except God - so I claim divinity and call you to worship me. Nor do I say: I am an angel sent to you, so that I would be lying in my claim. Rather, I am a human being like you, as you say. I was commanded to call you to God, and I have conveyed to you what I was sent with. And I do not say to those whom your eyes despise, ‘God will never give them any good.’ He says: Nor do I say to those who followed me and believed in God and made Him One, whom your eyes despise, and you said: They are the ones who despise you, “God will never give them any good,” and that is belief in God. God knows best what is in their souls, He says: God knows best what is in their hearts, and the belief of their hearts, and He is their guardian in that. I only have from them what is apparent and evident, and they have shown belief in God and followed me, so I do not expel them nor do I consider that permissible. Indeed, then I would be among the wrongdoers, He says: If I said to those who showed belief in God and my belief, God will never give them any good, and I judged their inner selves contrary to what I revealed, would I speak to them without my knowledge of what is in their souls, and would I expel them? By doing so, I am doing what they should not do, transgressing against what God has commanded them to do, and that is injustice. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: And I do not say to you that I have the treasures of God, which nothing will exhaust, so I am only calling you to follow me in them, so that I may give you from them, and I do not say: I am an angel who came down from the heavens with a message, I am not a human being like you, and I do not know the unseen, and I do not say: Follow me in knowledge of the unseen.
11:32: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: The people of Noah said to Noah, peace be upon him: You have argued with us and have increased your argument with us, so bring us what you threaten us with of punishment, if you are truthful in your hostility and your claim that you are a Messenger of God. He meant by that that he would not be able to do any of that. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: He argued with us, he said: We argued. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim narrated, he said, Al-Husayn narrated, he said, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Mujahid said: They said, ‘O Noah, you have disputed with us,’ he said: You have argued with us, ‘and you have prolonged your dispute with us, so bring us what you threaten us with,’ Ibn Jurayj said: Denying the punishment, and that it is false.
11:33: God Almighty said: “He said: Only God will bring it to you if He wills, and you will not cause failure.”
11:34: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Noah said to his people, when they hastened the punishment from him: O my people, the punishment that you hasten is not from Me, but rather it is from God and not from anyone else. He is the One who will bring it to you if He wills. And you will not escape it, meaning: And if He wants to punish you, you will not escape it, meaning: You will not escape it by escaping from it, because wherever you are in His kingdom, authority, and power, His rule over you is in effect. And my advice will not benefit you, meaning: And my warning of His punishment and the descent of His power upon you for your disbelief in Him will not benefit you. If I wanted to advise you, in my warning you of that, because my advice will not benefit you, because you will not accept it. If God wants to mislead you, meaning: If God wants to destroy you with His punishment, He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned, meaning: And to Him you will be returned after Destruction. It was narrated that Tayyi’ tribe used to say: So-and-so has become ill, meaning he has gone astray. It was narrated from others, as they heard it, that they said: I led someone astray, meaning: I destroyed him. And the young camel went astray, meaning it lost its milk and died. He mentioned that God’s saying: Then they will meet with destruction, means destruction.
11:35: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: Do these polytheists from your people say, O Muhammad, did Muhammad fabricate this Qur'an? And this story about Noah? Say to them: If I fabricated it, made it up and invented it, upon me is my crime, meaning: Upon me is my sin in my fabrication of what I fabricated about my Lord, not you. You will not be held accountable for my sin or my crime, and I will not be held accountable for your sin. And I am innocent of what you commit, meaning: And I am innocent of what you sin and commit sin against your Lord, of your fabrications against Him. It is said: I committed a crime, and I committed a crime, as the poet said: An outcast from my clan and a hostage of sin for what my hands have committed and my tongue has wrought
11:36: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And God revealed to Noah, when the word came true for his people, and God's command overshadowed them: That, O Noah, none of your people will believe in God, declare Him One, and follow you in what you call them to, except those who have already believed, so they believed in that and followed you, so do not be sad, meaning: do not be humble or grieve, for what they used to do, for I will destroy them, and save you from them and those who followed you. And God revealed that to him, after Noah had called for their destruction, saying: My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dwelling. It is derived from the verb to be miserable. It is said: So-and-so was miserable about the matter. What Labid bin Rabi'ah said: In a funeral like sheep, they are saddened by what we have suffered. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Do not be sad, he said: Do not be sad. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So do not be sad about what they used to do, meaning: Do not be sad. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed, and that was when he called upon them, saying: My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single inhabitant, his statement: So do not be sad, meaning: do not despair, and do not be sad. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: None of your people will believe except those who have already believed, then he invoked against his people, when God made clear to him that none of his people will believe except those who have already believed.
11:37: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And it was revealed to him that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed, and that build the ark, which is the ship, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, and he is the ship. And his saying: With our eyes means: With the eye of God and His revelation as He commands you, as: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And construct the ark under Our eyes and with Our inspiration, that he did not know how to construct the ark, so God inspired him to construct it on the likeness of a bird’s beak. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And Our revelation, he said: as we command you. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: With Our eyes and by Our revelation, as We command you. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And construct the ark under Our eyes and by Our revelation, he said: under the eye of God. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: And by Our revelation, he said: as We command you. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: By Our eyes and by Our revelation, he said: By the eye of God and His revelation. And His statement: “And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged themselves. Indeed, they will be drowned.” God Almighty says: And do not ask Me to pardon those of your people who have wronged themselves, and have brought about their transgression against themselves through their disbelief in God, destruction by drowning. Indeed, they will be drowned by the flood, as: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, And do not address me, he said, he says, and do not reply to me. He said: It was mentioned that they would not intercede with Him.
11:38: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And Noah builds the ship, and whenever a group of the leaders of his people pass by him, they mock him, meaning: They mocked Noah, and said to him: Have you become a carpenter after the prophecy, and are building the ship on land? Noah says to them: If you mock us, if you mock us today, then we will mock you in the Hereafter, just as you mock us in this world, then you will know, if you witness God’s punishment, who among us was the one who wronged himself. Noah's ship was made as follows: Al-Muthanna and Salih ibn Mismar told me, they said: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said: Musa ibn Yaqub told us, he said: Fa’id, the client of Ubayd God ibn Ali ibn Abi Rafi’, told me, that Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Rabi’ah told him, that Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If God had mercy on anyone from the people of Noah, He would have had mercy on the mother of the boy! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Noah remained among his people for a thousand years minus fifty years, calling them to God, until the end of his time. He planted a tree, and it grew large and went in all directions. Then he cut it down. Then he began to build a ship. They would pass by and ask him, and he would say: ‘Make it a ship!’ They would mock him and say: ‘Make a ship on land! How will it sail?’ He would say: ‘You will soon know.’ When he finished, and the oven overflowed and the water in the alleys became abundant, the boy’s mother feared for him, and she loved him very much. So she went out to the mountain until she reached a third of it. When the water reached her, she went out until she reached two-thirds of the mountain. When the water reached her, she went out until she was standing on the mountain. When the water reached her neck, she lifted him up in her hands until the water carried her away. If God had mercy on any of them, He would have had mercy on the boy’s mother.” Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: It was mentioned to us that the length of the ship is three hundred cubits, its width is fifty cubits, its height in the sky is thirty cubits, and its door is in its width. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The length of Noah’s ship was one thousand cubits, and its width was six hundred cubits. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Hussein narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Mufadhal bin Fadalah, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid bin Jud’an, on the authority of Yusuf bin Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The disciples said to Jesus, son of Maryam 19:If you would send us a man who witnessed the ark, then tell us about it! So he set off with them until he reached a mound of dirt. He took a handful of that dirt in his hand and said: Do you know what this is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: This is Ka’b Ham bin Noah. He struck the mound with his staff and said: Get up, by God’s permission. Then he was standing, shaking the dirt off his head, and he had turned gray. Jesus said to him: Is this how you perished? He said: No, but I died when I was young. However, I thought that it was the Hour, and that is how I turned gray. He said: Tell us about Noah’s ark! He said: Its length was one thousand and two hundred cubits, and its width was six hundred cubits, and it had three layers: one layer had animals and wild beasts, one layer had humans, and one layer had birds. When the animals’ dung became abundant, God inspired Noah to poke the elephant’s tail, so he poke it and a male and female pig fell out of it, and they headed towards the dung. When the mouse fell into the ship’s hull to gnaw at it, God inspired Noah to strike between the eyes of the lion, and a male and female cat came out of its nostrils, and they headed towards the mouse. Jesus said to him: How did Noah know that the land had been flooded? He said: He sent the crow to bring him the report, and it found a carcass and landed on it, so he cursed it with fear, and that is why it does not like houses. He said: Then he sent the dove, and it brought olive leaves in its beak and mud with its feet, so he knew that the land had been flooded. He said: So he put the greenery around its neck around it, and prayed that it would be at ease and safe, and that is why it would like to like houses. He said: So we said, O Messenger of God, shall we not take him to our family so that he may sit with us and talk to us? He said: How can one who has no provision follow you? He said: So he said to him, Return, by God’s permission! He said: So he returned to dust. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair al-Laythi: that he used to narrate that it had reached him that they used to beat him - meaning the people of Noah - and strangle him until he fainted. Then when he regained consciousness, he would say, O God, forgive my people, for they do not know. Then, when they persisted in their sin, and their sin became great on earth, and their affair became excessive towards him and towards them, and their affliction became severe upon him, and he would wait for the next generation, and no generation would come except that it was more evil than the generation before it, until the last of them would say, This one was with our fathers and grandfathers, like this madman! They did not accept anything from him, until Noah complained about their situation to God Almighty, as God told us in His Book: My Lord, indeed I called upon my people night and day, * But my call only increased them in flight, to the end of the story, until he said: (My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single inhabitant. Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not give birth except to wicked disbelievers), to the end of the story. When Noah complained about that to God and sought His help against them, God revealed to him: And construct the ark under Our eyes and with Our inspiration, and do not speak to Me concerning those who have wronged, meaning: after today, for they are to be drowned. So Noah began to work on the ark, and was distracted from his people. He began to cut wood, strike iron, and prepare the equipment for the ark from tar and other things that only he could repair. His people would pass by him while he was doing that work, and they would mock him and ridicule him. He would say: “If you ridicule us, then we will ridicule you as you ridicule. And you will soon know who will be afflicted with a punishment that will disgrace him and upon whom will be inflicted a lasting punishment.” He said: And they would say, as I have heard, O Noah, you have become a carpenter after becoming a prophet! He said: And God made the wombs of women barren, so that no children would be born to them. He said: The people of the Torah claim that God commanded him to build the ark from teak wood, to make it slate, to coat it with pitch inside and out, to make it eighty cubits long, to make it three levels, a bottom, a middle, and a top, and to make windows in it. So Noah did as God commanded him, until he finished it, and God had enjoined upon him: “When Our command comes and the oven overflows, We will say, ‘Load into it two mates of every kind and your family, except those against whom the word has preceded and those who believe.’ But none believed with him except a few.” And He made the oven a sign between him and Him, so He said: When Our command comes and the oven overflows, then take into it two mates of every kind, and embark. When the oven boiled, Noah carried in the ark those whom God had commanded, and they were few, as God had said. He carried in it two of every kind, of what had life and trees, male and female. He carried in it his three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their wives, and six people who had not believed in him, so they were ten men: Noah, his sons, and their wives. Then he brought in what he had been commanded to do of the animals, and his son Yam stayed behind, and he was a disbeliever. Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Hasan Ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ali Ibn Zayd, on the authority of Yusuf Ibn Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I heard him say: The first of the animals that Noah carried in the ark was the ant, and the last of what he carried was the donkey. When the donkey put its head in and its chest in, Satan clung to its tail, and its legs would not move. Noah kept saying: Woe to you! Enter! But he got up but could not, until Noah said: Woe to you! Enter! Even if Satan is with you! He said: A word that slipped from his tongue. When Noah said it, Satan let him go, so he entered and Satan entered with him. Noah said to him: What brought you in to me, O enemy of God? He said: Didn’t you say: Enter, even if Satan is with you? He said: Get out of me, O enemy of God! He said: You have no choice but to carry me! It was, as they claim, on the back of the ark. When Noah was reassured in the ark and brought into it those who believed in him, it was in the month of... of the year in which Noah entered, after six hundred years of his life, seventeen nights had passed of the month. When he entered and carried with him a load, the springs of the Great Gout stirred and the gates of heaven were opened, as He said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: (So We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water. And We caused springs to gush forth from the earth, and the waters met for a decree already decreed.) So Noah and those with him entered the ark, and it covered it and those with him with its layer. So between God sending the water and the water carrying the ark, there were forty days and forty nights, then the water carried, as the people of the Torah claim, and the water increased and became intense and rose. God says to Muhammad: And We carried him on planks and nails, and nails are iron nails - so the ark made it sail with him and those with him, with waves like mountains. And Noah called to his son who had perished among those who perished, and he was isolated, when Noah saw the truth of his Lord’s promise, he said: O my son, embark with us and be not with the disbelievers, and he was wretched and had concealed disbelief. He said: I will seek refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water, and the mountains were a protection from rain when it came, so he thought that it was as he had known. Noah said: “There is no protector this day from the command of God except for him on whom He has mercy. And the waves came between them, and he was among the drowned.” The water increased until it overflowed and rose above the mountains, as the people of the Torah claim, by fifteen cubits. Everything on the face of the earth was destroyed, including everything that had a soul or trees. Nothing remained of the creation except Noah and those with him in the ark, and except Uj bin Anq, as the people of the Book claim. So between God sending the flood and the water receding, there were six months and ten nights. Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Hasan Ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ali Ibn Zayd Ibn Jud’an - Ibn Humayd said, Salamah said, and Ali Ibn Zayd told me, on the authority of Yusuf Ibn Mihran, he said: I heard him say: When the excrement of people bothered Noah in the ark, he was ordered to wipe the tail of the elephant, so he wiped it, and two pigs came out of it, and that was enough for him. And the mice reproduced in the ark, and when they bothered him, he was ordered to order the lion to sneeze, so he sneezed, and two pigs came out of his nostrils, eating at the mice. Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Yusuf ibn Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When Noah was on the ship, a mouse gnawed at the ropes of the ship, so Noah complained, and God inspired him, so he stroked the tail of the lion, and two cats came out. There was excrement on the ship, so he complained about that to his Lord, so God inspired him, so he stroked the tail of the elephant, and two pigs came out. Ibrahim bin Yaqoub Al-Jawzjani told us, he said, Al-Aswad bin Aamer told us, he said, Sufyan bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Yusuf bin Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said: Sulayman Al-Qurashi said: Noah built the ark in four hundred years, and the teak tree grew in forty years, until its length was four hundred cubits, and the cubit reached the shoulder.
11:39: God Almighty says: Whoever is afflicted with a punishment that disgraces him and upon whom a lasting punishment descends.
11:40: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says, informing about what was said to his al-Nas 114:Then you will know, O people, when God’s command comes, who is the one who will perish, who will be afflicted with a punishment that will disgrace him, meaning: the one to whom God’s punishment comes from us and from you, humiliating and degrading him, and upon whom will befall a lasting punishment, meaning: and in the Hereafter, along with that, there will befall him a permanent punishment that will not cease, lasting upon him forever. And his saying: Until when Our command comes, he says: And Noah builds the ark, Until when Our command comes, which We promised him would save his people from the flood that would drown them. And his saying: And the oven overflowed. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that: Some of them said: Its meaning is: the water gushed forth from the surface of the earth, and the oven overflowed, which is the surface of the earth. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us, Al-Awam bin Hawshab told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said about it: And the oven overflowed, he said: The oven is the surface of the earth. He said: It was said to him: If you see water on the surface of the earth, then ride, you and those with you. He said: The Arabs call the surface of the earth the oven of the earth. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Awam, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, something similar. Abu Kuraib and Abu al-Sa’ib told us, they said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: Al-Shaibani told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: And the oven overflowed, he said: The face of the earth. Others said: It is the illumination of the morning, from their saying: The light of the morning is illumination. Who said that? Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Muhammad bin Fadil told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abbas, the freed slave of Abu Juhaifa, on the authority of Abu Juhaifa, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement: Until when Our command comes and the oven overflows, he said: It is the lighting of the morning. Ibn Wakee’ and Ishaq ibn Israel told us: Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ziyad, the freed slave of Abu Juhaifa, on the authority of Abu Juhaifa, on the authority of Ali, regarding his statement: And the oven overflowed, he said: The lighting of the morning. Hammad bin Ya’qub told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Ishaq, on the authority of the client of Abu Juhayfah - I think he named him - on the authority of Abu Juhayfah, on the authority of Ali: And the oven overflowed, he said: the lighting of the morning. Ishaq bin Shaheen told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of a man from Quraysh, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him: And the oven overflowed, he said: The dawn broke. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of a man whom he named, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding his statement: And the oven overflows, he said: When dawn comes. Others said: The meaning of this is: The highest part of the earth and the most honorable place in it is filled with water. He said: The oven is the most honorable place on earth. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Until when Our command came and the oven overflowed, we used to say that it was the highest and most honorable place on earth and it was a sign between Noah and his Lord. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Sulayman told us, Abu Hilal told us, I heard Qatada say: And the oven overflowed, he said: The highest and most elevated part of the earth, the water overflowed from it. Others said: It is the oven in which bread is baked. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Until when Our command comes and the oven overflows, he said: If you see water coming out of your family’s oven, then it is the destruction of your people. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Muhammad, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: It was an oven made of stones, it belonged to Eve until it was given to Noah. He said: It was said to him: If you see water bubbling from the oven, then you and your companions should get in. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Shibl, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And the oven overflowed, he said: When the water gushed forth, and Noah was commanded to board the ark with those with him. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And the oven overflowed, he said: Water gushed out of it, as a sign, that he would embark with his family and those with him on the ship. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar, except that he said: A sign is that his family and those with him board the ship. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, in a similar manner, except that he said: A sign is that he rides with his family and those with them in the ship. Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Qasim told us, he said, Khalaf bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Water sprang up in the oven, and his wife knew about it and informed him. He said: That was in the vicinity of Kufa. He said, Al-Qasim told us, Ali bin Thabit told us, on the authority of Al-Sari bin Ismail, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: He used to swear by God, the oven did not boil except from the direction of Kufa. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abdul Hamid Al-Hammani told us, on the authority of Al-Nadr Abu Omar Al-Khazzaz, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And the oven overflowed, he said: The oven overflowed in India. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And the oven overflowed, and it was a sign for Noah, when water came out of it, then destruction and drowning came to the people. Ibn Abbas used to say about the meaning of: Far, spring. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And the oven overflowed, he said: It sprang forth. Abu Jaafar said: The boiling of water is the surah that pushed it. It is said: The water boiled quickly, and it boiled quickly, and it boiled quickly, and it boiled quickly, and it is said when its flow moved. Abu Ja`far said: The most appropriate of these sayings in our view to interpret his statement, the oven, is the saying of those who said: It is the oven in which bread is baked, because that is what is known from the speech of the Arabs. And the speech of God is not directed except to the most common and well-known of its meanings among the Arabs, unless there is evidence for something in it that is contrary to that, in which case it is accepted. That is because He, may His praise be glorified, only addressed them with what He addressed them with, in order for them to understand the meaning of what He addressed them with. We said, to Noah when Our punishment came upon his people, which We had promised Noah that We would punish them with, and the oven whose boiling water We had made a sign of the coming of Our punishment between Us and him, for the destruction of his people, Load therein, meaning in the ark, of every kind two, meaning of every male and female, as: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Of every pair, two, he said: a male and a female, from every type. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his saying: of every pair two, so one is a pair, and the two pairs are a male and a female from every type. He said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: of every pair two, he said: a male and a female from every species. He said, Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: We said, ‘Carry on it two of each kind,’ meaning: two of each kind. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Of every pair, two, meaning by two pairs, two, a male and a female. Some of the scholars of Arabic language from Kufa said that the word zawn in Arabic means two. He said: It is said: He has two sandals if he has two sandals, but it is not said: He has two sandals. Likewise: He has two pigeons and He has two chains. He said: “Do you not hear His saying: And that He created the two mates, the male and the female, for they are two. Some of the Basrans who are experts in Arabic said about his statement: “We said, ‘Load on it two of each kind,’” he said: So he made the two kinds, the males and females. He said: Yunus claimed that the poet’s statement: You are a man who takes every opportunity by surprise, sometimes making mistakes and sometimes hitting the mark. He meant the wolf. He said: This is more unusual than that. Another of them said: The pair is the color. He said: And every type is called a color, and he cited the verse of Al-A’sha in that regard: And every pair of brocade worn by Abu Qudamah is loved by both of them. And Labid says: And the joy of his voice is like the bridles, and his adornment is pairs of light, a drink It was mentioned that Al-Hassan said regarding his statement: And of everything We created pairs: The sky is a pair, the earth is a pair, winter is a pair, summer is a pair, night is a pair, and day is a pair, until the matter is referred to God, the One, who is not like anything. And his saying: And your family, except for those against whom the word has already been decreed, meaning: And carry your family also in the ship, meaning by family, his children, his women, and his wives, except for those against whom the word has already been decreed, meaning: except for those about whom I said: I will destroy them with those of your people whom I will destroy. Then they differed about who God excluded from his family. Some of them said: He is one of Noah's wives. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said: And your family, except for he against whom the word has already passed, he said: The torment, she is his wife, she was among those who passed away in torment. Others said: Rather, it is his son who drowned. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: And your family, except for he against whom the word has already passed, he said: His son, drowned among those who drowned. And His saying: And whoever believed, meaning: And take with them whoever believed in you and followed you from your people. God says: And none believed with him except a few, meaning: And none from his people acknowledged the oneness of God with Noah except a few. They differed about the number of those who were with him, so he carried them with him in the ark. Some of them said about that: They were eight people. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “And your family, except for those against whom the word has already passed, and those who believed. And none believed with him except a few,” he said: It was mentioned to us that no one was left on the ship except Noah, his wife, his three sons, and their wives, so all of them were eight. Ibn Wakee’ and Al-Hasan Ibn Arafa told us, they said, Yahya Ibn Abdul Malik Ibn Abi Ghania told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Hakam: And none believed with him except a few, he said: Noah, his three sons, and his four daughters-in-law. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said: I was told that Noah took with him his three sons, and three wives for his sons, and Noah’s wife, so they were eight with their wives. The names of his sons were: Japheth, Shem, and Ham. Ham had intercourse with his wife in the ship, so Noah asked that his sperm be changed, and he came with a black man. Others said: Rather, they were seven souls. Who said that? Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash: And none believed with him except a few, he said: They were seven: Noah, his three daughters-in-law, and his three sons. Others said: They were ten, in addition to their wives. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: When the oven boiled, Noah carried in the ark those whom God had commanded him to carry, and they were few as God had said. So he carried his three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their wives, and six people who had believed, so they were ten people, with Noah, his sons, and their wives. Others said: Rather, they were eighty people. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: Noah carried eighty people with him on the ship. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us: Some of them used to say: They were eighty, meaning the few about whom God said: And none believed with him except a few. Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me, he said, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, he said, Hussain bin Waqid Al-Khurasani told me, he said, Abu Nahik told me, he said, I heard Ibn Abbas say: There were eighty men on Noah’s ship, one of them was Jurhum. Abu Ja`far said: The correct thing to say about that is to say as God said: And none believed with him except a few, describing them as being few, and He did not specify their number by any amount, nor is there any authentic report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So one should not exceed God’s limit in that, since there is no limit to the number in the Book of God, or a report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
11:41: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And Noah said: Embark on the ark, In the name of God is its running and its anchorage. There is an omission in the speech that has been dispensed with by the indication of what was mentioned in the report about it, which is His saying: “We said: ‘Load on it of every kind two mates and your family, except for those against whom the word has already passed and those who have believed.’ But none believed with him except a few.” So Noah carried them on it, and said to them, Embark on it. So the indication of His saying: “And said: Embark on it,” was dispensed with by the indication of His saying: “And said: Embark on it,” about his carrying them on it, so He left mentioning it. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: In the name of God is its course and its anchorage. The majority of the people of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it as: In the name of God, its course and its anchorage, with a damma on the m in both letters. If it is read in this way, it is from ajra and arsa, and there are two ways of parsing it: One of them is the nominative case, meaning: In the name of God, its course and its anchorage, so al-majra and al-marsa are in the nominative case with the b in His statement: In the name of God. The other: the accusative, meaning: In the name of God when it is carried out and anchored, or: at the time of its carrying out and anchoring, so his saying: In the name of God is a statement that is sufficient in itself, like the saying of the speaker when he begins to do something he is doing: In the name of God, then the course and the anchorage are accusative as the Arabs placed their saying: Praise be to God for your secret and your arrival, meaning the crescent, its beginning and its end, as if they said: Praise be to God for the beginning and end of the crescent. And it is also heard from them: Praise be to God for your arrival until your secret. The majority of the Kufic reciters read it as: In the name of God, its course and its anchorage, with the m of its course open and the m of its anchorage closed. They made its course a verbal noun from to run jarā, and its anchorage from to anchor arsā, yarsi, irsā.
