If it is read in this way, then the parsing of both of them is similar to what is in them, if they are read: its course and its anchorage, with the m closed in both of them, as I have explained. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Raja’ al-Attardi that he used to read it: In the name of God, its course and its anchorage, with a damma on the m in both of them, and he made them an attribute of God. If they are read in this way, there are also two ways of parsing in them, except that one of them is the accusative, and this is the most common of the two ways of parsing, because the meaning of the speech according to this reading is: In the name of God, the course and anchorage of the ark. So the course is an attribute of the name of God. It may also be possible for it to be accusative, and this is the second way, because it is appropriate to include the definite article in the course and the anchorage, like you say: In the name of God, the course and anchorage. If they are deleted, they are made accusative in the state, because they have the meaning of an indefinite noun, even if they are added to a definite noun. It was mentioned from some of the Kufians that he read it: its course and its anchorage, with the opening of the meem in both of them from the word jara and rasa, as if he directed it to mean: in the state of its course and the state of its anchorage, and he made both attributes for the ship, as Antara said: So I was patient, a free soul, anchored when the coward's soul arose. Abu Jaafar said: The reading that we choose in this regard is the reading of those who read: In the name of God, its course with a fat-ha on the m and its anchorage with a damma on the m, meaning: In the name of God when it runs and when it anchors. I chose the fat-ha on the meem of mujriha because of its proximity to His statement, And it runs with them in waves like mountains. He did not say, It runs with them. Whoever reads In the name of God, its course, the correct reading is to read, And it runs with them. Their consensus on reading, tajiri with the fat-ha on the ta' is clear evidence that the correct way to say, mujriha is to open the meem. We chose the damma on marsaha because of the consensus of the proof from the reciters on its damma. The meaning of His statement, mujriha is its journey, and marsaha is its stopping, from: God stopped it and anchored it. Mujahid used to read it with a damma on the meem in both letters. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid. He said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: In the name of God is its course and its anchorage. He said: When they ride, sail, and anchor. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: In the name of God when they mount, sail, and anchor. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: In the name of God is its course and its anchorage. He said: In the name of God when they sail and when they anchor. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said, Abu Rawq told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement: Embark therein, in the name of God is its course and its anchorage, he said: When it anchors, he says: In the name of God, and it anchors. And when he wants it to sail, he says: In the name of God, and it sails. And His saying: Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful, means: Indeed, my Lord covers the sins of those who repent and turn to Him, and He is too merciful to punish them after their repentance.
11:42: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty meant by His statement: And it sailed with them, the ark sailed with Noah and those with him in it, “in waves like mountains. And Noah called to his son,” Yam, and he was apart, from him, he did not ride the ark with him, O my son, embark with us, the ark, and be not with the disbelievers.
11:43: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: When Noah called him to board the ship with him, fearing that he would drown, Noah’s son said: I will seek refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water. He said: I will go to a mountain to take refuge from the water, so that it will prevent me from drowning. What he means by his saying: He protects me is that he prevents me, like the tether of a water skin, which is tied to its head, preventing water from flowing out of it. And his saying: There is no protector today from the command of God except for whom He has mercy, means: There is no one who can prevent the command of God that He has sent down upon creation from drowning and destruction, except for whom He has mercy upon us and saved us from it, for He is the One who protects and protects whomever He wills from His creation. So min is in the nominative case, because the meaning of the statement is: There is no protector who can protect today from God’s command except God. The Arab scholars differed about the position of min in this context. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is in the accusative case, because the infallible is different from the protected, and the deceased is infallible. He said: It is as if its accusative is like his saying: They have no knowledge thereof except the following of conjecture. He said: And whoever permits: following conjecture, and the nominative in his saying: A town with no companions except the camels and the wild donkeys He was not allowed to raise the word min because the one who said: except for the ya’afir made the ya’afir and the likes of them the companion of the wilderness. Likewise his saying: except for following conjecture, he says: He taught them conjecture. He said: And you are not allowed in any way to say: The infallible is the one who protects in a situation, but if you made the protector in the interpretation of the infallible, as if you said: There is no one protected today from the command of God, then raising min would be permissible. He said: And it is not denied that the object comes out on the subject, do you not see his saying: from gushing water, its meaning, and God knows best: gushing, and his saying: in a life of contentment, its meaning: pleasing. The poet said: Let the good deeds not depart for their purpose and sit, for you are the one who feeds and clothes. It means: clothed. Some Basra grammarians said: There is no protector today from the command of God except for whom He has mercy, on the basis of: but for whom He has mercy, and it is permissible for it to be on the basis of: there is no protection, meaning: protected, and except for whom He has mercy would be in the nominative case, instead of the protector. Abu Ja`far said: There is no basis for these statements that we have related from them, because the speech of God Almighty is directed to the most eloquent and famous of the speech of the one in whose tongue it was revealed, and there was no way to that. And nothing compelled us to make `Asim in the meaning of Ma`sumu, nor to make `Except in the meaning of Lakin, since we found for that in its meaning, which is its meaning, in the famous speech of the Arabs, a correct way out, which is what we said: that the meaning of that is: Noah said, There is no protector today from the command of God, except for he who has had mercy on us and saved us from His punishment, just as it is said: There is no savior today from the punishment of God except God, and there is no one to be fed today from the food of Zayd except Zayd. So this is the well-known speech and the understood meaning. And his saying: And a wave came between them, and he was among those who were drowned, means: A wave of water came between Noah and his son, and he drowned, and he was among those who were destroyed by drowning from the people of Noah, peace and blessings be upon him.
11:44: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: And God said to the earth, after His command to destroy the people of Noah by drowning them was completed: O earth, swallow your water, meaning: drink. From the saying: So-and-so swallowed such-and-such, or: he swallowed it, if he swallowed it. And O sky, withhold, meaning: withhold the rain, hold back, and the water subsided, meaning: the earth took it and dried it up, and the matter was accomplished, meaning: God’s command was accomplished, so it went with the destruction of Noah’s people, and it came to rest on al-Judi, meaning: the ark, came to rest, “on al-Judi,” which is a mountain, as mentioned, in the region of Mosul or al-Jazira, “and it was said: Away with the wrongdoing people,” meaning: God said: God distanced the wrongdoing people who disbelieved in God from the people of Noah. Abbad bin Yaqub al-Asadi told us, he said, al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Matar, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Abdul Ghafoor, on the authority of his father, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “On the first day of Rajab, Noah boarded the ship, and he and all those with him fasted, and the ship sailed with them for six months, until that ended in Muharram, and the ship anchored at al-Judi on the day of Ashura, and Noah fasted, and he ordered all those with him from the wild animals and beasts to fast in gratitude to God.” Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: The top of the ship was for the birds, the middle was for the people, and at the bottom was for the beasts. Its height in the sky was thirty cubits. It was launched from Ain Warda on Friday, ten nights before the end of Rajab, and it anchored on Mount Judi on the day of Ashura. It passed by the House and circled it seven times, and God raised it from drowning. Then it came to Yemen, then it returned. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Ja`far Al-Razi, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Noah descended from the ship on the tenth day of Muharram, and he said to those with him: Whoever among you is fasting today, let him complete his fast, and whoever is not fasting, let him fast. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Ma`shar, on the authority of Muhammad bin Qais, who said: At the time of Noah, there was not a hand span of land that did not have a person claiming it. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: It was mentioned to us that it - meaning the ark - set sail with them on the tenth of Rajab, and it was in the water for one hundred and fifty days, and it settled on Al-Judi for a month, and it landed with them on the tenth of Muharram, on the day of Ashura. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of his saying: And the water subsided and the matter was accomplished, and the ship came to rest on Al-Judi, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And the water subsided, he said: it decreased, and the matter was decided, he said: the destruction of the people of Noah. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. He said, Ibn Jurayj said: And the water subsided, meaning the earth dried it up. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: O sky, withhold, he said: hold back, and the water subsided, he said: the water disappeared. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, and the water subsided, and ghayyud is the disappearance of water, and it came to rest on al-Judi. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And it came to rest on al-Judi, he said: It is a mountain in the Arabian Peninsula, the mountains were raised high from drowning, and it humbled itself before God, so it did not drown, so it came to rest on it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And it came to rest on al-Judi, he said: al-Judi is a mountain in the Arabian Peninsula. The mountains rose high on that day from the drowning and became tall, but it humbled itself before God, so it did not drown, and Noah’s ship came to rest on it. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, he told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And it came to rest on al-Judi, meaning: on the mountain, and its name is al-Judi. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us: And it came to rest on Al-Judi, he said: A mountain in the island, the mountains were lofty, and it was humble when Noah’s ship wanted to rest on it. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And it came to rest on Al-Judi, God left it for us in the valley of the Arabian Peninsula as a lesson and a sign. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say: And it came to rest on Al-Judi, which is a mountain in Mosul. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: It was mentioned to us that Noah sent the raven to look at the water, and it found a corpse and landed on it, so he sent the dove and it brought him olive leaves, and it was given the necklace around its neck and the dye for its feet. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that when God wanted to stop that meaning the flood He sent a wind over the face of the earth, so the water calmed down, and the springs of the earth, the great abyss, and the gates of heaven were blocked. God the Most High says: And it was said, ‘O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain]’ to Away with the wrongdoing people, so the water began to decrease, diminish, and retreat. The ark settled on Mount Judi, as the people of the Torah claim, in the seventh month, seventeen nights had passed, on the first day of the tenth month, and the tops of the mountains were seen. Then, after forty days had passed, He opened the window of the ark in which He had made it, then He sent a raven to see what the water had done to him, but it did not return to him. So He sent a dove, and it returned to him, but he did not find a place for its feet, so he stretched out his hand to the dove and caught it. Then he stayed seven days, then he sent it to look for him, and it returned when evening came, and in its mouth were olive leaves, so Noah knew that the water had subsided from the face of the earth. Then he stayed seven days, then he sent it, but it did not return, so Noah knew that the earth had risen. When the year was completed between when God sent the flood and when Noah sent the dove, and one day of the first month of the year two had entered, the face of the earth rose, and dry land appeared, and Noah removed the covering of the ark and saw the face of the earth. In the second month of the year two, on twenty-seven nights of it, it was said to Nuh 71:(Descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from among those with you and nations We will grant enjoyment; then a painful punishment will touch them from Us.) It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: Some people claim that children who drowned were with their fathers. This is not the case. Children are like birds and all those whom God drowned without sin, but their appointed times came and they died at their appointed times. As for men and women who attain maturity, drowning was a punishment from God for them in this world, then their destiny is the Fire.
11:45: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And Noah called upon his Lord and said: My Lord, You promised me that You would save me and my family from drowning and destruction, and my son has perished, and my son is one of my family. And Your promise is true, which has no successor, and You are the most just of judges, with truth, so judge for me by fulfilling what You promised me, that You would save my family and return my son to me, as: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: And You are the most just of judges, he said: The most just of judges with truth.
11:46: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: God said: O Noah, the one whom you drowned and destroyed, the one whom you mentioned as being from your family, is not from your family. The interpreters differed about the meaning of his saying: He is not of your family. Some of them said: It means: He is not your son, he is someone else's. And they said: That was a sin. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: He is not of your family, he said: He was not his son. Abu Kuraib and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaafar: And Noah called to his son, he said: his wife’s son. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of his companions, Ibn Abi Arubah among them, on the authority of Al-Hasan: No, by God, he is not his son. He said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Ja`far: And Noah called to his son, he said: This is in the language of Tayy, he was not his son, he was the son of his wife. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Awf and Mansour, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: He is not of your family, he said: He was not his son, and he used to recite it: He is an act that is not righteous. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of Qatada, he said: I was with al-Hasan and he said: And Noah called to his son, By God, he is not his son! I said: O Abu Saeed, he says: And Noah called to his son! And you say: He is not his son! He said: What do you think of his statement: He is not of your family? I said: He is not of your family whom I promised you that I would save with you, and the People of the Book do not differ that he is his son. He said: The People of the Book lie. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: I heard Al-Hasan reciting this verse: “He is not of your family. Indeed, his work is not righteous.” Then he said: By God, he was not his son. Then he recited this verse: So they betrayed her. Saeed said: So I mentioned that to Qatada, and he said: He should not have sworn! Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: So do not ask about that of which you have no knowledge, he said: It became clear to Noah that he was not his son. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: So do not ask about that of which you have no knowledge, he said: God made it clear to Noah that he was not his son. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Jurayj said regarding his statement: And Noah called to his son, he said: He called to him while he thought that he was his son, and he was born on his bed. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Thawbar, on the authority of Abu Ja`far: He is not from your family. He said: If he were from his family, he would have been saved. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, he heard Ubaid bin Umair say: We see that what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, decreed regarding the child being for the bed, is because of the son of Noah. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: No, by God, he is not his son. Others said: The meaning of this is: He is not from your family whom I promised to save. Who said that? Abu Kuraib and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Aamer, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And Noah called to his son, he said: He is his son. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said, Abu Aamer told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said, Ibn Abbas said: He is his son, no prophet’s wife ever rebelled. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Amir al-Hamadani, on the authority of al-Dahhak bin Muzahim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: No wife of a prophet has ever been unjust. He said: And his saying: He is not of your family, is those whom I promised you that I would save with you. Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada and others, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: He is his son, except that he differed from him in action and intention. Ikrimah said in some of the letters: He did an evil deed, and betrayal is not done in a proper way. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Ikrimah used to say: He was his son, but he differed from him in intention and action, so it was said to him: He is not from your family. Al-Hasan told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Ath-Thawri and Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Aishah, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Qatah, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas being asked, while he was next to the Kaaba, about the statement of God, the Most High: And they both betrayed them. He said: It was not for adultery, but this one was telling people that he was crazy, and this one was pointing out the guests. Then he recited: Indeed, it was an unrighteous deed. Ibn Uyaynah said: Ammar al-Dahni told me that he asked Saeed ibn Jubayr about that, and he said: He was the son of Noah, for God does not lie! He said: And Noah called to his son, he said: Some of the scholars said: No prophet’s wife ever committed adultery. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ammar Al-Dahni, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: God said, and He is the Truthful: and He is His Son, And Noah called to his son. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Musa bin Abi Aisha, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: No prophet’s wife ever rebelled. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, Hisham told us: I asked Abu Bishr about his statement: He is not of your family. He said: He is not of your religion, and he is not among those I promised you that I would save. Yaqub said: Hisham said: Most of what Abu Bishr used to tell us was on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr. Ibn Wakee’ narrated that Muhammad ibn Ubayd narrated on the authority of Ya’qub ibn Qays, who said: A man came to Saeed ibn Jubayr and said: O Abu Abdullah, is the one whom God mentioned in His Book as the son of Noah his son? He said: Yes, by God, the Prophet of God ordered him to ride with him on the ship, but he disobeyed. So he said: I will seek refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water. He said: O Noah, he is not of your family; he has done something that is not righteous, because of the disobedience of the Prophet of God. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah al-Bajali, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr: That a man came to him and asked him, saying: Have you seen the son of Noah, his son? So he glorified God for a long time, then he said: There is no god but God. God tells Muhammad: Noah called his son and you say: He is not from him? But he differed from him in action, so he who does not believe is not from him. Yaqub and Ibn Wakee’ told me, they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Harun al-Ghanawi, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: And Noah called to his son, he said: I bear witness that he is his son. God said: And Noah called to his son. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah, they said: He is his son. Fadala bin Al-Fadl Al-Kufi told me, he said, Buzay’ said: A man asked Al-Dahhak about the son of Noah, so he said: Are you not amazed at this fool! He asks me about the son of Noah, and he is the son of Noah as God said: Noah said to his son! Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Ubayd told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, that he read: And Noah called to his son, and his saying: He is not of your family, he said: He is not of your family. He said: He is saying: He is not of those who are under your guardianship, nor of those whom I promised to save from your family, Indeed, his work was not righteous, he said: He said: His work was in polytheism. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: By God, he is his son. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: He is not of your family, he said: He is not of your religion, nor of those whom I promised you that I would save, and he was his son. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: He said, ‘O Noah, he is not of your family,’ meaning: He is not among those whom We promised salvation. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: He is not of your family, meaning: He is not of your people, nor of those whom I promised to save from your family. He is of unrighteous conduct, meaning: His conduct was in polytheism. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Khalid bin Hayyan told us, on the authority of Ja’far bin Burqan, on the authority of Maimun and Thabit bin Al-Hajjaj. They said: He is his son, born in his bed. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said: The interpretation of that is: He is not of your people whom I promised you that I would save, because he opposed your religion and disbelieved in me, and he was his son, because God, the Most High, mentioned it, informed His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he was his son, as He said: And Noah called to his son, and it is not permissible for him to inform that he was his son, so it would be contrary to what he informed. And in his statement: He is not of your people, there is no indication that he is not his son, since his statement: He is not of your people, could have the meaning we mentioned, and it could have been: He is not of your religion, then the religion is omitted and it is said: He is not of your people, as it was said: And ask the town in which we were. As for his saying: It is an unrighteous deed, the readings differed in its reading. So I read it as most of the countries read: It is an unrighteous deed, with the tanween of deed and the nominative case of unrighteous. Those who read it also differed in their interpretation. Some of them said: It means: Your asking me this is an improper act. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mugheerah, on the authority of Ibrahim: It is an unrighteous deed. He said: Your asking me this is an unrighteous deed. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: It is an unrighteous deed, meaning: bad, so do not ask about that of which you have no knowledge. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: It is an unrighteous deed, he said: Your question about something you have no knowledge of. Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Hamza Al-Zayyat, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: It is an unrighteous deed, he said: Your asking me is an unrighteous deed, So do not ask about that of which you have no knowledge. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: Those whom you mentioned as your son, and you asked me to save him, did not do good deeds, meaning: they are not of sound mind. They said: The ha’ in his statement he refers back to the son. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan that he read: an unrighteous deed, and he said: By God, he is not his son. It was narrated from a group of the Salaf that they read it: It is an unrighteous deed, as a report of a past tense verb, and other is in the accusative case. Among those who were narrated from him that he read it like this is Ibn Abbas. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Musa bin Abi Aisha, on the authority of Sulayman bin Qatah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he read: an unrighteous deed. They interpreted this as: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ghundar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is an unrighteous deed. He said: It was contrary to him in intention and deed. Abu Ja`far said: We do not know that any of the reciters of the regions read this reading, except some of the later ones. He based this on a report narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he read it like this, but its chain of transmission is not authentic. This is a hadith narrated from Shahr ibn Hawshab, and sometimes he says: from Umm Salamah, and sometimes he says: from Asma bint Yazid, and we do not know which bint Yazid he means? And we do not know of any authentic hearing from Shahr from Umm Salamah. Abu Ja`far said: The correct reading of this according to us is what the countries read, which is raising work with the tanween and raising ghair, meaning: Your asking of me what you are asking about your son, who opposes your religion, who is a follower of the polytheists with me, of salvation from destruction, and my answer to you has already passed in your supplication: Do not leave on the earth a single inhabitant of the disbelievers, what has already passed, without excluding any of them, is an invalid action, because it is a question from you to me not to do what I have previously said I would do, in my answer to your question to me to do it. So that is an invalid action. And His saying: So do not ask about that of which you have no knowledge, is a prohibition from God Almighty to His Prophet Noah from asking Him about the reasons for His actions, the knowledge of which He had concealed from him and from other human beings. God Almighty says to him: O Noah, I have informed you about your question about the reason for My destroying your son whom I destroyed, so do not ask after that about the reasons for My actions, the knowledge of which I have concealed from you, and of which you have no knowledge. I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant, in your asking Me about that. Ibn Zayd used to say in his statement: I advise you not to be among the ignorant what: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Indeed, I advise you lest you be among the ignorant, that your ignorance should reach the point where I do not fulfill a promise I made to you, until you ask me about something of which you have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers. The readings differed in the reading of his saying: So do not ask about that of which you have no knowledge. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it as: Do not ask about that of which you have no knowledge, with the nun pronounced with a kasra or with a light nun, and they tended to break it to indicate the ya which is a metaphor for the name of God in: Do not ask me. Some of the Meccans and some of the people of the Levant read it as: Do not ask, with a shaddah on the nun and a fathah on it, meaning: Do not ask, O Noah, about what you have no knowledge of. Abu Jaafar said: The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is to soften the nun and break it, because that is the eloquent speech of the Arabs used among them.
11:47: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says, informing His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Noah’s repentance to Him for his mistake, in his question that he asked his Lord about his son: He said, ‘My Lord, indeed I seek refuge in You,’ meaning: I seek refuge in You from asking You for something that I have no knowledge of, of which You have kept knowledge to Yourself and concealed from Your creation, so forgive me for my mistake in asking You for what I asked You about my son, and if You do not forgive me for it and have mercy on me and save me from Your wrath, I will be among the losers, meaning: among those who cheated themselves of their fortunes and were destroyed.
11:48: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: O Noah, descend from the ark to the earth, "in peace from Us", meaning: in safety from Us, you and those with you, from Our destruction, and blessings upon you, meaning: and blessings upon you, and upon nations from among those with you, meaning: and upon generations to come from your descendants and those with you from your offspring. So these believers are from the descendants of Noah, for whom happiness was previously granted by God, and He blessed them before He created them in the wombs of their mothers and the loins of their fathers. Then God Almighty informed Noah about what He would do to the wretched among his descendants, saying to him: And nations, meaning: and generations and groups, We will grant them enjoyment in the life of this world, meaning: We will provide them in it what they will enjoy, until they reach their appointed times, then a painful punishment will touch them from Us, meaning: then We will make them taste, when they come to Us, a painful, grievous punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi: “It was said, ‘O Noah, disembark with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon the nations of those with you,’” to the end of the verse. He said: Every believing man and woman entered into that peace until the Day of Resurrection, and every disbelieving woman entered into that punishment and enjoyment until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Dawud Al-Hafri told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi: “It was said, ‘O Noah, disembark with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon the nations of those with you.’” He said: Every believing man and woman entered Islam, and every unbelieving man and woman entered polytheism. Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, reciting on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And upon nations from among those with you, meaning: from those who have not yet been born. Blessings have been decreed for those for whom happiness has been predestined in God’s knowledge and decree, and nations We will grant enjoyment, for whom misery has been predestined in God’s knowledge and decree. Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, something similar, except that he said: And nations We will grant enjoyment to, the enjoyment of worldly life, for those who had previously been destined for misery in God’s knowledge and judgment. He said: And the children did not perish on the day that the people of Noah were drowned because of the sin of their fathers, like the birds and wild beasts, but their time came with the drowning. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said about His statement: “Descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from among those with you and nations We will grant enjoyment,” he said: They descended, and God was pleased with them. They descended with peace from God. They were people of mercy from the people of that time, then He brought forth from them a generation after that, nations, some of whom He had mercy on and some of whom He punished. And he recited: And upon nations from among those with you and nations We will grant enjoyment, and that is because the nations separated from that group that came out of that water and were safe. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj who said, I heard Abu Muadh who said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us who said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, “O Noah, disembark with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from among those with you,” the verse, he said: Blessings upon you and upon nations from among those with you who were not born, God has made blessings obligatory for them because of what has already been decreed for them in God’s knowledge of happiness, and nations We will grant enjoyment, meaning: the enjoyment of worldly life, then a painful punishment will touch them from Us, because of what has already been decreed for them in God’s knowledge of misery. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan: That when he recited Surat Hud and came to: “O Noah, disembark with peace from Us and blessings upon you,” until he finished the verse, Al-Hasan said: So God saved Noah and those who believed, and those who enjoyed themselves were destroyed! Until he mentioned the prophets, all of that he would say: God saved him and those who enjoyed themselves were destroyed! Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: We will grant them enjoyment, then a painful punishment will touch them from Us, he said: after the mercy. Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid told us, he said, my father told me, he said, Abdullah bin Shawdhab told us, he said, I heard Dawud bin Abi Hind narrating, on the authority of Al-Hasan: That he came upon this verse: “Descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon peoples from among those with you. And peoples We will grant enjoyment; then a painful punishment will touch them from Us.” He said: That was when God sent ‘Aad, and He sent Hud to them. Some believed him and some denied him, until the command of God came. When the command of God came, God saved Hud and those who believed with him, and God destroyed those who enjoyed themselves. Then God sent Thamud, and He sent Salih to them. Some believed him and some denied him, until the command of God came. When the command of God came, God saved Salih and those who believed with him, and God destroyed those who enjoyed themselves. Then the prophets settled, one by one, in something like this.
11:49: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: This story that I have informed you of, of the story of Noah and his report and the report of his people, is from the report of the unseen, meaning: it is from the report of the unseen that you did not witness, so you learn it. We reveal it to you, meaning: We reveal it to you, so we make it known to you. You did not know it, nor did your people, before this, the revelation that We reveal to you. So be patient, in carrying out God’s command and conveying His message, and in what you encounter from the polytheists of your people, as Noah was patient. Indeed, the [best] outcome is for the righteous, meaning: Indeed, the good outcome of matters is for those who fear God, so they perform His obligations and avoid His disobedience. They are the winners of what they hope for of bliss in the Hereafter, and success in this world with the seekers, as was the outcome of Noah when he was patient with God’s command, that He saved him from destruction with those who believed in Him, and gave him in The Hereafter, what honor He gave him, and drowned those who denied Him, and destroyed them all. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: “This is from the report of the unseen which We reveal to you. You did not know it, nor did your people, before this,” the Qur’an, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his people would not have known what Noah and his people did, had it not been for what God explained to him in His Book.
11:50: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And We sent to the people of `Ad their brother Hud, and he said to them: O my people, worship God, alone, without partner, without what you worship besides Him of gods and idols, You have no god other than Him, meaning: You have no god worthy of worship from you other than Him, so devote your worship to Him and single Him out as divinity, You are nothing but fabricators, meaning: You are, in your associating gods and idols with Him, nothing but people of a town who are liars, inventing falsehood, because there is no god other than Him.
11:51: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says, informing about what Hud said to his al-Nas 114:O my people, I do not ask you for any reward or recompense for what I call you to, of sincere worship of God and abandoning idols and disavowing them. My reward is only from Him who created me. He says: My reward and recompense for my advice to you and your calling to God is only from Him who created me. Do you not understand? He says: Do you not understand that if I had sought by calling you to God other than advice to you and seeking your good fortune in this world and the next, I would have sought from you for that some of the worldly goods and asked you for reward and recompense? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: My reward is only from Him who created me, meaning: He created me.
11:52: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says, informing about what Hud said to his al-Nas 114:O my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord, meaning: Believe in Him so that He may forgive you your sins. And seeking forgiveness is believing in God in this context, because Hud, peace be upon him, only called his people to the oneness of God so that He would forgive them their sins, as Noah said to his al-Nas 114:(Worship God and fear Him and obey me. He will forgive you some of your sins and give you respite for a specified term.) And His statement: Then repent to Him, meaning: Then repent to God for your previous sins and your worship of other than Him, after believing in Him, He will send down abundant rain upon you, meaning: If you believe in God and repent from your disbelief in Him, He will send down rain upon you, bringing you rain to satisfy your need for it, and your land will be revived from drought and famine. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali bin Dawud told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: profusely, meaning: one after the other. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: He sends down upon you abundant rain, he said: He sends down upon them rain and drops. As for his saying: And He will add strength to your strength, Mujahid used to say about that, what: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: And He will add strength to your strength, he said: Strength to your strength. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid and Ishaq, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid - Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Mujahid said, and he mentioned something similar. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And He will add strength to your strength, he said: He gave them strength, so if they had obeyed Him, He would have added strength to their strength. And he mentioned to us that it was only said to them, And He will add strength to your strength, he said: Because their offspring had been cut off for years, so Hud said to them: If you believe in God, God will revive your land and provide you with wealth and children. Because that is from strength. And His statement: And do not turn away as criminals, meaning: Do not turn away from what I call you to of the oneness of God and disavowal of idols and statues, as criminals, meaning: disbelievers in God.
11:53: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: The people of Hud said to Hud 11:O Hud, you have not brought us any explanation or proof for what you say, so we submit to you and acknowledge that you are truthful in what you call us to regarding the oneness of God and the acknowledgement of your prophethood. And we will not abandon our gods, meaning: because of what you say or because of what you say. And we will not believe in you, meaning: they said: And we will not believe in what you claim of prophethood and the message from God to us.
11:54: God Almighty said: We say nothing but that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil. He said, Indeed, I call God to witness, and you to witness, that I am innocent of what you associate with Him.
11:55: Abu Ja'far said: This is report from God, the Most High, about the words of the people of Hud, that they said to him, when he advised them and called them to the Oneness of God and to believe in Him, and to abandon the idols and to disavow them: We will not abandon the worship of our gods, and we only say that what made you criticize them and forbid the worship of them is that you have been afflicted with madness from them. So Hud said to them: I call God to witness against myself, and I also call you to witness, O people, that I am innocent of what you associate in the worship of God from your gods and idols besides Him, so plot against me all together, meaning: then plot against me, you all together, and your gods, to harm and hurt me, then do not wait, meaning: then do not delay that, so see if you and they will achieve what you claimed that your gods achieved for me of evil? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Some of our gods have afflicted you with evil, he said: The idols have afflicted you with madness. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Some of our gods have afflicted you with evil, he said: The idols have afflicted you with madness. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibn Dukayn told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Mujahid: Except that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil, he said: You have insulted and reviled our gods, so I have made you insane. He said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Some of our gods have afflicted you with evil, some of our gods have afflicted you with evil, meaning the idols. He said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: We say nothing but that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil, he said: The idols have afflicted you with madness. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: We say nothing but that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil, he said: Our gods have afflicted you with madness. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Except that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil, he said: What makes you criticize our gods is that they have afflicted you with evil. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: We say nothing but that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil, he said: You are only doing this to our gods, that they have afflicted you with evil. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Abdullah bin Katheer said: Our gods have afflicted you with evil. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: We say nothing but that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil, they say: We fear that evil will befall you from our gods, and we do not like for them to befall you. They say: Evil will befall you from them. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: We say nothing except that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil, they say: Your mind has become confused and this has afflicted you, because of what our gods have done to you. His saying: It afflicted you, is derived from: The thing afflicted me, meaning it struck you, as the poet said: From the people who are exposed to it with audacity and sin
11:56: Abu Ja`far said: He says: I am in God, He is my Master and your Master, and the Guardian of all His creation. I have put my trust in Him, that you and any other creation will harm me, for there is nothing that moves on the earth except that God is its Master, and it is in His grasp and His authority. It is humble and submissive to Him. If someone says: How is it said: He is holding her by the forelock, so that the forelock is specifically held, and not the rest of the body. It was said: Because the Arabs used to use that to describe themselves as humble and submissive, so they would say: The forelock of so-and-so is in the hand of so-and-so, meaning: He is obedient to him, and he directs him as he wishes. And when they captured a prisoner and wanted to release him and show him a favor, they would cut his forelock, so that they could take advantage of him by that as a source of pride when boasting. So God addressed them in a way that they knew in their speech, and the meaning is what I mentioned. And his saying: Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path, means that my Lord is on the path of truth. He rewards the good-doer among His creation with his goodness, and the evil-doer with his evil. He does not wrong any of them in the least, and He does not accept from them anything except Islam and belief in Him, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.
11:57: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says, informing about what Hud said to his al-Nas 114:But if they turn away, meaning if they turn away, turning away from what I call them to of the oneness of God and abandoning the worship of idols, I have conveyed to you, O people, that with which I have been sent to you, and the Messenger has no duty except to convey, and my Lord will replace you with a people other than you, meaning my Lord will destroy you, then my Lord will replace you with a people other than you, who will worship Him alone and be sincere in their worship of Him, and you will not harm Him at all, meaning you will not be able to harm Him if He wants to destroy you, or He destroys you. It has been said: Your destruction does not harm Him if He destroys you. You do not diminish anything from Him, because it is the same to Him whether you exist or not. Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over all things. He says: My Lord is Guardian and Knowledgeable over all His creation. He says: He is the One who protects me from being harmed by you.
11:58: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And when Our punishment came to the people of Hud, We saved Hud from it and those who believed in God with him, by mercy from Us, meaning: by His grace and favor upon them, and We saved them from a severe punishment, meaning: We also saved them from a severe punishment on the Day of Resurrection, just as We saved them in this world from the wrath that I brought down upon `Ad.
11:59: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And these are the ones upon whom We inflicted Our punishment and torment, the `Ad tribe, who denied God’s proofs and arguments, and disobeyed His messengers whom He sent to them to call to His Oneness and to follow His command, and they followed the command of every stubborn tyrant, meaning: every one who is arrogant towards God, deviating from the truth, not calling to Him or accepting Him. It is said: He is stubborn about the truth, so he is stubborn and the man is stubborn and stubborn. And from that it is said about the vein that bursts and does not stop: a stubborn vein, meaning harmful, and from that is the saying of the rajaz poet: I am too old to be stubborn Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And they followed the command of every stubborn tyrant, the polytheist.
11:60: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: And the people of Hud were pursued by ‘Aad in this world, in anger from God, and in wrath on the Day of Resurrection like it, a curse in addition to the curse that had preceded for them from God in this world, “Behold, ‘Aad disbelieved in their Lord. So away with ‘Aad, the people of Hud,” meaning: God distanced them from goodness. It is said: So-and-so disbelieved in his Lord and disbelieved in his Lord, and I thanked you, and I thanked you. It was said: The meaning of they disbelieved in their Lord is that they disbelieved in the blessing of their Lord.
11:61: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And We sent to Thamud their brother Salih, and he said to them: O my people, worship God alone, with no partner for Him, and devote worship to Him alone, without any other gods besides Him, for you have no god other than Him who requires your worship, and divinity is not permissible except for Him, He created you from the earth, meaning: He began your creation from the earth. He said that because he created Adam from the earth, so the address was directed to them, since that was what he did to those who were from him. And He made you inhabit it, meaning: He made you inhabit it, so the meaning was: He made you dwell in it for the days of your life. From their saying: So-and-so built so-and-so’s house, and it is his lifespan. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: And He made you live therein, he said: He made you live therein. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And He made you live therein, meaning: He made you live. And His statement: Then seek His forgiveness, meaning: Do an action that will be a reason for God to cover your sins, and that is belief in Him, and sincere worship of Him alone, and following His Messenger Salih. Then repent to Him, meaning: Then leave the actions that your Lord dislikes, for what He is pleased with and loves. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive, meaning: My Lord is near to whoever sincerely worships Him and desires repentance from Him, and He responds to him when he calls upon Him.
11:62: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Thamud said to their prophet Salih: O Salih, you were a source of hope among us, meaning: We were hoping that you would be a master among us before this statement that you made to us, that we have no god other than God. Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped? He says: Do you forbid us to worship the gods that our fathers worshipped? And indeed, we are in disquieting doubt about that to which you invite us, meaning that they did not know the truth of what he was calling them to of the oneness of God, and that divinity is only for Him alone. His saying: Suspicious, meaning that it causes suspicion, from: I made him suspicious, so I made him suspicious, if you did something to him that causes him suspicion, and from this is the saying of Al-Hudhali: If I came to him from the unseen, he would smell my affection and pluck my clothes. As if I had made him suspicious
11:63: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Salih said to his people from Thamud: O my people, have you considered, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, meaning: if I am upon proof and explanation from God that I have learned and been certain of, and He has given me mercy from Himself, meaning: and He has given me prophethood, wisdom, and Islam, then who will protect me from God if I disobey Him? meaning: who will repel His punishment from me if He punishes me if I disobey Him, and save me from Him? Then you will not increase me, with your excuse that you make, that you worship what your fathers used to worship, except loss, meaning that He will make you lose your share of God’s mercy, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Then you will not increase me except in loss, he said: You will not increase in anything but loss.
11:64: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says, informing about what Salih said to his people from Thamud, when they said to him: And indeed, we are in disquieting doubt about that to which you invite us, and they asked him for a sign for what he invited them to: O my people, this is the she-camel of God as a sign for you, meaning: an argument, a sign, and an indication of the truth of what I am calling you to, so leave her to graze in God’s land, so you are not responsible for her sustenance or her expenses, and do not touch her with harm, meaning: do not kill her or harm her by hamstringing her, lest a near punishment seize you, meaning: if you touch her with harm, a punishment from God will seize you not far away and destroy you.
11:65: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: So Thamud hamstrung the she-camel of God. There is an omission in the speech that has been omitted, as the apparent meaning is sufficient for it, which is: they denied him, they hamstrung her. Then Salih said to them: Enjoy yourselves in your home for three days, meaning: Enjoy your life in this world for three days. That is a promise not to be denied, meaning: This term that He has given you is a promise from God. He promised you that when it ends, you will be destroyed and that punishment will descend upon you. Not to be denied, meaning: He who informed you of that did not lie to you about it. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: “So they hamstrung her. He said, ‘Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. This is a promise not to be denied.’” And he mentioned to us that when Salih informed them that the punishment had come to them, they put on blankets and cloaks, and it was said to them: The sign of that is that your colors will turn yellow on the first day, then red on the second day, then black on the third day. And he mentioned to us that when they hamstrung the she-camel, they regretted it and said: You have to have a young camel! So the young camel climbed the mountain until the third day it faced the qiblah and said: O Lord of my mother! O Lord of my mother, three times. He said: Then the scream was sent at that time. Ibn Abbas used to say: If you climbed the continent, you would see the bones of the young camel. The dwellings of Thamud were in Hajar, between Ash-Sham and Madinah. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Enjoy yourselves in your home for three days, he said: the rest of their lifespans. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: Ibn Abbas said: If you climbed the continent, you would see the bones of the young camel.
11:66: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: So when Our punishment came to Thamud, We saved Salih and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, meaning by grace and favor from God, and from the disgrace of that Day, meaning: And We saved them from the humiliation of that Day, and the disgrace of that punishment, Indeed, your Lord is the Strong, in His might, when He strikes something He destroys it, as He destroyed Thamud when He struck them, the Mighty, so no one can overcome Him, and no one can subdue Him, rather He overcomes everything and subdues it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: With mercy from Us and from the disgrace of that Day, he said: God saved him with mercy from Him, and saved him from the disgrace of that Day. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Hussein narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdullah, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Amr bin Kharijah, who said: We said to him: Tell us the story of Thamud! He said: I will tell you from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Thamud: Thamud were the people of Salih. God granted them long life in this world, until one of them would build a house out of mud and it would collapse while the other man among them was still alive. When they saw that, they made houses out of the mountains and carved them out, dug them out, and hollowed them out. They were in a comfortable life. They said: O Salih, call upon your Lord to bring out for us a sign so that we may know that you are the Messenger of God! So Salih called upon his Lord, and He brought out for them the she-camel. She would drink one day, and they would drink one day at a time. When the day came for her to drink, they would leave her and the water, and milk her with milk that would fill every vessel, container, and waterskin. When the day of their drinking came, they turned her away from the water and she did not drink anything from it, so they filled every vessel, container and water skin. Then God revealed to Salih: Your people will hamstring your she-camel! He said to them, and they said: We would not do that! He said: Unless you hamstring her, a child will soon be born among you who will hamstring her. They said: What is the sign of that child? By God, if we find him, we will kill him! He said: He is a blond, blue-eyed, reddish boy who will not find a match for her. So they gathered in a council, and one of them said to the other: What prevents you from marrying your son? He said: I cannot find a match for him. He said: My daughter is a match for him, and I will marry you to her. So he married her, and that child was born between them. There were eight men in the city who were spreading corruption on earth and not reforming it. When Salih said to them, It is only a child born among you that will cause it to be barren, they chose eight women midwives from the village and appointed a police officer with them. They would go around the village and if they found a woman in labor they would see what her child was. If it was a boy they would turn him over and see what it was, but if it was a girl they would turn her away. When they found the child, the women cried out and said, This is the one whom the Messenger of God, Salih, wants! The police officers wanted to take him, but his grandparents stood between them and him and said, If Salih had wanted this, we would have killed him! He was the worst of children. He would grow up to be a youth in a day like other children on Friday, and a youth in a month like other children on Friday, and a youth in a month like other children on a year would grow up to be a youth in a month like other children on a year. Then the eight who were spreading corruption on earth and not reforming it gathered, including the two sheikhs, and said, Appoint this boy over us because of his status and the honor of his grandparents. There were nine of them. Salih did not sleep with them in the village. He was in a mosque called Salih’s Mosque, where he would spend the night. When morning came, he would come to them and preach to them and remind them. When evening came, he would go out to his mosque and spend the night there. Hajjaj said: Ibn Jurayj said: When Salih told them: A boy will be born who will be the cause of your destruction, they said: So what do you command us to do? He said: I command you to kill them! So they killed them except one. He said: That child barely reached the age of puberty. They said: If we did not kill our children, every man among us would have the same. This is the work of Salih! So they conspired among themselves to kill him, and they said: We will go out as travelers and people will see us openly, then we will return on such and such a night of such and such a month, and we will lie in wait for him at his prayer place and kill him, and people will think that we are travelers, just as we are! So they advanced until they entered under a rock to lie in wait for him, and God sent a rock upon them that crushed them, and they became crushed. Then some men who had seen that among them set out, and they were crushed, so they returned shouting in the village: O servants of God, was Salih not pleased that he ordered them to kill their children until he killed them! So the people of the village agreed to kill the she-camel all together, and they refrained from it except for that son of the tenth. Then the hadith returned to the hadith of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: They wanted to plot against Salih, so they walked until they came to a path on Salih’s road, and eight of them hid in it. They said: If he comes out against us, we will kill him and go to his family, so we spent the night with them! Then God commanded the earth to level out from them. He said: So they gathered and walked to the she-camel while it was standing at its watering place. The wicked man said to one of them: Go to her and hamstring her! So he went to her, and that was too much for him, so he refused. So he sent another, and that was too much for him. He would not send a man except that her matter was too much for him, until they walked to her, and he reached out and struck her hocks, so she fell running. One of them came to Salih and said: Catch up with the she-camel, she has been hamstrung! So he came, and they went out to meet him and apologize to him: O Prophet of God, it was so-and-so who hamstrung her, it is not our fault! He said: Then look, will you catch up with her foal? If you catch him, perhaps God will lift the punishment from you! So they went out looking for him, and when the foal saw his mother struggling, he came to a short mountain called Al-Qara. He climbed it, and they went to get him, but God inspired the mountain, and it rose high in the sky, so that the birds could not reach him. He said: Salih entered the village, and when the foal saw him, he cried until his tears flowed, then he met Salih and blew a foam, then blew another, then blew another. Salih said to his al-Nas 114:Every foam has a term of one day, “Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise that will not be denied.” Beware, the sign of the punishment is that on the first day your faces will become yellow, the second day red, and the third day black. So when they woke up, their faces were as if they had been smeared with saffron, young and old, male and female. When they reached the evening, they all cried out: Beware, a day of the term has passed, and the punishment has come to you! When they woke up on the second day, their faces were red, as if they had been stained with blood. They cried out and wept and recognized the sign of the punishment. When they reached evening, they cried out all together: Behold, two days have passed from the appointed time, and the punishment has come to you! When they woke up on the third day, their faces were black, as if they had been coated with tar. They cried out all together: Behold, the punishment has come to you! So they shrouded themselves and covered themselves. Their embalming was patience and steadfastness, and their shrouds were carpets. Then they threw themselves to the ground and began to turn their eyes, looking at the sky one time and at the earth another time, not knowing from where the punishment would come to them, from above them in the sky, or from beneath their feet in the earth, out of greed and fear. When they woke up on the fourth day, a cry came to them from the sky, in which was the sound of every thunderbolt and the sound of everything that has a sound on earth. Their hearts were torn in their chests, and they became kneeling in their homes. Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Hussein narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: I was told that when the blast overtook them, God destroyed them from the east and the west, except for one man who was in the sanctuary of God, and the sanctuary of God protected him from the punishment of God. It was said: Who is he, O Messenger of God? He said: He said: Abu Righal. “And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions when he came upon the village of Thamud: Let none of you enter the village, and do not drink from their water.” And he showed them the ascent of the camel when it ascended the continent. Ibn Jurayj said: Musa bin Uqbah informed me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to the village of Thamud, he said: Do not enter upon these people who are being punished unless you are weeping. If you are not weeping, then do not enter upon them, lest what befell them befall you.” Ibn Jurayj said, Jabir ibn Abdullah said: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to the stone, he praised God and thanked Him, then said: ‘As for what follows, do not ask your Messenger for signs. These are the people of Salih who asked their Messenger for a sign, so he sent them the she-camel, which would come from this pass and come from that pass, and drink their water on the day it came.’” Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: “It was mentioned to us that when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by the valley of Thamud while he was heading towards Tabuk, he said: He ordered his companions to hasten their journey, and not to stop in it, nor to drink from its water, and he informed them that it was a cursed valley. He said: It was mentioned to us that a wealthy man from the people of Salih would give the poor among them what they could shroud themselves with, and a man from among them would dig a grave for himself and his family, for the appointment with the Prophet of God, Salih, which he had promised them. And he told those who saw them on the roads, in the courtyards, and in the houses, among them were young men and old men, God left them as a lesson and a sign.” Ismail bin Al-Mutawakkil Al-Ashja’i from the people of Homs narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Katheer narrated to us, he said: Abdullah bin Waqid narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Othman bin Khathim, he said: Abu Al-Tufayl narrated to us, he said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to fight in Tabuk, Al-Hijr came down and said: O people, do not ask your Prophet for signs. These are the people of Salih who asked their Prophet to send them a sign, so God sent them the she-camel as a sign. She would come to them on the day she came from this pass, and drink their water. On the day she came, they would provision themselves from it, then milk her as they had provisioned themselves from their water before that, milk. Then she would come out from that pass. But they rebelled against the command of their Lord and hamstrung her, so God promised them punishment after three days, and it was a promise from God that was not to be denied. So God destroyed everyone of them in the east and west of the earth except one man who was in the sanctuary of God, so the sanctuary of God protected him from the punishment of God. They said: Who is that man, O Messenger of God? He said: Abu Righal.
11:67: God Almighty says: And the shriek seized those who did wrong, and they became within their homes, fallen down.
11:68: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And those who did what they should not have done, of hamstringing God’s she-camel and disbelieving in Him, were struck by the blast, and they became in their homes, fallen down, death had crushed them and left them dormant in their courtyards, as: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And they became in their homes, prostrate, meaning: they became destroyed. As if they had never sung in it, he says: as if they had never lived in it, nor inhabited it, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: As if they had never lived in it, means as if they had never lived in it. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. We have already explained this with evidence, so there is no need to repeat it. And His statement: Indeed, Thamud disbelieved in their Lord, meaning: Indeed, Thamud disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and denied them. Indeed, away with Thamud, meaning: May God distance Thamud, for the punishment descended upon them.
11:69: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And Our messengers came, from the angels, and they were, as mentioned, Gabriel and two other angels, and it was said: that the other two angels were Michael and Israfil with him, to Abraham, meaning: Abraham the friend of God, with good tidings, meaning: with good tidings. They differed about the good report they brought him. Some of them said: It is the good report of Isaac. Some of them said: It is the good report of the destruction of Lot's people. They said, "Peace be upon you," meaning, they greeted him with peace. And the word “peace” is in the accusative case by applying they said to it, as if it was said: They said a saying and greeted with peace. He said, “Peace,” meaning: Abraham said to them, “Peace,” so he raised “Peace,” meaning: Peace be upon you, or meaning: Peace from you. It was mentioned that the Arabs say: Salam in the sense of peace, just as they said: Hal and Halal, Haram and Haram. Al-Farra’ mentioned that some Arabs recited: We passed by and said: "Yes, peace be upon you." So I was safe, just as the clouds are covered with lightning. Meaning: Peace. It has been narrated: As he was rejected. Some of them claimed that its meaning, if read in this way, is: We are at peace with you, from the word “peace,” which is the opposite of war. This is a general reading of the Kufians. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Basra read this as: “They said, ‘Peace.’ He said, ‘Peace.’” This means that the response from Abraham, peace be upon him, to them was similar to their greeting: “Peace be upon you.” Abu Ja`far said: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two readings with similar meanings, because as-salam may mean peace, as I have described, and as-salam may mean peace, because greeting is almost never done except between people of peace, not enemies. So if greeting is mentioned from one people to another, and the response of others to them, this indicates that they are at peace with one another. And despite that, they are two readings, and each of them has been read by people who are role models in reading, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. He said: He did not take long to bring a roasted calf. Its origin is Mahnuth, which was changed from Mafool to Fa’il. Arabs differed about its meaning. Some of the people of Basra said: The meaning of Mahnuth is roasted. He said: It is also said: Hanathat Farsi, meaning: I heated it and made it sweat. And he cited as evidence for his saying that the following verse of the Rajaz: And he was afraid that they would make a mess Another of them said: He made his horse lean, meaning he made it thin. And he said: They said: He made him lean, meaning he made him sweat. Some of the people of Kufa said: Everything that is roasted in the ground, if you dig a trench for it in it, bury it and cover it, it is called Haneeth and Mahnoth. He said: And horses are called Haneeth if you throw blankets over them, one on top of the other, so that they sweat.
