He said: And it is said: If you give water to drink, then Haneeth means: I lower it, meaning: I lower the water and increase the wine. As for the people of interpretation, they said about its meaning what I am mentioning, and that is what: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: With a roasted calf, he said: cooked. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: With a roasted calf, he said: With a roasted calf, meaning the offal of a cow, and the roasted calf means the roasted meat. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And Our messengers had brought Abraham good tidings to a roasted calf, he said: cooked, ground, cooked with stones. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: He did not delay in bringing a cooked calf, and cooked calf means cooked meat. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: With a roasted calf, he said: cooked. He said: Al-Kalbi said: And the roasted calf is that which is roasted on the ground. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Hamid, on the authority of Shammar, regarding his statement: Then he brought a roasted calf, he said: The roasted calf is the one dripping with water, and it has been roasted. Hafs said: The roasted calf is like the roasted calf of a horse. Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: He slaughtered it and then roasted it in the brazier, so it is the Haneeth when he roasted it. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Zaid told us, on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Hafs ibn Hamid, on the authority of Shammar ibn Atiyah: So he brought a roasted calf, he said: the roasted one that drips. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Hafs bin Hamid, on the authority of Shammar bin Atiyah, he said: Al-Haneeth is that from which water drips, and it has been roasted. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: With a cooked veal, he said: cooked. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: with a roasted calf, that is, one that was cooked with stones. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us: He did not wait long before he brought a roasted calf, he said: Roasted. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, he said, Abdul Samad told me: that he heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: Haneeth, meaning: grilled. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: Hanadh is ripening. Abu Jaafar said: These sayings that we mentioned from the people of Arabic and the people of interpretation are close in meaning to each other. The position of an in his saying: that he came with a roasted calf, is in the accusative case because of his saying: and he did not delay in coming.
11:70: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: When Abraham saw that their hands could not reach the calf that he had brought to them, and the food that was presented to them, he was surprised at them. This is because when he presented his food to them, peace and blessings of God be upon him, as mentioned, they refrained from eating it, because they were not among those who would eat it. Their refraining from eating it, in the presence of Abraham, while they were his guests, was surprising. There was no acquaintance or respect between them, and he felt fear of them in his soul. Qatada used to say: His denial of that was part of their affair, as: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: When he saw that their hands did not reach him, he was not pleased with them and felt fear of them. When a guest came to the Arabs and he did not eat their food, they thought that he had not brought good report and that he was thinking evil of himself. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: But when he saw that their hands did not reach it, he disliked them, he said: When a guest came to them and he did not eat from their food, they thought that he had not brought any good, and that he was thinking evil of himself. Then they told him at that time what they had brought. Another said about this: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Qais, on the authority of Jundub bin Sufyan, he said: When the guest of Abraham, peace be upon him, entered, the calf was brought to them, and they began to poke arrows in their hands, but their hands could not reach it. He did not recognize them at that. It is said: I denied the thing and I denied and I denied have the same meaning. From I denied and I denied, the saying of Al-A’sha: And you denied me, and the only thing you denied of the events was gray hair and baldness. He combined both languages in one verse, and Abu Dhu’ayb said: We denied it, we fled, and a violent, raging, and violent storm swept through it. And His saying: And he felt fear of them, meaning: He felt fear of them in himself and concealed it. They said, ‘Do not fear,’ meaning: The angels said, when they saw Abraham’s fear of them: Do not fear us and be safe, for we are the angels of your Lord, ‘sent to the people of Lot.’ The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And his wife was standing and laughing. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And his wife, Sarah, daughter of Haran, son of Nahor, son of Saruj, son of Ra’u, son of Peleg, and she is the cousin of Abraham, standing. It was said: She was standing from behind the curtain, listening to the words of the messengers and the words of Abraham, peace be upon him. It was also said: She was standing, serving the messengers, and Abraham was sitting with the messengers. And his saying: So I laughed. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his saying: So I laughed, and regarding the reason for which she laughed. Some of them said: She laughed the well-known laugh, in amazement that she and her husband Ibrahim were serving their guests themselves, as an honor to them, while they were abstaining from their food and not eating. Who said that? Musa bin Harun told me, Amr bin Hammad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: God sent the angels to destroy the people of Lot. They came walking in the form of young men, until they descended upon Abraham and offered him hospitality. When Abraham saw them, he went back to his family and brought a fattened calf, slaughtered it, then roasted it on embers. It is called Haneeth when it is roasted. He came to them and sat with them, and Sarah stood serving them. This is when it says: And his wife was standing while he was sitting, in the recitation of Ibn Masoud. When he brought it near to them, he said: Will you not eat? They said: O Abraham, we do not eat food except for a price. He said: This has a price. They said: What is its price? He said: You mention the name of God at the beginning of it, and praise Him at the end of it. Gabriel looked at Michael and said: It is right for this man to be taken by his Lord as a friend. When he saw that their hands did not reach him - he said: they did not eat - he was terrified of them and felt fear of them. When Sarah saw that he had honored them and she stood up to serve them, she laughed and said: It is strange that these are our guests. We serve them ourselves out of honor for them, and they do not eat our food. Others said: Rather, she laughed because Lot’s people were heedless, and God’s messengers had come to destroy them. Who said that? Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: When Abraham felt fear in his soul, they told him what they had come with, so his wife laughed and was amazed that a people had been afflicted with punishment while they were unaware. So she laughed at that and was amazed: So We gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, that he said, I laughed in amazement at the heedlessness of the people of Lot, and at the punishment that came to them. Others said: Rather, she laughed because she thought that they wanted to do the work of the people of Lot. Who said that? Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Ma`shar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Qais, regarding his statement: And his wife was standing, and she laughed, he said: When the angels came, she thought that they wanted to do as the people of Lot did. Others said: Rather, she laughed when she saw her husband Ibrahim in fear. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Kalbi: She laughed, he said: She laughed when they frightened Ibrahim, because of what she saw of the fright in Ibrahim. Others said: Rather, she laughed when she was given the good report of Isaac, out of astonishment that she would have a son at her advanced age and the age of her husband. Those who said that mentioned: Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq told us, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, Abdul Samad told me: He heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: When the angels came to Abraham, peace be upon him, and he saw them, he was amazed by their appearance and beauty, so they greeted him and sat down next to him. He stood up and ordered a fattened calf to be prepared for him, and the food was brought to them. But when he saw that their hands did not reach it, he did not recognize them and felt fear of them, and Sarah was behind the house listening. They said: Do not fear, for we give you good tidings of a forbearing and blessed boy. He gave his wife Sarah good tidings of him, so she laughed and wondered: How can I have a son when I am old, and he is a very old man? They said: Are you amazed at the command of God, for He is able to do whatever He wills. God has given him to you, so be glad about him. Some of those who interpreted this interpretation said: This is from the introduction which means delay, as if the meaning of the speech according to him is: And his wife was standing, so We gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob. So she laughed and said: Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman? Others said: Rather, the meaning of his saying, So she laughed, in this context is that she menstruated. Who said that? Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me, he said, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, on the authority of Ali bin Harun, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Azhar, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: So she laughed, he said: She menstruated, and she was ninety-something years old. He said: And Ibrahim was one hundred years old. Others said: Rather, she laughed with joy at being safe from them, when they said to Abraham: Do not be afraid, because he had feared them, and she also feared them as Abraham feared them. So when she felt safe, she laughed, and they followed her with the good report of Isaac. Some of the Kufian Arabs claimed that they had not heard the word dahkat meaning menstruated from a reliable person. Some of the Basran Arabists mentioned that some of the people of Hijaz told him on the authority of some of them that the Arabs say: The woman laughed, she menstruated. He said: And he said: Laughter, menstruation. And some of them said: Laughter is the mouth, and he mentioned the verse of Abu Dhu’ayb: He came up with a mixture that people had never seen before, which was laughter, except that it was the work of bees. He mentioned that some of his companions recited to him about laughter, meaning menstruation: The laughter of the rabbits on the rock is like the blood of the belly on the day of the encounter. He said: Some of his companions told him that he heard Al-Kumait say: So the hyenas laughed at Saad's swords by killing me. He did not bury or pay a debt. He said: He means menstruation. He said: And on the authority of Bilharith bin Kaab, they say: The palm tree laughed, if it produced the date palm or the unripe dates. And they said: The laughter, the date palm. He said: And we heard someone say: I made a pond laugh, meaning: I filled it until it overflowed. He said: And it is as if the meaning is close to each other, because it is as if it is something that is filled and then overflows. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the statements mentioned in this regard is the statement of the one who said: The meaning of his statement, So I laughed, is that I was amazed at the heedlessness of the people of Lot regarding the punishment of God that had surrounded them and their heedlessness of it. We said that this statement is more correct because it was mentioned after their saying to Abraham: Do not fear, indeed we have been sent to the people of Lot. If that is the case, and there is no reason to laugh and be amazed at their saying to Abraham: Do not fear, then the laughter and amazement were only about the matter of the people of Lot.
11:71: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: So We gave good tidings to Sarah, the wife of Abraham, as a reward from Us for her disapproval and astonishment at what Lot had said, of Isaac, a son for her, and after Isaac, Jacob, meaning: after Isaac, Jacob, from her son Isaac. In Arabic, the word back means the son’s child, and this is how the interpreters interpreted it. Who said that? Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of `Amir, who said: And after Isaac, Jacob. He said: The descendants are the descendants of the descendants. Amr bin Ali and Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, each of them said: Abu Al-Yasa’ Ismail bin Hammad bin Abi Al-Mughirah, the client of Al-Ash’ari, told me: I was next to my grandfather, Abu Al-Mughirah bin Mihran, in the mosque of Ali bin Zaid, when Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan passed by us and said: O Abu Al-Mughirah, who is this young man? He said: The son of the one behind me. Al-Hasan said: Then we gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob. Amr bin Ali and Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, they said, Muhammad bin Abi Uday told us, he said, Dawud bin Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding his statement: So We gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob, he said: The son is the offspring, which is the successor. Ishaq bin Shaheen told me, he said, Khalid told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Amer, regarding his statement: And after Isaac, Jacob, he said: The successors are the children of the children. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, the same. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Amr Al-Azdi told us, he said: I heard Al-Sha’bi say: The children of the children are the children from behind. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, he said: A man came to Ibn Abbas with his grandson, and he said: Who is this with you? He said: This is my grandson. He said: This is your son from behind. It seemed that this was hard on that man, so Ibn Abbas said: God says: Then We gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob, so the children were born from behind. Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: When Sarah laughed and said: How strange are these guests of ours! We serve them ourselves out of honor for them, and they do not eat our food, Gabriel said to her: Rejoice in the good report of a son whose name will be Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob. She struck her face in amazement, and that is what He said: So she struck her face, and said: Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and my husband is an old man? Indeed, this is a strange thing. They said: “Do you marvel at the command of God? May the mercy and blessings of God be upon you, O people of the House. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious.” Sarah said: What is the sign of that? He said: “Then he took a dry stick in his hand and twisted it between his fingers, and it shook green. Then Abraham said: Then it is a sacrifice for God.” Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: So she laughed, meaning Sarah, when she learned of the command of God, may He be glorified, and when she learned of the people of Lot, who gave her the good report of Isaac and after Isaac, Jacob, with a son and a son’s son. So she said, striking her face - it is said: she struck her forehead - Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman? until His saying: Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious. There are different readings of this: The general reading of Iraq and the Hijaz is: And after Isaac, Jacob, with Jacob in the nominative case. He repeats the beginning of the speech by saying: And after Isaac, Jacob. And even though it is a subject, it indicates the meaning of good tidings. Some people from Kufa and Ash-Sham read, And after Isaac, Jacob, in the accusative case. As for the one from Syria, he mentioned that he used to incline Jacob towards the accusative case, by implying another verb similar to the good report, as if he said: And We gave him Jacob after Isaac. So since We gave him did not appear, the good report was applied to it, and it was conjoined with the position of Isaac. Since Isaac, even if it was preserved, it was in the sense of the accusative case by the action of We gave him good report, as the poet said: Bring me someone like the Banu Badr for their people, or someone like the family of Manzur bin Sayyar. Or Amer bin Tufail in his ship, or Harith, the day he called out to the al-Nas 114:O Harith! As for the Kufi, he read it with the interpretation of the genitive case, as mentioned about him, except that he put it in the accusative case because it does not flow. The scholars of Arabic have rejected this, because of the adjective entering between the conjunction and the noun. They said: It is wrong to say: I passed by Amr in the house, and in the house is Zaid, and you are conjoining Zaid to Amr, except by repeating the ba’ and repeating it. If you do not repeat it, then the correct way of speaking according to them is to raise it, and the accusative case is permissible. If the noun precedes the adjective, then the genitive case is permissible. This is if you say: I passed by Amr in the house, and Zaid is in the house. Some grammarians of Basra have permitted the genitive case, and the adjective is inserted between the conjunction and the noun. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads it in the nominative case, because that is the well-known speech of the Arabs, which is not disputed by those who know Arabic, and it is what the readings of the regions are based on. As for the accusative case, it has a reason, but I do not like to read it in this way, because the Book of God was revealed in the most eloquent of the Arab tongues, and the one who is more deserving of knowledge of what it was revealed in is eloquence.
11:72: God Almighty said: She said, ‘Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and my husband is an old man? Indeed, this is a strange thing.’
11:73: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: When Sarah was given the good report of Isaac that she would give birth, she was amazed at what was said to her, since she had reached the age at which no man or woman would give birth. It was said: She was ninety-nine years old at that time, and Ibrahim was one hundred years old. The narration was mentioned in what was narrated about that from Mujahid before: As for Ibn Ishaq, he said about that: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: Sarah was ninety years old when she was given the good report of Isaac, according to what some scholars told me, and Abraham was one hundred and twenty years old. Woe to me! is a word that Arabs say when they are surprised or disapproving of something. They say when they are surprised: Woe to his mother! What legs he has! The Arab scholars differed about this alif in Oh woe to me. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: This is a real alif. If you stop, you say: Woe to me! It is like the alif of lamentation, so it was made more subtle so that it would not be in a pause, and the ha’ was placed after it, so that it would be more clear and more distant in sound. That is because if the alif is between two letters, it has an echo, like the sound that is in the middle of something and reverberates in it, so it is more and more clear. Another said: This is the alif of lamentation, so if you stop on it, it is permissible, and if you stop on the ha’, it is permissible. He said: Do you not see that they stopped at his saying: And man calls, so they deleted the waw and confirmed it, and likewise: We did not desire, with the ya’ and other than the ya’. He said: This is stronger than the alif of lamentation and its ha’. Abu Jaafar said: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that this alif is the alif of lamentation, and stopping on it with the ha’ or without the ha’ is permissible in speech, because the Arabs use this in their speech. And his saying: Shall I give birth while I am old? means you say: How can I have a child, while I am old and my husband is an old man? And the husband, in this context, is the spouse. And he was called that because he is the one who takes care of her affairs, just as they called the owner of something its husband, and just as they said of the palm trees that are independent of the water of rivers and springs with rainwater, the husband, because the owner of the thing is the one who takes care of it, and the palm trees are the husband, with the water of the rain their life. And his saying: This is indeed a strange thing, meaning: The fact that a child is like me and my husband, at the age we are, is a strange thing. “They said: Do you marvel at the command of God?” God Almighty says: The messengers said to her: Do you marvel at a command that God has commanded to happen, and a decree that God has decreed concerning you and your husband? And his saying: The mercy of God and His blessings be upon you, the people of the house, he says: The mercy of God and His happiness be upon you, the people of the house of Abraham, and the alif and lam were made a successor of the addition, and his saying: He is Praiseworthy, Glorious, he says: God is praised for His favor upon you with what He has favored you with of blessings upon you and upon all of His creation, Glorious, he says: Possessor of glory, praise, and noble commendation. It is said of an action of his: The man glorified with glory, if he became like that. And if you mean that you praised him, you say: He glorified him with glorification.
11:74: God Almighty says: So when the fear had departed from Abraham and the good tidings had come to him, he began to argue with Us concerning the people of Lot.
11:75: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: When the fear that he had felt in his soul about Our messengers had gone away from Abraham, when he saw that their hands did not reach his food, and he felt secure that he had no intention of harming himself or his family, and the good tidings came to him, of Isaac, he continued, to argue with Us about the people of Lot. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: So when the fear had departed from Abraham, he said: the fear had departed from him, and the good tidings came to him, of Isaac. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: When the fear had left Abraham and the good report had come to him, of Isaac, and Jacob was born from the loins of Isaac, and he was safe from what he had feared, he said: (Praise be to God, who has given me, in my old age, Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.) It has been said: The meaning of this is: And the good report came to him that they did not want him. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And the good report came to him, he said: When they informed him that they had been sent to the people of Lot, and that they did not mean him. Others said: He was given good report of Isaac. As for al-Raw’, it is fear. It is said: Kadha terrified me meaning he feared it. “And from this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to a man: How can you be terrified by the believer?” And from this is the saying of Antarah: What surprised me was the load of its people in the middle of the country, pouring out the love of the Khamkham Meaning: What scared me. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Terror means separation. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid. He said, and Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: So when the fear had departed from Abraham, he said: the fear. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: When the fear had gone away from Abraham, he said: the fear. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: When the fear left Abraham, he said: the fear left him. And his saying: He disputes with us about the people of Lot, means: He disputes with us, as: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: He argues with us, he argues with us. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Some Arabists from Basra claimed that the meaning of his saying, He argues with us, is that he speaks to us. He said: Because Abraham does not argue with God, but rather asks Him and requests from Him. Abu Ja`far said: This is an ignorant statement, because God Almighty informed us in His Book that He would argue with the people of Lot. So the statement of the one who says: Abraham does not argue, giving the impression that the statement of the one who said in the interpretation of His statement: argues with us is that Abraham was arguing with his Lord, is an ignorant statement, and his argument with the messengers was in the form of disputing with them. The meaning of that is: And the good report came to him, and he argues with Our messengers, but when he knew what was meant by the statement, he omitted the messengers. His argument with them was as follows: Ibn Hamid narrated, Yaqub al-Qummi narrated, Ja`far narrated, on the authority of Sa`id: He argues with us about the people of Lot, he said: When Gabriel and those with him came, they said to Abraham: We will destroy the people of this town, for its people were wrongdoers! Abraham said to them: Will you destroy a town in which there are four hundred believers? They said: No! He said: Will you destroy a town in which there are three hundred believers? They said: No! He said: Will you destroy a town in which there are two hundred believers? They said: No! He said: Will you destroy a town in which there are forty believers? They said: No! He said: Will you destroy a town in which there are fourteen believers? They said: No! Abraham counted them as fourteen because of Lot’s wife, but he remained silent and felt at ease. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Al-Hammani told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The king said to Abraham: If there are five of them praying, the punishment will be lifted from them. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: He argues with us about the people of Lot, he mentioned to us that his argument with them was that he said to them: Tell me, if there are fifty believers among them, will you punish them? They said: No! Until it became ten. He said: Tell me, if there are ten among them, will you punish them? They said: No! And they are three villages, in which there is whatever God willed of great numbers and abundance. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: He argues with us about the people of Lot. He said: It has reached us that he said to them on that day: Tell me, what if there were fifty Muslims among them? They said: If there were fifty among them, we would not punish them! He said: Forty? They said: And forty! He said: Thirty? They said: And thirty! Until he reached ten. They said: And if there were ten among them! He said: What people do not have ten among them in whom there is goodness? Ibn Abd al-A'la said, Muhammad ibn Thawr said: Muammar said: It has reached us that there were four thousand people in the village of Lot, or whatever God willed of that. Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, So when the fear had departed from Abraham and the good tidings had come to him, he said: What is the matter with you, O messengers? They said: We have been sent to the people of Lot. So he argued with them about the people of Lot. He said: Tell me, if there are a hundred Muslims among them, will you destroy them? They said: No! He kept decreasing until he reached ten Muslims. They said: We will not punish them if there are ten Muslims among them. Then they said: O Abraham, turn away from this one. There is none among them except a household of believers, namely Lot and his household. This is the statement of God, the Most High: He argues with us about the people of Lot. The angels said: “O Abraham, turn away from this one. Indeed, the command of your Lord has come, and there will surely come upon them a punishment that cannot be averted.” Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: When the fear had left Abraham and the good report had come to him, meaning Abraham, he argued on behalf of the people of Lot to avert the punishment from them. He said: The people of the Torah claim that Abraham argued with them when he argued with them about the people of Lot to avert the punishment from them, and he only said to the messengers in what he was saying to them: Tell me, if there were a hundred believers among them, would you destroy them? They said: No! He said: What if there were ninety? They said: No! He said: What if there were eighty? They said: No! He said: What if there were seventy? They said: No! He said: What if there were sixty? They said: No! He said: What if there were fifty? They said: No! He said: What if there were one Muslim man? They said: No! He said: When they did not mention to Abraham that there was a single believer in it, he said: Indeed, in it is Lot, to ward off the punishment from them. “They said, ‘We know best who is in it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she was among those who remained behind.’” “O Abraham, turn away from this. Indeed, the command of your Lord has come, and indeed, there will come upon them a punishment that cannot be averted.” Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said, Ibrahim said: Will you destroy them if you find among them a hundred believers? Then ninety, until it went down to five. He said: And in the village of Lot there were four thousand thousand. Muhammad bin Auf told us, Abu Al-Mughira told us, Safwan told us, Al-Muthanna and Muslim Abu Al-Habil Al-Ashja’i told us: When the fear left Abraham, to the end of the verse, Abraham said: Will I torment a scholar of yours so much, among them a hundred men? He said: No, by My glory! Not even fifty. He said: Then forty? Thirty? Until he reached five, he said: No! By My glory, I will not torment them, even if there were five among them who worshipped Me! God the Almighty said: And We found therein not but one house of Muslims, meaning Lot and his two daughters. He said: So the torment came upon them. God the Almighty said: And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment. And He said: So when the fear left Abraham and the good report came to him, he argued with Us concerning the people of Lot. The Arabs hardly ever use the word lama when it is followed by a past verb except with a past tense. They say: lama qama he stood up, but they hardly ever say: lama qama he stood up. It may be permissible in cases where the verb has a long duration, such as argument, dispute, and fighting. They say in that case: lama maqaltuhu aqataluhu I began to fight him, meaning: I began to fight him. And His saying: Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, grieving, and turning back [to God], the Most High says: Indeed, Abraham was slow to anger, humble before his Lord, submissive to Him, obedient to His command, turning back, returning to His obedience, as: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid: O God, the penitent, he said: the obedient, the returner. We have previously explained the meaning of awwah according to the differences of opinion among those who differ, and the evidence for the correct opinion among us is that it is sufficient to make it unnecessary to repeat it.
11:76: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says, informing about the words of His messengers to Abraham: O Abraham, turn away from this, and that is what they said to him when he argued with them about the people of Lot, and they said: Stop arguing about their matter and disputing about it, for the command of your Lord has come, meaning: the command of your Lord has come to punish them. The word of punishment has come true upon them, and the decree of their destruction has been carried out against them, and there will come upon them a punishment that cannot be averted, meaning: And the people of Lot, a punishment from God will descend upon them that cannot be repelled. The narration has already been mentioned in what we mentioned about those who mentioned it about him.
11:77: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And when Our angels came to Lot, their coming grieved him - and it is an evil action, and he was distressed by them, by their coming, with great distress, meaning: his soul was distressed by their coming. That is because he did not know that they were messengers of God in the state in which their coming grieved him, and he knew what his people were like in committing immorality, and he feared for them, so he was distressed by their coming because of that, and he knew that he would need to defend his guests, and that is why he said: And he said, This is a difficult day. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed by them and was irritated by them, meaning: He had a bad opinion of his people and was irritated by his guests. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Hudhayfah, that he said: When the messengers came to Lot, they came to him while he was working a land of his, and it had been said to them - and God knows best - Do not destroy them until Lot bears witness. He said: So they came to him and said: We are your guests tonight. So he set off with them, and after walking for a while, he turned and said: Do you not know what the people of this town are doing? By God, I do not know of people on the face of the earth more wicked than them! He said: So he went with them, then he said the same thing a second time, and they set off with them. When his evil old wife saw them, she set off and warned them. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said, Hudhayfah said, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Hamid narrated, Al-Hakam bin Bashir narrated, Amr bin Qais Al-Mala’i narrated, on the authority of Saeed bin Bishr, on the authority of Qatada, who said: The angels came to Lot while he was on his farm, and God said to the angels: If Lot bears witness against them four times, then I have given you permission to destroy them. They said: O Lot, we want to host you tonight. He said: What has brought you their affair? They said: What is their affair? He said: I bear witness by God that it is the worst town on earth in terms of deeds! He said that four times, and Lot bore witness against them four times, and they entered his house with him. Musa bin Harun told me, Amr bin Hammad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: The angels left Abraham toward the village of Lot, and they came to it at noon. When they reached the River of Sodom, they met Lot's daughter drawing water for her family. He had two daughters: the name of the elder was Rathiya, and the younger was Zgharta. They said to her: O girl, is there a place to stay? She said: Yes, stay where you are, do not enter until I come to you! Some of her people were afraid of them. She went to her father and said: "O my father, young men want to see you at the gate of the city. I have never seen faces more beautiful than theirs. Do not let your people seize them and disgrace them!" His people had forbidden him to host a man, so they said: Leave us alone, so we can host men. So he brought them, and no one knew except the people of Lot's household. His wife went out and told her people, saying: In Lot's house there are men the likes of whose faces I have never seen! So his people came running to him. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: The messengers went out, as the people of the Torah claim, from Abraham to Lot at Al-Mu’tafikah. When the messengers came to Lot, he was upset with them and felt fed up with them, because his people feared that they would disgrace him in his guest, so he said: This is a difficult day! As for his saying: And he said, ‘This is a difficult day,’ he says: And Lot said: This day is a day of great evil and great affliction. It is said: The nerve of our day is nerved, and from it is the saying of Adi bin Zaid: I was your enemy's enemy, I did not turn back, and they took you on a difficult day. The rajaz poet said: A tough day that makes the heroes nervous, the strong ones nervous, the tall ones nervous And the other said: If you are not satisfied with Bakr bin Wael, you will have a difficult day in Iraq. Kaab bin Ja'il said: And those who are in the lowest depths, knowing that it will be a difficult day And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Asib means severe. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: This is a difficult day, meaning: severe. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: This is a difficult day, meaning: a day of calamity and hardship. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: A difficult day, meaning severe. Ali told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And he said, ‘This is a difficult day,’ meaning: a difficult day.
11:78: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: And Lot's people came to him, urging him on, trembling with the speed of their walking, because of their desire for immorality. It is said: A man trembled, from cold, anger or fever, if he thundered, and he is hurried if he is hasty and eager, as the rajaz poet said: With acceleration towards him, I rush And from it is the saying of Muhalhil: They came running, prisoners of their money, in spite of their noses. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: They rush to Him, he said: They run, which is to walk quickly. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid and Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: And his people came to him, rushing towards him, he said: They were running towards him. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: So they came to him, rushing to him, he said: quickly to him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: They rush to it, he said: They hasten to it. Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And his people came to him, running towards him, he said: They walked quickly towards him. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Yahya bin Zakariya told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And his people came to him, running to him, he said: running while walking. Sufyan said: rushing to him, they hastened to him. Suwar bin Abdullah told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah said, regarding his statement: They rush to it, he said: As if they were being pushed. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqoub told us, he said, Hafs Ibn Hamid told us, on the authority of Shammar Ibn Atiyah, he said: They came walking quickly, between running and jogging. Ali bin Dad told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: And his people came to him, rushing to him, he said: quickly. And his saying: And before that they used to do evil deeds, means: Before they came to Lot, they used to come to men from behind, as: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: And before that they used to do evil deeds, he said: They used to come to men. And His saying: He said, ‘O my people, these are my daughters,’ God Almighty says: Lot said to his people when they came to him to seduce him about his guest: O my people, these are my daughters - meaning the women of his nation - so marry them, for they are purer for you, as: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: These are my daughters, they are purer for you, he said: Lot ordered them to marry women, and he said: They are purer for you. Muhammad told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said: This was also conveyed to me on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: These are my daughters, they are purer for you. He said: They were not his daughters, but they were from his nation, and every prophet is the father of his nation. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: These are my daughters; they are purer for you, he said: He ordered them to marry women, and he did not offer them fornication. Yaqub told me, he said, Abu Bishr told us: I heard Ibn Abi Nujayh say regarding His statement: They are purer for you, he said: He did not offer them marriage or fornication. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: These are my daughters; they are purer for you, he said: He ordered them to marry women. And the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to protect his guests with his daughters. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa`d told us, he said, Abu Ja`far told us, on the authority of al-Rabi`, regarding his statement: These are my daughters; they are purer for you, meaning marriage. Abu Ja`far told me, on the authority of al-Rabi`, regarding his statement: These are my daughters; they are purer for you, meaning marriage. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Al-Nu’man A’rim told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, he said, Muhammad bin Shabib Al-Zahrani told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding the words of Lot: These are my daughters, they are purer for you, meaning: their women, they are his daughters, he is their prophet, and he said in some of the reading: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers, and he is a father to them. Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And his people came running to him, they said: Did we not forbid you from hosting people of knowledge? He said: These are my daughters; they are purer for you, if you are going to do something, is there not among you a man of sound mind? Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that he said: When the messengers came to Lot, his people rushed to him when they were informed of them. They claimed, and God knows best, that it was Lot’s wife who informed them of their whereabouts, and she said: Lot has guests whom I have never seen more beautiful or handsome than them! They used to approach men out of lust, rather than women, an indecency that no one in the world had ever committed before them. So when they came to him, they said: Did we not forbid you from the worlds? That is, did we not tell you: No one should come near you, for we will not find anyone with you except that we will commit an indecency with him? He said: O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you. So I would ransom my guest with them than you. And he did not invite them except to lawful marriage. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: These are my daughters, he said: the women. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: They are purer for you. The general reading of the Qur’an is with the nominative case: purer, so that they made her a noun and purer its predicate, as if it was said: My daughters are purer for you than what you want of immorality from men. It was mentioned on the authority of Isa bin Omar Al-Basri that he used to read it as: They are purer for you, with the accusative case of purer. Some Basra grammarians used to say: This does not happen. Rather, the predicate of a verb that cannot do without a predicate is placed in the accusative case if there are these implied nouns between the noun and the predicate. Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: Whoever puts it in the accusative case makes it an indefinite noun that is not definite, and his saying, hen, is a pillar for the verb, so he does not make it work. Another of them said: It is heard from the Arabs: This is Zayd himself specifically. He said: So he made it a predicate for this, like your saying: Abdullah himself was. He said: And the verb was not permissible to occur here, because approximation is a rejection of speech, so they did not come together, because they contradict each other, because that is reporting something familiar, and this is reporting the beginning of what it is in: Here I am, present or: Zayd is the scholar, so it is contradictory to include the known in the present, so it is not permissible. Abu Jaafar said: The reading that I do not seek refuge from in this is the nominative case: They are purer for you, because the proof of the readings of the regions agrees on it, despite its correctness in Arabic, and after the accusative case in it is correct. And His saying: So fear God and do not be disgraced in my guest, meaning: So fear God, O people, and beware of His punishment, for committing the immorality that you commit and seek. And do not be disgraced in my guest, meaning: Do not humiliate me, by doing to my guest what they would hate for you to do to them. The word guest is used in one expression in this context, meaning a group. The Arabs call both the singular and the plural guest with one expression, just as they said: a just man and a just people. And his saying: Is there not among you a man of sound mind? He says: Is there not among you a man of sound mind, who would forbid my guest from committing an immoral act, and stand between them and that? Like: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: “So fear God and do not disgrace me in my guest. Is there not among you a man of sound mind?” That is, a man who knows the truth and forbids evil?
11:79: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: The people of Lot said to Lot: You have certainly known, O Lot, that we have no right to your daughters, because they are not our wives, as: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: They said, ‘You know that we have no right to your daughters,’ meaning, to wives, and you know what we want. And his saying: Indeed, you know what we want, means that they said: And you, Lot, know that our need is not in your daughters, and that what we want is what you forbid us from. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And you know what we want, we want men. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: And indeed, you know what we want, meaning: our desire is for something other than that. So when they did not stop, and his words did not deter them, and they did not accept anything from him of what he offered them regarding the affairs of his daughters, he said: If only I had power over you, or could take refuge in a strong support.
11:80: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Lot said to his people, when they refused to do anything except go ahead with what they had come to him to ask for the immorality, and despaired of them responding to him with anything he had offered them: If only I had power over you, with supporters who would support me against you, and helpers who would assist me, or could take refuge in a strong support, meaning: or could join a forbidding clan that would protect me from you, I would come between you and what you came to want from me in my hospitality. The answer to if was omitted because the speech indicates it, and its meaning is understood. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, Lot said: If I had power over you or could take refuge in a strong support, meaning: in a strong paradise, I would fight you. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: Or I seek refuge in a strong support, he said: the clan. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: To a strong corner, he said: the clan. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Mubarak bin Fadala told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Or I seek refuge in a strong support, he said: in a support from the people. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: His statement: Or I seek refuge in a strong support, he said: It has reached us that no prophet was sent after Lot except in the wealth of his people, until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: If I had power over you, or could take refuge in a strong support, meaning: a clan that would protect me, or a group that would support me, I would stand between you and this. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: If only I had power over you or could take refuge in a strong support, he said: He means the clan. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that when this verse was revealed: If only I had power over you or could take refuge in a strong support, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God have mercy on Lot, he used to take refuge in a strong support! Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God have mercy on my brother Lot, he used to take refuge in a strong corner, so why did he submit to anything?! Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abda and Abd al-Rahim told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, he said, Abu Salamah told us, “On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God’s mercy be upon Lot, for he used to take refuge in a strong support, when he said to his al-Nas 114:‘If only I had power over you or could take refuge in a strong support.’ God did not send a prophet after him except that he was among the wealth of his people.” Muhammad said: Wealth means abundance and strength. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Katheer told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said, Abu Salamah told us, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Sulayman bin Bilal told me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abaan Al-Masry told me, he said, Saeed bin Talid told us, he said, Abdul Rahman bin Al-Qasim told us, he said, Bakr bin Mudar told me, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Yunus bin Yazid, on the authority of Ibn Shihab Al-Zuhri, he said, Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab told me, “on the authority of Abu Hurairah: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God have mercy on Lot, for he used to take refuge in a strong support!” Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman, and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned something similar. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding His statement: Or take refuge in a strong support, he took refuge in a strong support, meaning God Almighty. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God did not send a prophet after him except in the wealth of his people. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad bin Harb told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, “On the authority of Abu Yunus, he heard Abu Hurairah narrating, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: May God have mercy on Lot, for he used to take refuge in a strong support!” He said, Ibn Abi Maryam Saeed bin Abdul Hakam told us, he said, Abdul Rahman bin Abi Al-Zinad told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdul Rahman Al-Araj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: It was mentioned to us that whenever the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse - or came to this verse - he would say: May God have mercy on Lot, for he used to take refuge in a strong support! And he mentioned to us that God Almighty did not send a prophet after Lot, peace be upon him, except to a wealthy person from his people, until God sent your Prophet to a wealthy person from his people. It is said from I take refuge in a strong corner, I take refuge in you, so I take refuge in you, Oya, meaning: I came to you and joined you, as the rajaz poet said: He takes refuge in a corner of the corners in the number of the mud and the glory of Ban It was said: When Lot said this statement, the messengers found fault with him for that. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, he said, Abdul Samad told me: that he heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: Lot said: If only I had power over you or could take refuge in a strong support, so the messengers were angry with him and said: Your support is strong!
11:81: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: The angels said to Lot, when Lot said to his al-Nas 114:If only I had power over you, or could take refuge in a strong support, and they saw the distress he suffered because of them: O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord, sent to destroy them, and they will not reach you and your guest with harm, so make the matter easy for you, so set out with your family during a part of the night, meaning: so leave from among them, you and your family, during the remainder of the night. It is said: Asra and Sara, which means walking at night, And let none of you look back except your wife. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: So he went out. This was read by most of the Meccan and Medinan reciters: fasir, connected without the hamza of the alif, from sara. The majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra read it as: Fasra, with the letter alif, from Asra. Abu Jaafar said: My opinion on this matter is that they are two readings, and each of them has been read by people who are exemplary in reading. They are two well-known languages among the Arabs, and their meaning is the same. So whichever of them the reader reads, he is correct in that. As for his saying: Except your wife, most of the reciters from Hijaz and Kufa and some of the people of Basra read in the accusative case: Except your wife, with the interpretation: So travel with your family except your wife. And since Lot was commanded to travel with his family except his wife, he was forbidden to travel with her, and he was commanded to leave her behind with her people. Some Basrans read it as: Except your wife, in the nominative case - meaning: And let none of you turn back, except your wife - because Lot had taken her out with him, and he forbade Lot and those who were taken captive with him from turning back except his wife, and she turned back and was destroyed because of that. And His saying: That which befell them shall befall her, means: That which befell your wife shall befall your people of torment. Their appointed time is the morning, means: The appointed time for your people to perish is the morning. So Lot was slow to accept that from them and said to them: Rather, hasten their perishing! They said: Is not the morning near? That is, at morning the torment will descend upon them, as: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: Is not the dawn near? meaning: It will only descend upon them in the morning of this night of yours, so go on with what you are commanded. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Humayd narrated that Yaqub narrated from Ja`far from Sa`id that he said: The messengers went from Abraham to Lot. When they came to Lot, and what happened to them was what God mentioned, Gabriel said to Lot: O Lot, we are going to destroy the people of this city. Indeed, its people were wrongdoers! Lot said to them: Destroy them now! Gabriel said to him: “Their appointed time is the morning. Is not the morning near?” So the verse: Is not the morning near? was revealed to Lot. He said: So he ordered him to travel with his family during part of the night and not to look back among them except his wife. He said: So he traveled, and when the hour came in which they were to be destroyed, Gabriel put his wing in and raised it, until the people of the heaven heard the crowing of roosters and the barking of dogs. So he turned it upside down and rained down upon it stones of baked clay. He said: And Lot’s wife heard the rooster’s roar and said: Oh my people! Then a stone overtook her and killed her. Ibn Humayd narrated, saying, Yaqub narrated, on the authority of Hafs ibn Humayd, on the authority of Shammar ibn Atiyah, who said: Lot had taken a vow from his wife that she would not divulge any of the secrets of his guests. He said: When Gabriel and those with him entered upon him, she saw them in a form she had never seen before. So she set out running to her people. She came to the gathering and waved her hand like this! And they came running, walking at a trot, between jogging and running. When they reached Lot, Lot said to them what God had said in His Book. Gabriel said: O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you. He said: So he waved his hand, and blinded their eyes, and they began to seek them out, touching the walls, but they could not see. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: When the evil old woman, his wife, saw them - meaning the messengers - she went and warned them, and said: Lot has been visited by people, I have never seen people with more beautiful faces! - He said: I do not know him except that she said: Nor whiter and more fragrant! - He said: So they came to him, rushing to him, as God had said, and Lot slammed the door. He said: So they began to treat him. He said: Gabriel asked his Lord for permission to punish them, and He gave him permission, so he slammed them with his wing, and left them blind, wandering around in the most evil night that had ever come upon them. So they told him: Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord... So travel with your family during a part of the night. He said: It was mentioned to us that Lot's wife was with him when he left the village, then she heard the sound and turned around, and God sent a stone upon her and destroyed her. And his saying: “Their appointment is the morning. Is not the morning near?” So the Prophet of God wanted something more urgent than that, so they said: Is not the morning near? Ibn Humayd narrated that Al-Hakam ibn Bishr narrated that Amr ibn Qays Al-Mala’i narrated that Saeed ibn Bishr narrated that Qatada said: His wife - meaning Lot’s wife - went to her people when she saw them - meaning when she saw the messengers - and said: He was hosted tonight by people whose faces are more beautiful than any I have ever seen, nor whose scent is more pleasant! So they came running to him, and Lot rushed to them and crowded them to the door, and said: These are my daughters, if you will do so. They said: Did we not forbid you from the worlds? So they entered upon the angels, and the angels seized them and blinded their eyes, and they said: O Lot, you have brought to us a people who have bewitched us! Stay as you are until morning! Gabriel carried the four cities of Lot, in each city there were a hundred thousand, and he lifted them up on his wing between the sky and the earth, until the people of the lowest heaven heard the cries of their roosters, then he turned them over, and God turned the top of it upside down. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Hudhayfah said: When they entered upon him, his old woman, a bad old woman, went to her people and said: Lot has been hosted tonight by people whose faces are more beautiful than those of whom I have never seen! He said: So they came running, and he hastened them to Lot, and an angel stood up and blocked the door - he says: he blocked it - and asked Gabriel for permission to punish them, and he gave him permission. Gabriel struck them with his wing, and left them blind, and they spent the worst night. Then they said: We are messengers of your Lord... So set out with your family during a part of the night and let none of you look back except your wife. He said: We were informed that she heard a sound and turned around, and a stone hit her, and she was an oddity among the people and her location was known. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Hudhayfah, something similar, except that he said: So Lot hastened them. Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: When Lot said: If only I had power over you, or could take refuge in a strong support, then Gabriel, peace be upon him, spread his wings and gouged out their eyes, and they went out, trampling one another’s backs, blind, saying: Escape, escape! For in the house of Lot are the most sorcerers on earth! That is what His saying means: And they certainly sought to seduce him from his guest, but We blinded their eyes. And they said to Lot: Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you. So set out with your family during a part of the night and do not look back among you, except your wife, for indeed, she will be afflicted. And follow the backs of your family, he says: set out with them, and go where you are commanded. So God brought them out to Ash-Sham. And Lot said: Destroy them now! They said: We were not commanded except at dawn. Is not dawn near? When it was dawn, Lot and his family went out with him, except for his wife. This is what He said: (Except for the family of Lot. We saved them by dawn). Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, on the authority of Abdul Samad: that he heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: The people of Sodom, among whom were Lot, were a people who had dispensed with women by using men. When God saw that from them, He sent the angels to torment them. They came to Abraham, and his command and their command were as God mentioned in His Book. When they gave Sarah the good report of the child, they stood up and Abraham stood up walking with them. He said: Tell me, why have you been sent? And what is your business? They said: We were sent to the people of Sodom to destroy it, and they are an evil people who have dispensed with women by using men! Abraham said: What if there are fifty righteous men among them? They said: Then we will not torment them! He began to subtract until he said: A household? They said: What if there is a righteous household among them? He said: Lot and his household? They said: His wife, her passion is with them! When Abraham despaired, he turned away. They went to the people of Sodom and entered upon Lot. When his wife saw them, she was impressed by their beauty and handsomeness, so she sent word to the people of the town: A people have come to us, the likes of whom no people have ever been seen, more handsome or more beautiful! When they heard about this, they invaded Lot’s house from every side and climbed over the walls. Lot met them and said: “O my people, do not disgrace me in front of my guests. I will marry you to my daughters, for they are purer for you!” They said: If we had wanted your daughters, we would have known their place! He said: If only I had power over you, or could take refuge in a strong support! The messengers were angry with him and said: Your support is strong! And they will be afflicted with a punishment that cannot be averted!” Then one of them wiped their eyes with his wing, and their sight was blinded. They said: He has bewitched us! Let us turn away until we return to him! So what happened to them was what God, the Most High, has related in the Qur’an. Then Michael, the tormentor, entered his wing until he reached the bottom of the earth, and kissed it. Then stones came down from the sky and pursued those who were not from them in the village wherever they were. So God destroyed them, and saved Lot and his family except for his wife. Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, and on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah - and Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Muammar - on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Hudhayfah, some of their hadiths were mixed with each other. He said: Abraham, peace be upon him, would come to them and say: Woe to you, I forbid you from God to expose yourself to His punishment! But they did not obey, until the written term had come, due to the place of their torment and the wrath of the Lord over them. He said: The angels came to Lot while he was working in his land, so he invited them to hospitality, and they said: We are your hosts tonight! And God, the Most High, mentioned, had enjoined Gabriel, peace be upon him, that He would not torment them until Lot testified against them three times. So when Lot took them to hospitality, he mentioned the evil and great calamities that his people were doing, so he walked with them for a while, then he turned to them and said: Do you not know what the people of this town are doing? I do not know of anyone on the face of the earth who is worse than them! Where shall I take you? To my people, who are the worst of God’s creation! Gabriel turned to the angels and said: Remember, this is one! Then he walked for a while, and when he reached the middle of the village, he felt compassion for them and was shy of them, and said: Do you not know what the people of this village are doing? I do not know of anyone on the face of the earth who is worse than them. My people are the worst of God’s creation! Gabriel turned to the angels and said: Remember, these are two! When he reached the door of the house, he cried out of shame and compassion for them and said: My people are the worst of God’s creation. Do you not know what the people of this village are doing? I do not know of anyone on the face of the earth who is worse than them! Gabriel said to the angels: Remember, these are three, the punishment has come true! When they entered, the evil old woman went, climbed up and waved her garment, and the wicked came running to her. They said: What do you have? She said: The guests of Lot tonight are people I have never seen more beautiful faces or a better scent than them! So they rushed to the door, and Lot rushed at the door, and they pushed him away for a long time, he inside and they outside, imploring God and saying: These are my daughters; they are purer for you! Then the angel stood up and blocked the door - he said: he blocked it - and asked Gabriel's permission to punish them, and God gave him permission. So he stood up in the form in which he is in heaven, and spread his wing - and Gabriel has two wings, and he was wearing a scarf of strung pearls, and his front teeth were shining, his forehead was prominent, and his head was like coral, which is pearls, like snow, and his feet were green - and he said: O Lot, Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you. Come out, O Lot, from the door and leave me and them. So Lot stepped away from the door, and went out to them, and spread his wing, and struck their faces with it a blow that blinded them, so they became blind, not knowing the way, nor finding their way to their homes. Then he ordered Lot to set out with his family during the night. He said: So set out with your family during a part of the night. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that he said: When Lot said to his al-Nas 114:If only I had power over you, or could take refuge in some strong support, the messengers heard what he was saying and what was being said to him, and they saw the distress he was in. So when they saw what he had heard, they said: O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you, meaning: with anything you would dislike, “so set out with your family during a part of the night and let not anyone of you look back, except your wife. Indeed, what has befallen them will strike her. Indeed, their appointed time is the morning. Is not the morning near?” meaning: The punishment will only descend upon them in the morning of this night of yours, so go as you are commanded. He said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi: that he narrated: that the messengers then slapped the faces of those of his people who had come to Lot to seduce him about his guest, so they returned blind. He said: God says: And indeed they had seduce him about his guest, but We blinded their eyes. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: in parts of the night, he said: in a part of the night. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: In parts of the night, in a part of the night. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said, his statement: In parts of the night, he said: the middle of the night, and his statement: and follow their backs, he said: and follow the backs of your family, and let none of you turn back. Mujahid used to say about this: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And let none of you look back, he said: let none look behind him, except your wife. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud that he used to recite: So set out with your family during a part of the night, except for your wife. Ahmad bin Yusuf told me that, he said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, he said: In the letter of Ibn Masoud: So set out with your family during a part of the night, except for your wife. Abu Jaafar said: This indicates the correctness of reading in the accusative case.
11:82: God Almighty says: So when Our command came, We turned it upside down and rained down upon it stones of hard clay, one after the other.
11:83: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And when Our command to punish came, and Our judgment concerning them was to destroy them, We turned its upper part meaning: the upper part of their village: its lower part, and We rained upon it meaning: and We sent upon it, stones of baked clay. The interpreters differed about the meaning of Sijjil. Some of them said: In Persian it is: Sanak, and Kal. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: of baked clay, in Persian, the first letter is stone and the last letter is clay. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr: Stones of baked clay, he said: Persian, Arabized, tooth and all. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Sijjil is clay. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and Ikrimah: Of baked clay, they said: Of clay. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, he said, Abdul Samad told me, on the authority of Wahb, he said: Sijil in Persian means: tooth, and everything. Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Stones of baked clay. As for baked clay, Ibn Abbas said: In Persian it is sanak and jal. Sanak means stone and jal means clay. He says: We sent upon them stones of clay. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Stones of baked clay, he said: Clay in stones. Ibn Zayd said about this: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: stones of baked clay, he said: the lowest heaven. He said: and the lowest heaven’s name is Sijjil, and it is the one that God sent down upon the people of Lot. Some of the scholars of the Arabic language from Basra used to say: Sajjil is a hard, strong stone, and it is a type of beating. He used as evidence for that the words of the poet: A strike that heroes recommend to be recorded He said: Some of them change the letter lam to nun. Another of them said: It is a noun of action, from the saying of the speaker: I registered it, I sent it, so it is as if it is from that, meaning: sent to them.
