Another of them said: Rather, it is someone for whom I recorded a record of giving, as if it was said: They erased that affliction and gave it to him. And they said: I recorded it, I neglected it. Some of them said: It is from the register, because it contained knowledge like a book. Another of them said: Rather, it is clay that is cooked like bricks, and he recited the verse of Al-Fadl Ibn Abbas: Whoever debates with me debates with a noble man who fills the bucket to the limit of distress So, if you record a record for him, give it to him. Abu Jaafar said: The correct statement regarding this, according to us, is what the commentators said, which is that they are stones of clay, and God described them in this way in His Book in one place, and that is His saying: (That We may send upon them stones of clay, marked from your Lord for the transgressors). It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that he used to say: It is Persian and Nabataean. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: Persian and Nabataean, Saj, Ail. Saeed bin Jubair went on to say that the name of clay in Persian is Jal, not Il, and that if it were in Persian it would be Sajil, not Sajil, because stone in Persian is called Saj, and clay is Jal, so there is no reason for the Ya’ in it, which is Persian. Abu Jaafar said: We have explained the correct statement in our opinion at the beginning of the book, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. It was reported on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he said: The origin of the stones was clay, then they were strengthened. As for his saying: arranged, Qatada and Ikrimah say about it what: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and Ikrimah: Arranged, he says: arranged. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Arranged, he says: arranged. And Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said about it what: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas, regarding his statement: arranged, he said: Arranged some of it next to some. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali Ibn Abdullah: As for his saying: arranged, it is arranged and prepared in the sky, and it is from the provisions that God has prepared for the darkness. Some of them said: In order, one after the other upon them. He said: That is its order. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement about this is what Al-Rabi` bin Anas said, and that is that his saying, arranged, is a description of sijjil, not a description of stones. Rather, the people were rained down with stones of clay. The description of that clay is that it was arranged one on top of the other, so it became stones. They did not rain down clay, so it was described as coming one after the other upon the people. Abu Jaafar said: It would have been permissible for it to be as this interpreter interpreted it, if the revelation had been in the accusative case, in which case it would have been a description of the stones. As for his saying: Marked with your Lord, he is saying: Marked with God, God taught it, and marked is a description of stones, and therefore it is in the accusative case as a description. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Marked, he said: marked. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Jurayj said: Marked, it does not resemble the stones of the earth. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and Ikrimah: Marked, they said: It has a collar, and it has a reddish tinge. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Marked, it has a known mark. Some of those who saw it said that it is a ringed stone, on it - or: in it - a tinge of redness, not like your stones. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, regarding his statement: marked, he said: It has lines marked on it. Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Marked, he said: Marked is the sealed. As for his saying: And it is not far from the wrongdoers, then God Almighty says, threatening the polytheists of Quraysh 106:And these stones that you rained down on the people of Lot are not far from the polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, if they do not repent from their polytheism. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Atab Al-Dallal Sahl bin Hammad told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, he said, Aban bin Taghlib told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And it is not far from the wrongdoers, he said: That what happened to the people will happen to them. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And it is not far from the wrongdoers, he said: He terrifies with it whomever He wills. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And it is not far from the wrongdoers, meaning: God did not protect any wrongdoer from it after the people of Lot. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and Ikrimah: And it is not far from the wrongdoers, meaning: He did not leave any wrongdoer after them. Ali bin Sahl told us, Damrah bin Rabi’ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Shawdhab, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And it is not far from the wrongdoers, he said: He means the wrongdoers of this nation. He said: By God, I have not protected a wrongdoer from it yet! Musa bin Harun told us, Hammad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And it is not far from the wrongdoers, meaning: from the wrongdoers of the Arabs, if they do not repent, then they will be punished with it. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali Ibn Abdullah, who said: He says: And it is not far from the wrongdoers, from the wrongdoers of your nation, so no wrongdoer will feel safe from them. The heart of the angels was high and low in the land of Sodom, as: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, took the people of Lot from their pastures and homes, and carried them with their livestock and their belongings, until the people of heaven heard the barking of their dogs, then he turned them over. Abu Kuraib told us about it again, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Gabriel entered his wing under the lower ground of the people of Lot, then he took them with the right wing and took them from their livestock and cattle, then he raised them up. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: He used to say: So when Our command came, We turned it upside down. He said: When they woke up, Gabriel came to their village and tore it apart from its corners, then he put his wing in, then he carried it on the tips of his wings. He said, Shabl told us, he said, Ibn Abi Nujayh told me this, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Abi Bakr - he said: Ibn Abi Nujayh did not hear it, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: So he carried it on the wings of his wings with what was in it, then he ascended with it to the sky, until the people of the sky heard the barking of their dogs, then he turned it over. The first thing to fall was its top. That is what God said: And We turned it upside down and rained down upon it stones of baked clay. Mujahid said: So no people were afflicted with what afflicted them, for God blinded their eyes, then He turned their city over, and rained down upon them stones of baked clay. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said: It has reached us that Gabriel, peace be upon him, took hold of the middle handle of the village, then he turned it towards the sky, until the people of the sky heard the roaring of their dogs, then he destroyed some of it on top of others, turning its top into its bottom, then he followed them with stones. Qatada said: It has reached us that they were four thousand thousand. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that Gabriel, peace be upon him, took hold of its middle handle, then he twisted it into the atmosphere of the sky, until the angels heard the howls of their dogs, then he destroyed some of them on top of each other, then Shadhan of the people followed Sakhr. He said: They are three villages called Sodom, and they are between Medina and Ash-Sham. He said: It was mentioned to us that there were four million in it. It was mentioned to us that Abraham, peace be upon him, used to look out and say: Sodom, the day of Malik! Musa told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: When they, meaning the people of Lot, woke up in the morning, Gabriel descended and uprooted the earth from seven earths, and carried it until he reached the lowest heaven, until the people of heaven heard the barking of their dogs and the crows of their roosters, then he turned it upside down and killed them. That is when he says: And the overturned I have cast down, the overturned, when Gabriel caused the earth to fall with it and uprooted it with his wing. Whoever did not die when he caused the earth to fall, God rained stones upon him while he was under the earth, and whoever of them was scattered in the earth. This is the saying of God: And We turned it upside down and rained upon it stones of baked clay. Then He pursued them in the villages, and a man would speak and a stone would come to him and kill him. This is the saying of God Almighty: And We rained upon it stones of baked clay. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Abu Bakr and Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said: It has reached us that when Gabriel, peace be upon him, woke up, he spread his wing and blew up their land with it, including its palaces, animals, stones, trees, and everything in it. He gathered it in his wing, rolled it up and folded it in the interior of his wing, then he ascended with it to the lowest heaven, until the inhabitants of the heaven heard the voices of people and dogs, and they were four thousand thousand. Then he turned it over and sent it to the earth upside down, some of it rumbling against others, making its top its bottom, then he followed it with stones of baked clay. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, he said: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi narrated to me, he said: “I was told that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God sent Gabriel, peace be upon him, to the ruined city, the city of Lot, peace be upon him, in which Lot was. He carried it with his wing, then ascended with it until the people of the lowest heaven could hear the barking of its dogs and the clucking of its chickens. Then he turned it over on its face, then God followed it with stones. God says: ‘We turned it upside down and rained upon it stones of baked clay.’ So God destroyed it and the ruined cities around it, and there were five cities: San’a, Sa’wa, Athara, Douma, and Sodom - and Sodom is the largest city - and God saved Lot and those of his family with him, except for his wife, who was among those who perished.”
11:84: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And We sent to the children of Madyan their brother Shu`ayb, and when he came to them he said: O my people, worship God; you have no god other than Him, meaning: Obey Him, and humble yourselves before Him by obeying what He has commanded you to do and what He has forbidden you to do. You have no god other than Him, meaning: You have no deity other than Him who deserves your worship other than Him. And do not reduce the measure and the weight, meaning: Do not reduce the rights of people in your measure and your weight. Indeed, I see you in goodness. The people of interpretation differed about the good that God told about Shuaib, that he said to Madyan that he saw them through him. Some of them said: That was because the price was cheap, and they were afraid of its high price. Who said that? Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me, he said, Abdullah bin Dawud al-Wasiti told us, he said, Muhammad bin Musa told us, on the authority of al-Dhiyal bin Amr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed, I see you in good health, he said: low prices, Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an encompassing Day, he said: high prices. Ahmad bin Amr Al-Basri told me, he said, Abd Al-Samad bin Abd Al-Warith told me, he said, Saleh bin Rustum told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, and he mentioned the people of Shu`ayb, he said: I see you in good health, he said: The price has decreased. Muhammad bin Amr bin Ali told me, he said, Abd al-Samad bin Abd al-Warith told us, on the authority of Abu Amir al-Kharraz, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement: Indeed, I see you in good health, he said: Wealth and cheap prices. Others said: What he meant by that is: I see for you wealth and adornment from the adornments of this world. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Indeed, I see you in goodness, he said: He means the goodness of this world and its adornment. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: I see you in goodness, he saw on them a shell of the shell of the world and its adornments. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: Indeed, I see you in goodness, he said: In your worldly life, as God Almighty said: (If he leaves behind goodness), he called it goodness, because people call wealth goodness. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is what God has reported about Shu`ayb that he said to his people, and that is His saying: Indeed, I see you in goodness, meaning: in the goodness of this world. And the goodness of this world may include wealth, the adornments of worldly life, and cheap prices, and there is no evidence that he meant by his saying that some of the goodness of this world and not others, for that is according to all the meanings of the goodness of this world that the people of knowledge have mentioned that they were given. Shu`ayb said that because his people were living comfortably, their prices were cheap, and their wealth was plentiful. So he said to them: “Do not reduce people’s rights in your measures and scales, for God has increased your provision for you. “And I fear for you,” because of your disobeying God’s command, and reducing people’s wealth in your measures and scales, the punishment of an encompassing Day. He said: That the punishment of a Day will befall you, its punishment encompassing you. So he made encompassing a description of the Day, and it is a description of the punishment, since its meaning was understood, and the punishment was on the Day, so it became like their saying: Some of your garment is burnt.
11:85: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says, informing about what Shu`ayb said to his al-Nas 114:Give people full measure and weight, justly, meaning: with justice, and that is by giving those who have rights that are measured or weighed their rights, in full, without any shortcoming or deficiency. And his saying: And do not deprive people of their things, means: Do not deprive people of their rights that you must give them by measure, weight, or otherwise, such as: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Ali bin Saleh bin Hayy told us, he said: It reached me regarding his statement: And do not deprive people of their due rights, he said: Do not deprive them. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And do not deprive people of their due rights, meaning: Do not wrong people in their due rights. And His saying: And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption, means: Do not travel on the earth committing acts of disobedience to God, as: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated that Abd al-Razzaq told us that Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption, he said: Do not walk on the earth. And it was narrated on the authority of Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption, meaning: Do not strive to spread corruption on the earth, meaning: reducing the measure and the weight.
11:86: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty means by His statement: What remains from God is better for you, that what God has left for you, after you have given people their rights by measure and weight in justice, and He has made it lawful for you, is better for you than what remains for you by depriving people of their rights by measure and weight, if you are believers, meaning: if you believe in God’s promise and threat, and what He has made lawful and unlawful. This is a statement narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas with a chain of transmission that is not acceptable to the people of transmission. The interpreters differed on this. Some of them said that it means: Obeying God is better for you. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: What remains with God is better for you, he said: Obedience to God is better for you. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid: The remainder of God, he said: Obedience to God is better for you. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: The remainder of God, he said: Obedience to God. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: What remains with God is better for you, he said: Obedience to God is better for you. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: What remains of God is better for you, he said: Obedience to God. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Others said: The meaning of this is: Your portion from your Lord is better for you. Who said that? Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: What remains with God is better for you if you are believers, your portion from your Lord is better for you. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: What remains from God is better for you, he said: Your portion from God is better for you. Others said: It means: God’s provision is better for you. Who said that? Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of someone who mentioned it, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The remainder of God, he said: God’s provision. Ibn Zayd said about this: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: What remains from God is better for you if you are believers, he said: Destruction, in torment, and what remains, in mercy. Abu Ja`far said: I have chosen the interpretation of that statement that I have chosen, because God Almighty mentioned it before them with the prohibition against defrauding people of their things in measure and weight, and to abandon defrauding in measure and defrauding in weight Shu`ayb called them, so following that up with the report of what they have of a share in fulfillment in this world and the hereafter is more appropriate, even though his saying: a remainder is only a source from the saying of the speaker: a remainder of such-and-such remains, so there is no way to direct the meaning of that except to: the remainder of God that He left for you, from what you have after you fulfill the people’s rights, is better for you than your remainder of what is forbidden, which remains for you from your oppression of people, by your defrauding them in measure and weight. And His statement: And I am not a guardian over you, means: And I am not a watcher over you, O people, watching you when you measure and weigh. Do you give people their rights or do you wrong them? My duty is only to convey to you the message of my Lord, and I have conveyed it to you.
11:87: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: The people of Shu`ayb said: O Shu`ayb, do your prayers command you that we should abandon the worship of what our fathers worshipped of idols and statues, or that we should do with our wealth as we please, such as breaking and cutting up dirhams, and cheating people in measure and weight, Indeed, you are the Forbearing, which is the one who is not driven by anger to do what he would not do when he was pleased, the Rightly-Guided, meaning the Rightly-Guided in his command to them to abandon the worship of idols, as: Mahmoud bin Khidash told us, he said, Hammad bin Khalid Al-Khayyat told us, he said, Dawud bin Qais told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, regarding the statement of God: Does your prayer command you that we should leave what our fathers worshipped or that we should do with our wealth as we please? Indeed, you are the Forbearing, the Rightly-Guided, he said: Among what he forbade them from was deleting the dirhams, or he said: cutting off the dirhams, the doubt is from Hammad. Sahl bin Musa Al-Razi told us, he said, Ibn Abi Fadik told us, on the authority of Abu Mawdud, he said: I heard Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi say: It has reached me that the people of Shu’ayb were punished for cutting off dirhams. I found that in the Qur’an: Your prayer commands you that we should leave what our fathers worshipped or do with our wealth as we wish. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zaid bin Habbab told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, he said: The people of Shu’aib were punished for cutting off the dirhams, so they said: O Shu’aib, does your prayer command you to abandon what our fathers worshipped or to do with our money as we wish? He said, Hammad bin Khalid Al-Khayyat told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Qais, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, regarding his statement: Or that we do with our wealth what we will, he said: Among the things he forbade them from doing was deleting the dirhams. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: “They said, ‘O Shu’aib, does your prayer command you that we should abandon what our fathers worshipped or that we should do with our wealth as we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided.’” He said: He forbade them from cutting up the dinars and dirhams, so they said: They are our wealth, we do with them as we please. If we wish, we cut them up, if we wish, we alter them, and if we wish, we throw them away! He said, and Ibn Wahb told us, and Dawud bin Qais al-Mari told me: that he heard Zaid bin Aslam say about the statement of God: They said, O Shu`ayb, does your prayer command you that we should abandon what our fathers worshipped or that we should do with our wealth as we wish? Zabad said: Among that was cutting off their land. And his saying: Your prayers, Al-A’mash used to say in its interpretation, what: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, regarding his statement: your prayers, he said: your recitation. If someone says: How was it said: Your prayers command you to abandon what our fathers worshipped or to do with our money as we wish, when Shu`ayb only forbade them from doing with their money what you mentioned that he forbade them from doing with it? It was said: The meaning of this is different from what you imagined. The Arab scholars differed about the meaning of this. Some of the Basrans said: The meaning of this is: Your prayers command you to abandon what our fathers worshipped or to abandon doing what we want with our money. It does not mean: They command you to do what we want with our money, because this is not their command. Some of the Kufians said something similar to this statement. He said: There is another interpretation of it, which makes the command like the prohibition, as if he said: Do your prayers command you to do this, and forbid us from that? So it is then rejected because the first is accusative by his saying: command you, and that the second is accusative in apposition to what in his saying: what is worshipped. If that is the case, the meaning of the statement is: Do your prayers command you to leave what our fathers worshipped, or to leave doing with our money as we wish. It was mentioned that some of the reciters read it as: Whatever we wish. Abu Jaafar said: Whoever reads it in this way, there is no difficulty in it, and the second an is then connected to the first an. As for his saying to Shu`ayb: Indeed, you are the forbearing, the wise, they are the enemies of God. They said that to him in mockery of him, and they only made him foolish and ignorant with these words. And what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided. He said: They are mocking. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided, the mockers mock: Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided!
11:88: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Shu`ayb said to his al-Nas 114:O my people, have you seen if I have a clear and evident proof from my Lord regarding what I call you to of worshipping God, and disavowing the worship of idols and statues, and regarding what I forbid you from of corrupting wealth, and He has provided me from it a good provision, meaning: lawful and good, and I do not want to go against you in what I forbid you from, meaning: and I do not want to forbid you from a matter, then do the opposite of it, rather I do not do it except what I command you to do, and I do not refrain except from what I forbid you from, as: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And I do not want to go against you in what I forbid you from, he says: I did not forbid you from something that I do or do. I only desire reform, meaning: I do not desire, in what I command you to do and what I forbid you from, except your reform and the reform of your affairs, as much as I am able, meaning: as much as I am able to reform, lest a severe punishment befall you from God, for you have disobeyed His command and His Messenger. And my success is only through God, meaning: And I have not attained the truth in my attempt to reform you and your affairs except through God, for He is the One who helps me in that, unless he means that I have not attained the truth in it. And his saying: I have put my trust in Him, means: I entrust my affair to God, for He is my trust in me, and I rely on Him in my affair. And his saying: And to Him I turn, and to Him I turn in obedience, and return in repentance, as: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And to Him I turn, he said: I return. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said -... and Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And to Him I turn, he said: I return. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And to Him I turn, he said: I return.
11:89: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says, informing about what Shu`ayb said to his al-Nas 114:And O my people, let not my dissension incite you, meaning: Do not let my enmity and hatred, and the departure from the religion that I am upon, lead you to persist in what you are upon of disbelief in God, worshipping idols, cheating people in measure and weight, and abandoning repentance and repentance, lest you be afflicted with the like of what afflicted the people of Noah, of drowning, or the people of Hud, of torment, or the people of Salih, of the earthquake, and the people of Lot, whom the earth was shaken with, are not far from you, their destruction, so will you not learn from it and take heed? He says: So take heed from these people and beware that my dissension afflicts you with the like of what afflicted them, as: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Let not my dissension prevent you, meaning: let not my separation cause you to become afflicted with the like of that which afflicted the people of Noah, the verse. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Let not my dissent lead you to sin, he said: Let not my dissent lead you to sin. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: Let not my dissension cause you to sin, he said: My enmity, hatred, and separation. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, And the people of Lot are not far from you, he said: They were only a recent story from them, meaning the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, and Salih. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And the people of Lot are not far from you, he said: They were only recent arrivals, after Noah and Thamud. Abu Jaafar said: It may be possible to say that its meaning is: The people of Lot are not far from you.
11:90: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says, informing about what Shu`ayb said to his al-Nas 114:Ask forgiveness of your Lord, O people, for your sins between you and your Lord, which you are committed to, from worshipping gods and idols, and depriving people of their rights in the scales and weights, then repent to Him, meaning: then return to obeying Him and abiding by His commands and prohibitions, Indeed, my Lord is Merciful, meaning: He is Merciful to whoever repents and turns to Him, that He does not punish him after repentance, Loving, meaning: He has love for whoever turns and turns to Him, He loves him and loves him.
11:91: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: The people of Shu`ayb said to Shu`ayb: O Shu`ayb, we do not understand much of what you say, meaning: We do not know the truth of much of what you say and tell us, and we see you weak among us. He mentioned that he was blind, so they said to him, We see you as weak among us. Who said that? Abdul-A’la bin Wasil told me, he said, Asad bin Zaid Al-Jassas told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: And indeed, we see you among us weak, he said: He was blind. Abbas bin Abi Talib told us, Ibrahim bin Mahdi Al-Masisi told us, Khalaf bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Saeed, the same. Ahmad bin Al-Walid Al-Ramli told us, he said, Ibrahim bin Ziyad, Ishaq bin Al-Mundhir, and Abdul Malik bin Yazid told us, they said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed, similarly. He said, Amr bin Awn and Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, they said, we heard Sharik say about his statement: And indeed, we see you among us weak, he said: Blind. Sa’dawayh told us, he said, ‘Ibad told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubair, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, regarding his statement: And indeed, we see you among us as weak, he said: He had weak eyesight. Sufyan said: And he was called: The orator of the prophets. He said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed: And indeed, we see you weak among us, he said: He was blind. And his saying: And had it not been for your people, we would have stoned you, he says: They say: And had it not been for you being among your people and clan, we would have stoned you, meaning: We would have cursed you. Some of them said: It means: We would have killed you. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: And had it not been for your people, we would have stoned you, he said: They said: Had it not been for the fact that we fear your people and your people, we would have stoned you. His saying: And you are not dear to us, means: You are not one of those who are honored by us, so that his humiliation and disgrace would be great for us, rather that is easy for us.
11:92: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Shu`ayb said to his al-Nas 114:O my people, you have supported your people, so they are more powerful than God, and you have belittled your Lord, so you have put Him behind your backs, not obeying His command, nor fearing His punishment, nor glorifying Him as He should be glorified? It is said of a man, if he does not fulfill another man’s need: He threw his need behind his back, meaning he left it without paying attention to it. And if he fulfills it, it is said: He put it in front of him, and set his eyes on it, and said: I appeared with my need, and made it behind your back, meaning behind your back, as the poet said: We found the Banu Barasa from the descendants of Al-Dhahr Meaning that they appear to be concerned with people’s needs, but they do not pay attention to them. The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: He said, ‘O my people, is my family more honorable to you than God, and you have taken Him behind your backs?’ That is because the people of Shu’aib and his family were more honorable to them than God, and God’s status was insignificant to them, may our Lord be glorified and exalted. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And you took it behind you, behind your backs, he said: behind. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: O my people, is my family more honorable to you than God, and you have taken Him behind you as a back, meaning: You have honored your people, and you have shown your Lord. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And you took him behind your backs, he said: You did not observe him in anything, rather you observed my people. And you took him behind your backs, he said: You supported your people, and you showed your Lord. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And you took him behind your backs, he said: You did not watch him in anything, you only watched my people, And you took him behind your backs, you did not fear him. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Is my family more honorable to you than God? He said: You have honored your people and been deceived by your Lord. I heard Ishaq bin Abi Isra’il say: Sufyan said: And you have taken it behind your backs, as a man says to another: I have left my need behind you. And you have taken it behind your backs, you have taken his matter lightly. So when a man wants to fulfill the need of his companion, he places it in front of him, in front of him, and does not take it lightly. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And you have taken it behind you, as a back, he said, “The back is the surplus, like the camels that go out with him with the back camels, surplus, he does not load anything on them, unless he needs them. He said: Then he says: Your Lord is with you like this, if you need Him. And if you do not need Him, then He is nothing.” Others said: The meaning of this is: And you took what Shu`ayb brought behind you, so the ha’ in his statement: And you took it, according to this, is from the mention of what Shu`ayb brought. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And you took it behind you, as a back, he said: You left what Shu’ayb brought. He said, Jaafar bin Awn told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: They rejected his command. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid: And you took it behind you, as a back, he said: You abandoned his command. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And you took it behind your backs, he said, they are the people of Shu’ayb, by leaving what he brought behind their backs, behind them. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said... and Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And you took it behind your backs, he said: Their exception was the people of Shu’ayb, and their leaving what Shu’ayb had brought behind their backs, behind their backs. Abu Ja`far said: We chose the statement that we chose in interpreting that, because his statement, And you took it behind you, is close to his statement, Is my family more precious to you than God? So the ha in his statement, And you took it, was more appropriate and more fitting, as it was from the mention of God, because of its close proximity to Him. And His saying: Indeed, my Lord encompasses what you do, means: My Lord encompasses in His knowledge what you do, and nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for all of it, sooner or later. The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “And O my people, work according to your position. Indeed, I am working. You will soon know.” Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says, informing about what Shuaib said to his al-Nas 114:And O my people, work according to your position, meaning: according to your ability. It is said: The man works according to his ability and his ability, meaning: according to his ability, and the man is enabled, enabled, and positioned. Some of the interpreters said about the meaning of his saying: on your positions, “on your homes.” Abu Ja`far said: The meaning of the statement then is: O people, work to enable you to do the work that you do. I am working slowly from the knowledge that I do. You will know, which of us is the one who has wronged himself, who has erred in his actions, and who is correct in his actions and who has done good to himself.
11:93: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says, informing about what His Prophet Shu`ayb said to his al-Nas 114:What will come to him from us and from you, O people, is a punishment that will disgrace him, meaning: it will humiliate and degrade him, and whoever is a liar, meaning: it will also disgrace whoever is a liar in what he says and reports from us and from you, and watch, meaning: wait and check, from the neck. It is said: I watched someone, I watch him. And his saying: I am with you, watching, means: I am also the one who is responsible for that punishment with you, and I am watching it, with whoever is descending from us and from you.
11:94: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: When Our judgment came to the people of Shu'ayb, with Our punishment, We saved Shu'ayb, Our Messenger, and those who believed in him and confirmed what he brought to them from their Lord, with Shu'ayb from Our punishment that We sent upon his people, by a mercy from Us, for him and for those who believed in him and followed him in what he brought to them from their Lord. And a blast from the sky seized those who did wrong, extinguishing them and destroying them for their disbelief in their Lord. It was said that Gabriel, peace be upon him, shouted at them a blast that took their souls from their bodies, and they became in their homes prostrate, on their knees, and fallen in their courtyards.
11:95: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: It is as if the people of Shuaib, whom God destroyed with His punishment, had never lived when they became crouched in their homes before that, and they had not sufficed. From their saying: I sang in such and such a place, if I stayed there, and from it is the saying of Al-Nabigha: I sang about that when they were my neighbors, they sent me a letter of affection and courtesy. And as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: As if they had never lived therein, he said: He says: As if they had never lived therein. Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. And His statement: Away with Madyan, as Thamud was removed, God Almighty says: May God distance Madyan from His mercy, by bringing down His vengeance upon them, as Thamud was removed, meaning: as He distanced Thamud before them from His mercy, by bringing down His wrath upon them.
11:96: God Almighty says: And We sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority.
11:97: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And We sent Moses with Our proofs of Our Oneness, and a proof that is clear to whoever sees it and ponders it with a sound heart, that it indicates the Oneness of God, and the falsity of everyone who claims divinity without Him, and the lengthy statement of those who associate others with Him in divinity, to Pharaoh and his chiefs, meaning: to the nobles of his army and his followers, and they followed the command of Pharaoh, he says: So Pharaoh and his chiefs denied Moses, and denied the Oneness of God, and refused to accept what Moses brought them from God, and the chiefs of Pharaoh followed the command of God without God, and obeyed him in denying Moses, and rejecting what he brought them from God upon him, God Almighty says: And Pharaoh's command was not right, meaning: that Pharaoh's command before him, in denying Moses, does not guide him to good, nor does it direct him to righteousness, rather it leads him to the fire of Hell.
11:98: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Pharaoh will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection, leading them and going with them to the Fire until he brings them into it and roasts them in its blazing heat. And what an evil place it is, meaning: What an evil place they will be brought to. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection, he said: Pharaoh, he will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection, he will go before them, until he rushes with them into the Fire. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection, meaning: he will lead his people, and he will lead them into the Fire. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said, regarding his statement: He will lead his people forward on the Day of Resurrection, he means: He led them astray and led them to the Fire. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of someone who heard Ibn Abbas say regarding His statement: Then He will lead them into the Fire, he said: The entry means entering. Al-Husayn narrated, he said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement: And He will lead them into the Fire, Ibn Abbas used to say: The mention in the Qur’an is four: In Hud, His statement: What an evil destination is that which is led into, and in Maryam, And there is not one of you but will pass over it, and in Al-Anbiya, it is mentioned: Firewood of Hell, you will pass over it, and in Maryam also it is mentioned: And We will drive the criminals to Hell in droves. Ibn Abbas used to say: All of these entrances. By God, every righteous and wicked person will pass over Hell: Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees.
11:99: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And God pursued them in this - meaning in this world - with the punishment that He hastened for them in it, of drowning in the sea, His curse, and on the Day of Resurrection, meaning: And on the Day of Resurrection they will also be cursed with another curse, such as: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid: And they will be pursued in this and on the Day of Resurrection, he said: Another curse. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And they will be followed in this with a curse and on the Day of Resurrection, he said: Add to his curse another curse, so those are two curses. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And they will be followed in this by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection, what an evil provision it will be. A curse follows a curse. He said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And they will be pursued in this and on the Day of Resurrection, he said: They will be followed by another curse, so those are two curses. His saying: What a bad support, means: What a bad helper, the curse added to it is another like it. The origin of rafd is help. It is said from it: rafd so-and-so with the prince yarafdhu rafdan with a kasra on the ra. If it is opened, it means drinking from a large cup. rafd is a huge cup. From it is the saying of Al-A’sha: May God provide for his blood that day and take captives from the fighting crowd. It is said: So-and-so supported his wall, meaning he propped it up with a piece of wood so that it would not fall. Rafd, with the first letter ra pronounced with a fat-ha, is the verbal noun. It is said: Rafda yarfuduhu rafdan, and rafd is the name of the thing that is given to a person, which is the support. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: What an evil provision is it, he said: The curse of this world and the hereafter. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: What a wretched provision! He said: God cursed them in this world, and the curse was increased for them in the Hereafter. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And on the Day of Resurrection, what an evil provision it will be, he said: A curse in this world, and they will be given an additional curse in the Hereafter. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And they will be followed in this world by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection, what an evil provision it is. He said: Two curses from God followed one after the other upon them, a curse in this world and a curse in the Hereafter. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: They were afflicted with two curses in this world, one of which was augmented by the other, and that is His statement: And on the Day of Resurrection, what an evil provision it is.
11:100: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: This story that we have mentioned to you in this surah, and the report that we have informed you of in it, of the report of the towns whose people we destroyed for their disbelief in God and their denial of His messengers, We relate it to you, so we inform you of it, Some of them are standing, meaning: Some of them have their buildings standing, their people destroyed and perishing, and some of them have their buildings standing and inhabited, and some of them have their buildings harvested, ruined and crumbling, their traces obliterated and forgotten. From their saying: A harvest has been harvested, if its pieces have been uprooted. It is actually harvested, but it has been converted to fa’il, as we have explained in its counterparts. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: This is from the report of the towns which We relate to you, of them are standing and some have been harvested, meaning by standing are inhabited towns and by harvest are dormant towns. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Standing and harvested, he said: Standing, on its thrones, and harvested, uprooted. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Some of it is standing, its place is seen, and a harvest, no trace of it is seen. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Some of it is standing, he said: empty on its thrones, and harvested, stuck to the ground. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash: Some of it is standing and some is harvested, he said: Its building collapsed. Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash: Some of it is standing and some is harvested. He said: Harvested is what has its building collapsed. Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his saying: Some of it is standing and some is harvested, some of it is standing and its trace is visible, and some of it is harvested and its trace is gone and its trace is not seen.
11:101: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And We did not punish the people of these towns whose report We related to you, O Muhammad, without them deserving Our punishment, so we would have put Our punishment in the wrong place, but they wronged themselves, meaning: but they made His punishment and torment obligatory for themselves through their disobedience to God and their disbelief in Him, so they made lawful for themselves what they should not have made lawful for them, and made lawful for them what they should not have made lawful for them, so their gods which they invoke besides God availed them nothing, meaning: their gods which they invoke besides God, and whom they call as lords, did not repel from them God’s punishment and torment when their Lord made it lawful, nor did they repel any of it from them, when the command of your Lord came, O Muhammad, meaning: when the judgment of your Lord came to punish them, His punishment became due upon them, and His wrath descended upon them, and they only increased them in affliction. Tabbab means: And their gods did not increase them, when the command of your Lord came to these polytheists with the punishment of God, except loss, destruction, and devastation. It is said: I cursed him, I cursed him, and from it they say to a man: May you perish. Jarir said: Arada from the rest of Lot's people, do not perish for what they did, perish And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Saeed bin Salam Abu Al-Hasan Al-Basri told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Naseer bin Dhaluq, on the authority of Ibn Omar, regarding his statement: And they did not increase them except in destruction, he said: except in loss. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: other than destruction, he said: loss. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: other than destruction, he says: other than loss. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Not causing loss, he said: Not causing loss. Abu Ja`far said: This report is from God, the Most High, and even if it is report about the nations that came before us, it is a threat from God, the Most High, to us, O nation. If we follow the path of the nations before us in disagreeing with Him and His Messenger, He will follow their path in punishment. It is an announcement from Him to us that He does not wrong any of His creation, and that the servants are the ones who wrong themselves, as: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: He - meaning our Lord, may His praise be glorified - apologized to His creation and said: And We did not wrong them, from what we mentioned to you of the punishment of those nations whom We punished, but they wronged themselves, so their gods did not avail them, until he reached: And they did not increase them except in destruction, he said: Those whom they worshipped did not increase them except in destruction.
11:102: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And just as I seized, O people, the people of these towns whose people I have related to you, with the punishment I inflicted upon them, for their disobedience to My command, their denial of My messengers, and their rejection of My signs, so will I seize the towns and their people when I seize them with My punishment, while they are wrongdoers to themselves because of their disbelief in God, their associating others with Him, and their denial of His messengers. His seizure is painful, meaning: If your Lord seizes with punishment whoever seizes Him, painful, meaning: painful, severe in pain. This is a warning from God to this nation, lest they follow in disobeying Him the path of the wicked nations before them, lest the same punishments that befell them will befall them, such as: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Burdah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Musa, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God gives the oppressor respite - or perhaps he said: He gives him time - until when He seizes him, He does not let him go. Then he recited: ‘And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are doing wrong.’” Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: God warned this nation of His wrath, by saying: “And thus is the punishment of your Lord when He punishes the towns while they are wrongdoers. Indeed, His punishment is painful and severe.” Asim Al-Jahdary used to recite it: And thus did your Lord seize when He seized the towns while they were unjust. This is a recitation that I do not permit reciting, because it is contrary to the Muslims’ copies of the Qur’an, and what the regions recite according to.
11:103: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Indeed, in Our taking of those We took from the people of the towns whose report We related to you, O people, is a sign, meaning: a lesson and admonition for those of His servants who fear God’s punishment and torment in the Hereafter, and an argument against him before his Lord, and a deterrent that restrains him from disobeying God and opposing Him in what He has commanded and forbidden. It was said: Rather, the meaning of this is: It contains a lesson for those who fear the torment of the Hereafter, that God will fulfill His promise to them. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: Indeed in that is a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter, We will fulfill for them what We promised them in the Hereafter, just as We fulfilled for the prophets: We will support them. And His statement: That is a Day for which the people will be gathered, God Almighty says: This Day - meaning the Day of Resurrection - is a Day for which the people will be gathered, meaning: God will gather the people from their graves for it, and will gather them on it for recompense, reward, and punishment. And that is a witnessed Day, meaning: It is a Day that all creatures will witness, and none of them will be left behind. Then He will take revenge on those who disobeyed God, opposed His command, and denied His messengers. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: That is a Day when the people will be gathered together, and that is a witnessed Day, he said: The Day of Resurrection. Yaqoub told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Ikrimah, the same. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Yusuf al-Makki, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The witness is Muhammad, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited: That is a Day when the people will be gathered together, and that is a witnessed Day. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The witness is Muhammad, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited this verse: That is a Day when the people will be gathered together, and that is a witnessed Day. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said: That is a Day when people will be gathered together, and that is a witnessed Day. He said: That is the Day of Resurrection, on which all of creation will be gathered, and the people of heaven and earth will witness it.
11:104: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And We do not delay the Day of Resurrection from bringing it to you except for its fulfillment. So He has decreed a term for it, counted it, and enumerated it, so it will not come except for that term. Its coming will not precede it or be delayed.
11:105: God Almighty says: “On the Day when it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission. Then among them will be the wretched and the happy.”
11:106: God Almighty says: “But as for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire. Therein they will have sighing and sobbing.”
11:107: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: On the Day when the Resurrection comes, O people, and the Hour is established, no soul will speak except by permission of its Lord. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: The Day comes. The majority of the people of Medina read it with the addition of the letter ya in it: The day comes when no soul will speak. Some of the people of Basra and some of the people of Kufa read this by confirming the ya’ in it when connected and deleting it when stopping. A group of people from Kufa read it without the letter ya in both connected and paused verses: On the Day He comes, no soul will speak except by His permission. Abu Ja`far said: The correct reading of this, in my opinion, is: the day it comes, deleting the ya’ in both connected and paused words, following the script of the Qur’an, and it is a well-known language of Hudhayl, which says: I do not know what you say, and from this is the saying of the poet: Enough, a hand that does not befit a generous dirham and another that gives blood with the sword It was said: Do not speak, but it is: Do not speak, so one of the two ta’s was deleted, out of boldness, as the remaining one indicates it. And his saying: Among them are the wretched and the happy, he says: Among these souls that will not speak on the Day of Resurrection except with the permission of their Lord, are the wretched and the happy, and it returns to the soul, and it is one in the wording, by mentioning all of them in his saying: Among them are the wretched and the happy. God Almighty says: “As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire. Therein they will have a sigh,” which is the first braying of a donkey or something similar, and a sob, which is the last braying of a donkey when it returns it to the stomach when it finishes braying, as Ru’bah ibn al-‘Ajaj said: He made a gasp in his stomach, or he gasped, until it was said that he brayed, but he did not bray. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Therein they will have sighing and sobbing, meaning: a loud sound and a weak sound. He said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah, regarding his statement: For them therein is sighing and breathing, he said: The sigh is in the throat, and the breathing is in the chest. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, something similar. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: The voice of the unbeliever in the Fire is the voice of a donkey, its beginning is a sigh and its end is a sob. Abu Hisham Al-Rifai, Muhammad bin Muammar Al-Bahrani, Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna, and Muhammad bin Bashar narrated to us, they said: Abu Amir narrated to us, he said: Sulayman bin Sufyan narrated to us, he said: Abdullah bin Dinar narrated to us, “On the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: When this verse was revealed: ‘Among them are the wretched and the blessed,’ I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: O Prophet of God, then what did we act upon? On something that had already been completed, or on something that had not yet been completed? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On something that had already been completed, O Umar, and the pens had written about it, but everyone is facilitated for what he was created for.” The wording is from the hadith of Ibn Muammar. And His statement: “They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is the Doer of what He intends.” God Almighty means by His statement: They will abide therein, remaining therein. And by His statement: As long as the heavens and the earth endure, He means forever. When the Arabs wanted to describe something as lasting forever, they would say: This is as lasting as the heavens and the earth, meaning: it is lasting forever. They also say: It remains as long as night and day differ, and As long as the two sons of Samir stay up late, and As long as the dust of the earth twinkles with its tails, meaning by all of that: forever. So God, the Most High, addressed them in a way that they would recognize among themselves, saying: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, and the meaning of that is: they will abide therein forever. Ibn Zayd used to say something similar to what we said about it. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, he said: As long as the earth remains earth and the sky remains sky. Then he said: Except what your Lord wills. The scholars and interpreters differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: This is an exception that God made for the people of monotheism, that He will take them out of the Fire if He wills, after He has put them in the Fire. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “But as for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire. Therein they will have sighing and sobbing, abiding eternally as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills.” He said: God knows best what is in his two prongs. And he mentioned to us that people will be afflicted with the scorching of the Fire because of sins they committed, then He will admit them to Paradise. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. And God knows best what he meant by his second verse. He mentioned to us that people will be afflicted with the scorching heat of the Fire because of sins they have committed, then God will admit them to Paradise by virtue of His mercy. They will be called the people of Hell. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Shaiban ibn Farukh told us, Abu Hilal told us, Qatada told us, and he recited this verse: “But as for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire. Therein they will have sighing and sobbing,” until His saying: for what they desire, then he said: “Anas ibn Malik told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘A people will come out of the Fire,’” Qatada said: And we do not say what the people of Harura say. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Abu Malik, meaning Tha’laba, on the authority of Abu Sinan, regarding his statement: “But as for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire. Therein they will have sighing and sobbing, abiding eternally as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is the Doer of what He intends.” He said: An exception for the people of monotheism. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim: As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire, until His saying: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills, he said: A people will come out of the Fire and enter Paradise, and they are the ones for whom an exception was made. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Amer bin Jushayb, on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, regarding his statement: They will abide therein for ages, and his statement: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills, that they are regarding the people of monotheism. Others said: The exception in this verse is for the people of monotheism, except that they said: The meaning of His saying: except what your Lord wills, is except that your Lord wills to overlook them and not let them enter the Fire. They explained the exception to the fact that it is from His saying: As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire, “except what your Lord wills,” not from eternity. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn al-Taymi told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Jabir - or: Abu Saeed, meaning al-Khudri, or: on the authority of a man from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding His statement: “Except what your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is the Doer of what He intends,” he said: This verse comes to the entire Qur’an. He says: Where it says in the Qur’an: abiding therein, it comes to it. He said: And I heard Mujaliz say: This is his reward, and if God wills, He will overlook his punishment. Others said: He meant the people of Hell and everyone who entered it. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Musayyab, on the authority of someone who mentioned it, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, they will not die nor will they emerge from it, as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills, he said: God’s exception. He said: He will command the Fire to consume them. He said: Ibn Mas’ud said: A time will come upon Hell when its gates will be flailing, and there will be no one in it, and that will be after they have remained in it for ages. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Bayan, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: Hell is the quickest of the two abodes to be populated, and the quickest of them to be destroyed. Others said: God informed us of His will for the people of Paradise, so we knew the meaning of His two verses in His saying: An uninterrupted gift, that it is in addition to the duration of the heavens and the earth. He said: And He did not inform us of His will for the people of Hell. It is possible that His will is in increase, and it is possible that it is in decrease. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. So he recited until he reached: A gift uninterrupted. He said: And He informed us of what He wills for the people of Paradise, so He said: A gift uninterrupted, and He did not inform us of what He wills for the people of Hell. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these sayings in interpreting this verse is the saying that we mentioned from Qatada and Ad-Dahhak: that this is an exception for the people of monotheism from the people of major sins, that He will put them in the Fire to abide therein forever, except for what He wills of leaving them in it for less than that, then He will take them out and put them in Paradise, as we have explained in other places, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. We said that this is the most correct opinion on this matter, because God, the Most High, promised the polytheists eternally in Hell, and the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are consistent with this. So it is not permissible for it to be an exception for the polytheists. And the reports have been transmitted in succession from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that God will admit some people of the people of faith in Him into Hell because of sins they committed, then He will take them out of it and admit them into Paradise. So it is not permissible for this to be an exception for the people of monotheism before they enter it, with the soundness of the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as we have mentioned. And if we were to make it an exception in this matter, we would have entered into the opinion of those who say: A sinner will not enter Paradise, and a believer will not enter Hell. This is contrary to the schools of thought of the people of knowledge, and what the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have brought. So if these two views are corrupt, then there is no opinion that the role model among the people of knowledge has said except the third. The Arabs have a different opinion on this, which we will mention later and explain, God willing. And His saying: Indeed, your Lord is the Doer of what He wills, the Most High says: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, is not prevented from doing what He wills to those who disobey Him and go against His command, from taking revenge on them, but He does what He wills to do, so He carries out His action and His judgment upon them and upon whomever He wills of His creation.
11:108: Abu Jaafar said: There are different readings of this. The majority of the people of Medina, Hijaz, Basra, and some of the people of Kufa read it as: And as for those who were happy, with the seen open. A group of Kufa reciters read it as: And as for those who were blessed, with a damma on the seen, meaning: they were granted happiness. Abu Jaafar said: The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. If someone says: How is it said, They were made happy, when the subject is not named, and it is not said, They were made happy, and you do not say in the report when the subject is named, May God make him happy, but rather you say, May God make him happy? This is said similar to their saying: He is crazy, and beloved, in cases where the doer is not named. If they name the doer, it is said: God has made him crazy and beloved. The Arabs do this a lot. We have explained some of this previously in this book of ours. The interpretation of this is: As for those who are blessed with the mercy of God, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure. He says: forever, except what your Lord wills. The interpreters differed about the meaning of that. Some of them said: Except what your Lord wills, of the amount of time they spent in Hell before entering Paradise. They said: This is for those believers who were taken out of Hell and entered Paradise. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: But those who are blessed will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills, he said: It also refers to those who are taken out of the Fire and enter Paradise. He says: Abiding in Paradise as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. He says: Except for as long as they remain in the Fire until they are admitted to Paradise. Others said: The meaning of this is: except what your Lord wills, of the increase in the amount of time of the heavens and the earth. They said: And that is eternity in it forever. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Abu Malik - meaning Tha’laba - on the authority of Abu Sinan: And as for those who are blessed, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. He said: And His will is for them to abide therein forever, then he followed it by saying: A gift uninterrupted. The Arab scholars differed on the reason for the exception in this place. Some of them said: There are two meanings to this: One of them: That he makes it an exception that he excludes and does not do, like your saying: By God, I will hit you unless I see otherwise, and your intention to hit him. He said: So likewise he said: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills, and He does not will it, and He knows best. He said: The other statement is that when the Arabs except something that is a lot with its like, or with what is more than it, the meaning of except and the meaning of the waw are the same. So whoever says: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except for what God wills of increasing eternity, then he puts except in place of except, and it is correct, and it is as if he said: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure except for what God wills of increasing eternity and everlastingness.
