And similar to it in speech is that you say: I owe you a thousand except for the two thousand that were from so-and-so. Do you not see that it means: I owe you a thousand in addition to the two thousand? He said: And this is the more preferable of the two interpretations to me, because God does not break His promise. And the exception has reached them in eternity without being cut off from them. Another of them said something similar to this statement. They said: A third aspect is permissible: that he excluded from their eternity in Paradise their being detained from it between death and resurrection, which is the Barzakh, until they reach Paradise, and then it is eternity forever. He says: They were not absent from Paradise except for the duration of their stay in the Barzakh. Another of them said: It is possible that the perpetuity of the heavens and the earth means: eternity, according to what the Arabs know and use, and the will is excluded from its perpetuity, because the people of Paradise and the people of Hell were at a time of the perpetuity of the heavens and the earth in this world, not in Paradise, so it is as if he said: eternal in Paradise, and eternal in Hell, the perpetuity of the heavens and the earth, except for what your Lord wills of their longevity in this world before that. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the saying you mentioned on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, which is: And as for those who are blessed, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills, according to the amount of time they will remain in the Fire, from the time they enter it until they are admitted to Paradise. The meaning of the verse is specific, because the most common of the speech of the Arabs in except is to direct it to the meaning of exception, and to exclude the meaning of what comes after it from what comes before it, unless there is an indication with it that indicates otherwise. And there is no indication in the speech, I mean in His statement: except what your Lord wills, that indicates that its meaning is other than the meaning of exception understood in the speech, so it is directed to it. As for his saying: A gift that is not cut off, he means: a gift from God that is not cut off from them. From their saying: I cut off the thing, I cut it off, as Al-Nabigha said: The double greyhound pulls its web and lights the fire of the firebirds with its blades. He means by his saying: to cut off, to cut off. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: A gift that is not cut off, he said: not cut off. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: A gift that is not cut off, meaning: not interrupted. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A gift that is not cut off, he said: a gift that is not cut off. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Majdhudh he said: cut off. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: A gift that is not cut off, he said: Not cut off. He said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, regarding his statement: A gift that is not cut off, he said: As for this, he has confirmed it, meaning: a gift that is not interrupted. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: A gift not cut off, not taken away from them.
11:109: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not be in doubt, O Muhammad, about what these polytheists of your people worship of gods and idols, that it is misguidance and falsehood, and that it is polytheism with God, They worship nothing but as their fathers worshipped before, meaning: except as their fathers worshipped, before they worshipped them. God Almighty informs us that they did not worship what they worshipped of idols except by following the path of their fathers, and by following in their footsteps in their worship of them, not because of God's command to them to do so, nor because of a proof that they had clarified that would require them to worship them. Then He, the Most High, informed His Prophet what He would do to them for their worship of that, and He, the Most High, said: And We will surely give them their share, undiminished. Meaning: Their portion of what I promised them that I would give them, whether good or evil, undiminished. He says: I will not diminish what I promised them, but rather I will complete it for them in its entirety and perfection, as: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We will surely give them their share, undiminished, he said: What they were promised of good or evil. Abu Kurayb and Muhammad ibn Bashar told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same, except that Abu Kurayb said in his hadith: of good and evil. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We will surely give them their share, undiminished, he said: What was decreed for them of good and evil. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And We will surely give them their share, undiminished, he said: Whatever good or evil befalls them. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And We will surely give them their share, undiminished, he said: Their share of the punishment.
11:110: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says, consoling His Prophet for the denial of the polytheists of his people regarding what he brought them from God, with the actions of the Children of Israel regarding what he brought them from God. God Almighty says to him: Do not be sad, O Muhammad, for these polytheists to deny you, and continue with what your Lord has commanded you to do, in conveying His message, for what these people are doing to you, in rejecting the advice you brought them, is the action of their peers among the nations before them, and is one of their traditions. Then He, the Most High, informed us of what the people of Moses did to him, saying: And We gave Moses the Book, meaning the Torah, just as We gave you the Criterion. The people of Moses differed concerning that Book, so some of them denied it and some of them believed in it, just as your people did with the Criterion, by some believing in it and others disbelieving in it. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, the Most High says: And had it not been for a word that preceded, O Muhammad, from your Lord that He does not hasten the punishment of His creation, but rather waits until the Book reaches its term, it would have been decided between them, meaning: it would have been decided between those among them who denied it and those who believed in it, by God destroying those among them who denied it and saving those who believed in it. And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt about it, meaning: And indeed, those among them who denied it are in disquieting doubt about its truth that it is from God, disquieting, meaning: it makes them doubt, so they do not know whether it is true or false? But they are in doubt about it.
11:111: Abu Jaafar said: The reading of that differed. A group of the people of Medina and Kufa read it as: Wa-in with emphasis, Kala-lama with emphasis. The Arabs differed about the meaning of this. Some Kufi grammarians said: Its meaning, if it is read like this, is: And indeed, each of them is for your Lord to pay them their deeds in full. But when the two meems came together, one was deleted, leaving two, so one was assimilated into the other, as the poet said: I am one of those who issue orders, if he is exhausted by the path of its sources Then it is lightened, as some reciters read: And the oppressor admonishes you, the ya is lightened with the ya. It was mentioned that Al-Kisa’i recited it: The enemies gloated over us, so they came to me and rejoiced over what we had suffered. He said: He means that they are rejoicing over what we have encountered, so he deleted the ya because of their movement and their coming together. He said: And similar to it: As if from the end of it the one coming is perforated, and the Najd is tall and prominent He said: He meant: to the one who is coming, so he deleted the lam when it came to the lam. Others said: The meaning of that, if it is read in this way: “And indeed each is severe and true. Your Lord will surely pay them their deeds in full.” He said: Rather, what is meant, if it is read in this way, is: And indeed each is for you, with emphasis and tanween. However, the one who reads it in this way deleted the tanween from it, so he made it sound like fa’l lama, as he did in His statement: Then We sent Our messengers in succession. Some of them read tatara with tanween, as the one who read lama read it with tanween, and others read it without tanween, as the one who read lama read it without tanween. They said: Its origin is from lam from the statement of God the Most High: And you consume the inheritance with a severe devotion, meaning: a severe devotion. Others said: The meaning of that, if it is read in this way, is: And none but He will pay them their due, as one says: By God, why did you stand up for us? And by God, why did you stand up for us? Abu Ja`far said: I found most of the scholars of Arabic rejecting this statement, and refusing that it is permissible to direct lama to the meaning of illa, except in oaths in particular. They said: If it were permissible for it to mean illa, then it would be permissible to say: The people stood up when your brother stood up, meaning: except your brother, and its inclusion in every place where illa is permissible to include. Abu Ja`far said: I see that this is invalid in a way that is clearer than what those Arabists whose words we have mentioned have said about its invalidity, which is that in is an affirmation of something and a confirmation of it, and illa is also a confirmation, and it only enters to refute a denial that precedes it. So if that is its meaning, then it is necessary that the one who interprets it have the interpretation that we mentioned about him, that in means denial according to him, so that illa would be a refutation of it. And that is if someone says it, a statement that does not hide the ignorance of its speaker, unless the reader of in makes it lighter and makes it mean in which means denial. And if he does that, then his reading of it is invalid in another way, which is that he then becomes the subject of kull by saying: li-yawwafinhum, and it is not in Arabic that what comes after illa of the verb is the subject of the noun that precedes it. The Arabs do not say: Ma Zaidan illa darbat, which would be invalid if it is read in this way, unless the one who raises the whole is raised, in which case reading it in this way would contradict the reading of the Qur’an and the script of the Muslims’ Qur’ans, and it would not be considered defective because it is outside the well-known speech of the Arabs. Some of the Kufians read it as: And both, with a light in and a heavy kala lama in the accusative case. Some Arabists claimed that the reader of that is like that, he meant the heavy in so he lightened it, and it was mentioned on the authority of Abu Zaid al-Basri that he heard: As if his breasts were two halves, so he made it accusative with as if, and the nun is lightened from as if, and from it is the saying of the poet: A face with a bright neck, as if his breasts were two halves Some of the Medinans read it with a lightened in and a nasb for kala and a lightened lama. It may be possible that the reader of that was like that, intending the meaning that we narrated from the reader of Kufa in his lightening of the nun of in while he wanted to make it heavy, and he meant by ma in lamma that enters into the speech a connection, and that he intended to load the speech with the meaning: And indeed, both of them will be fully paid. It is possible that its meaning was that in his reading of it like that: And indeed, each one of them will be paid in full, meaning: To pay each one of them, so his intention in putting each one of them in the accusative case was by saying: To pay each one of them. If that is what he meant, then what I mentioned is ugly in it, as it is contrary to the speech of the Arabs. That is because it is not put in the accusative case by a verb after the lam of the oath, a noun before it. Some of the people of Hijaz and Basra read it as: Wa-in, with a shaddah on both la-ma, with a light li-yuwafayyinhum. This reading has two meanings: One of them: that the reader intended: And indeed, all of them are for your Lord to pay them in full for their deeds, so he directs the ma in lama to the meaning of min as the Most High said: Then marry such women as seem good to you, even though the Arabs used it most of the time for other than the sons of Adam. And he intends by the lam in lama the lam with which in is received as an answer to it, and by the lam in His saying: for them to pay them in full, the lam of the oath, which entered between what it connected, as the Most High said: And indeed, among you are those who are slow to do so, and as it is said: This is what is better for someone else than it. The other aspect: to make the ma in lama mean the ma that enters into a connection in the speech, and the lam in it is the lam with which it is answered, and the lam in liyuwafinhum is also the lam with which it is answered if, it was repeated and re-repeated, since that was its place, and the first was one of those that the Arabs insert in a place other than its place, then they repeat it later in its place, as the poet said: If my people were not honorable, I would have inevitably met with death. Al-Zuhri read it as mentioned by him: And both, with emphasis on in, and lama with a tanween, meaning: very strongly, truly, and all together. Abu Jaafar said: The most correct of these readings, based on the widespread speech of the Arabs, is the reading of those who read: And indeed with emphasis on its noon, both for and for with emphasis on for, for your Lord will pay them in full, meaning: Indeed, all of those about whom We have related to you, O Muhammad, their stories in this surah, for those whom Your Lord will pay them in full for their deeds, for the good among them with a great reward, and for the bad among them with emphasis with punishment. So for is in the sense of for, and the for in it is an answer to for, and the for in His statement, for your Lord will pay them in full, is a for oath. And His statement: He is All-Aware of what they do, the Most High says: Your Lord is All-Aware of what these polytheists among your people, O Muhammad, do. Nothing of their actions is hidden from Him, rather He informs of all of it and knows it and encompasses it, until He rewards them for all of it with their reward.
11:112: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: So, O Muhammad, stand firm on the command of your Lord, and the religion with which He sent you, and call to it as your Lord has commanded you, and whoever repents with you, meaning: whoever returns with you to obeying God, and doing what his Lord has commanded him to do after his disbelief, and do not transgress, meaning: do not transgress His command to what He has forbidden you from, Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do, meaning: Your Lord, O people, of all the deeds you do, whether they are obedient to Him or disobey Him, is Seeing, He has knowledge of them, nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He is All-Seeing of all of them. God Almighty says: So fear God, O people, lest your Lord see you while you are doing something contrary to His command, for He is All-Knowing of what you do, and He is watching you. Ibn Uyaynah used to say about the meaning of his saying: So stand firm as you have been commanded, what: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Sufyan, regarding his statement: So stand firm as you have been commanded, he said: Stand firm on the Qur’an. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And do not transgress, he said: Transgression is disobeying God and committing His disobedience. That is transgression.
11:113: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: “And do not incline, O people, to the saying of those who disbelieved in God, so that you accept from them and are pleased with their deeds, ‘lest the Fire touch you’, because of your doing that, and you will have no helper to support you and no guardian to watch over you, ‘then you will not be helped’,” meaning: If you do that, God will not help you, but rather He will deprive you of His help and will give power to your enemy over you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: And do not incline toward those who do wrong, lest the Fire touch you, meaning: inclining toward polytheism. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah: And do not incline toward those who do wrong, meaning: Do not be pleased with their deeds. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, regarding his statement: And do not incline toward those who do wrong, he said: Do not be pleased with their deeds. He said: Inclination means contentment. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And do not incline toward those who do wrong, he said, Ibn Abbas said: And do not incline toward those who do wrong. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And do not incline toward those who do wrong, lest the Fire touch you, meaning: Do not join polytheism, which is what you have come out of. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, {And do not incline toward those who do wrong, lest the Fire touch you}, he said, incline means abasement. And he recited: {They wish that you would compromise, so they would compromise}. He said: Incline toward them, and do not denounce them for what they said, and they have said the great thing about their disbelief in God, His Book, and His Messengers. He said: This is only for the people of disbelief and polytheism, and not for the people of Islam. As for the sinners among the people of Islam, God knows best about their sins and deeds. No one should compromise over any of the sins of God, nor incline toward Him in them.
11:114: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And establish prayer, O Muhammad, meaning: pray, at the two ends of the day, meaning: morning and evening. The interpreters differed as to which of the evening prayers was meant by this verse, after they all agreed that the one designated from the morning prayers was the dawn prayer. Some of them said: I meant the noon and afternoon prayers. They said: They are part of the evening prayer. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day, he said: the dawn prayer, and the two evening prayers, meaning the noon and afternoon prayers. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day, he said: The dawn prayer and the evening prayer. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Aflah bin Saeed, he said: I heard Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi say: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day. He said: The two ends of the day are dawn, noon, and afternoon. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Ma`shar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka`b Al-Qurazi: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day. He said: The two ends of the day are dawn, noon, and afternoon. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day, he said: Fajr, noon, and afternoon. Others said: Rather, he meant the Maghrib prayer. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day, he said: the dawn prayer and the sunset prayer. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Yahya told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day, he said: the dawn and sunset prayers. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day, the dawn and sunset prayers. Others said: He meant the afternoon prayer. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abda bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day, he said: the dawn and afternoon prayers. He said, Zaid bin Habbab told us, on the authority of Aflah bin Saeed Al-Qaba’i, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day, he said, the dawn and afternoon prayers. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Abu Raja told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day, he said: The dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told me, he said, my father told us, he said, Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: God said to His Prophet: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day, he said: The two ends of the day, the morning and the afternoon prayers. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day, meaning the afternoon and morning prayers. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Mubarak bin Fadala, on the authority of al-Hasan: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day, the morning and afternoon prayers. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zaid bin Habbab told us, on the authority of Aflah bin Saeed, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day, the dawn and afternoon prayers. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Amer told us, he said, Qurra told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day, he said: the morning and afternoon prayers. Some of them said: Rather, he meant by the two ends of the day, noon and afternoon, and by saying: near the end of the night, sunset, evening, and dawn. Abu Jaafar said: The most correct of these statements in my opinion is the statement of the one who said: It is the Maghrib prayer, as we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Rather, we said: It is more correct, because everyone has agreed that the prayer of one of the two parties is the Fajr prayer, and it is prayed before sunrise. So, since this was agreed upon by all of them, it is obligatory that the prayer of the other party be Maghrib, because it is prayed after sunset. If it were obligatory that what is meant by the prayer of one of the two parties be before sunset, then what is meant by the prayer of the other party be after sunrise. And that is what we do not know of anyone who said, except for the one who said: He meant the Dhuhr and Asr prayers. And that is a statement that is not likely to be corrupt, because they are closer to being both part of the prayer of one of the two parties than they are to being part of the prayer of the two ends of the day. That is because there is no doubt that Dhuhr is prayed after half the day has passed in the second half of it, so it is impossible for it to be part of the first end of the day, while it is in its other end. If no scholar says: What is meant by the prayer of the two ends of the first day is the prayer after sunrise, then it must be impermissible to say: What is meant by the prayer of the other end of the day is the prayer before sunset. If that is the case, then what we have said about it is correct, and what contradicts it is invalid. As for his saying: and the approach of the night, he means: hours of the night. It is the plural of zalfa, and zalfa means the hour, the place of residence, and the place of nearness. It was said: It was called Muzdalifah and the plural of it, because it is a place of residence after Arafat, and it was said that it was called that because Adam approached from Arafat to Eve while she was there, and from this is the saying of al-Ajjaj in describing a camel: He survived the nights that were far away from him, and he was cut off from them one by one. There are different readings of this. The general reading of the people of Medina and Iraq is: wazalfa, with a damma on the zay and a fatha on the lam. Some of the people of Medina read it with a damma on the zay and the lam, as if he meant that it is one and that it is like a dream. Some Meccans read it as: Wazalfa, with a damma on the zay and a sukoon on the lam. Abu Jaafar said: The most amazing readings in this regard, until I read it: and zalfa, with a damma on the zay and a fatha on the lam, meaning the plural of zalfa, just as a room is pluralized as ghurf and a room is pluralized as hijr. I chose to read it this way because the last ‘Isha’ prayer is only performed after the end of the night, which is what I meant by his saying: and the end of the night. And similar to what we said about his statement: And at the approach of the night, a group of people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: And the approach of the night, he said: Hours of the night, the Isha prayer. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: At a close moment of the night, he said: the Isha prayer. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Yahya told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And the approach of the night, he said: the evening prayer. Abu Kuraib told us, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abi Yazid, who said, Ibn Abbas liked to delay the Isha prayer, and he would recite: And at the approach of the night. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And at the approach of the night, he said: an hour of the night, the Isha prayer. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And the approach of the night, meaning darkness. And I have not heard any of our jurists and sheikhs say Isha. They only say darkness. Some people said: The prayer that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded to be performed at the beginning of the night is the sunset and evening prayers. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim and Ibn Wakee’ told me - and the wording is Yaqub’s - they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Abu Raja’ told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And two approaches of the night, he said: They are two approaches of the night, the Maghrib prayer and the Isha prayer. Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And the approach of the night, he said: the sunset and the evening prayers. Al-Hasan bin Ali told me, he said, my father told us, he said, Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. He said: At the approach of the night, the sunset and the evening prayers. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are the two ends of the night, the sunset and the evening prayers.” Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And the approach of the night, he said: the sunset and the evening prayers. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Naim told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Mubarak ibn Fadala, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said: God has explained the times of prayer in the Qur’an. He said: {Establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night}, he said: Its decline is when it has passed its zenith and has shade on the earth. And He said: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day, dawn and afternoon, and at the approach of the night, sunset and evening. He said: “Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are the two approaches of the night, sunset and evening.” Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the approach of the night, he said: He means the Maghrib prayer and the Isha prayer. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Aflah bin Saeed, he said: I heard Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi say: At the end of the night means the sunset and evening prayers. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zaid bin Habab told us, on the authority of Aflah bin Saeed, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, the same. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Ma`shar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka`b Al-Qurazi: And the approach of the night means the sunset and evening prayers. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Asim bin Sulayman, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The two times of night have approached, the sunset and the evening. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: And at the approach of the night, he said: the sunset and the evening prayers. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And the approach of the night, he said: the sunset and evening prayers. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abda bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: And the approach of the night, he said: the sunset and evening prayers. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Hasan: At the end of the night means the Maghrib and Isha prayers. And His statement: Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds, the Almighty says: Indeed, turning to obeying God and doing what pleases Him removes the sins of disobeying God and expiates transgressions. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the good deeds that God meant in this place, which remove the bad deeds. Some of them said: They are the five obligatory prayers. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Al-Ward bin Thamamah, on the authority of Abu Muhammad bin Al-Hadrami, he said, Ka`b told us in this mosque, he said: By the One in Whose Hand is Ka`b’s soul, the five daily prayers have good deeds that remove bad deeds, just as water washes away dirt. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Aflah, he said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi say regarding His statement: Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds, he said: They are the five daily prayers. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muslim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed, good deeds do away with bad deeds, he said: the five daily prayers. He said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: The good deeds are the prayers. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Yahya told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, Abu Usamah told us, all of them, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, Indeed, good deeds do away with bad deeds, he said: the five daily prayers. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds, he said: The five daily prayers. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The five prayers. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah: Indeed, good deeds do away with bad deeds, he said: the five daily prayers. He said, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Saeed al-Jariri, who said, Abu Uthman told me, on the authority of Salman, who said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the good deeds with which God erases the bad deeds, just as water washes away dirt, are the five daily prayers. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muslim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed, good deeds do away with bad deeds, he said: the five daily prayers. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Mazida bin Zaid, on the authority of Masruq: Indeed, good deeds eliminate bad deeds, he said: the five daily prayers. Muhammad ibn Amara al-Asadi and Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatwani told me, they said, Abdullah ibn Yazid told us, he said, Haywah told us, he said, Abu Aqil Zuhra ibn Mu’id al-Qurashi from Banu Taym from the people of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, told us: He heard al-Harith, the freed slave of Uthman ibn Affan, may God have mercy on him, say: “Uthman sat one day and we sat with him, then the muezzin came to him, so Uthman called for water in a vessel, I think there would be enough water in it for a mudd, so he performed ablution and then said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution as I do, then he said: Whoever performs ablution as I do, then stands up and prays the noon prayer, his sins between him and the dawn prayer will be forgiven, then he prays the afternoon prayer, his sins between him and the noon prayer will be forgiven, then he prays the sunset prayer, his sins between him and the afternoon prayer will be forgiven, then he prays the ‘Isha’ prayer, his sins between him and the sunset prayer will be forgiven, then perhaps he will spend the night wallowing, then if he stands up and performs ablution and prays the dawn prayer, his sins between him and the ‘Isha’ prayer will be forgiven, and these are the good deeds that eliminate the bad deeds.”. Saad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me, he said, Abu Zur’ah told us, he said, Haywah told us, he said, Abu Aqil Zuhra bin Ma’bad told us, that he heard Al-Harith, the client of Uthman bin Affan, say: Uthman bin Affan sat one day on the seats, and he mentioned something similar to it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except that he said: And they are the good deeds: Indeed, good deeds eliminate bad deeds. Ibn al-Barqi told us, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Nafi’ ibn Yazid and Rashdin ibn Sa’d told us, they said, Zuhra ibn Ma’bad told us, he said: I heard al-Harith, the freed slave of Uthman ibn Affan, say: Uthman ibn Affan sat one day on the seats, then he mentioned something similar to that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except that he said: And they are the good deeds: Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds. Ibn Sayyar al-Qazzaz narrated, al-Hajjaj narrated, Hammad narrated, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: I was with Salman under a tree, and he took one of its dry branches and shook it until its leaves fell off. Then he said: This is what the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) did. I was with him under a tree, and he took one of its dry branches and shook it until its leaves fell off. Then he said: Will you not ask me why I did this, O Salman? I said: Why did you do it? He said: When a Muslim performs ablution and does it well, then prays the five daily prayers, his sins fall off just as these leaves fall off. Then he recited this verse: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night, to the end of the verse. Others said: It is saying: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is the greatest. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed, good deeds eliminate bad deeds. He said: Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is greatest. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two interpretations in this regard is the statement of the one who said: They are the five daily prayers, because of the authenticity of the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their being transmitted in succession from him, that he said: The example of the five daily prayers is like a river flowing at the door of one of you, in which he immerses himself five times each day, so what remains of his filth? And that this is in the context of God’s command to establish the prayers, and the promise of a great reward for establishing them, which is more appropriate than the promise for what was not mentioned of the other good deeds, if some are specifically intended for that and not others. And His statement: That is a reminder for those who remember, God Almighty says: This is what you have been threatened with, of inclining to injustice, and what you have been threatened with, of establishing the prayers that remove evil deeds, a reminder with which you remind a people who remember God’s promise, so they hope for His reward and His threat, and fear His punishment, not one whose heart has been sealed, so he does not respond to a caller, nor listen to a warning. He mentioned that this verse was revealed because of a man who had taken from someone other than his wife and whom he did not own some of what was forbidden to him, so he repented of his sin. The novel mentioned that: Hannad bin Al-Sarri narrated to us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas narrated to us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah and Al-Aswad, they said, Abdullah bin Masoud said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I had sexual intercourse with a woman in one of the districts of Madinah, and I had intercourse with her without touching her. As for this, decide as you wish! Umar said: God has concealed you, if only you had concealed yourself! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not want anything from him. So the man got up and left, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, followed him with a man and called him. When he came to him, he recited to him: ‘Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.’ A man from the people said: Is this specifically for him, O Messenger of God? He said: Rather, it is for all people.” Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said: Wakee’ narrated to us, and Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah and Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I met a woman in the garden, so I embraced her, and touched her, and kissed her, and did everything to her except that I did not have intercourse with her. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained silent, and this verse was revealed: ‘Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.’ So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and recited it to him, and Umar said: O Messenger of God, is it specifically for him, or for all of the people? He said: No, rather for all of the people.” The wording of the hadith is from Ibn Wakee’. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, that he heard Ibrahim bin Yazid narrating, on the authority of Alqamah and al-Aswad, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I found a woman in a garden, and I did everything to her, except that I did not have intercourse with her. I kissed her, and I stuck to her, and I did nothing else, so do with me whatever you wish. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not say anything to him. So the man went away, and `Umar said: God had concealed him, if only He had concealed himself! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, followed him with his gaze and said: Bring him back to me! So they brought him back, and he recited to him: ‘Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.’ Mu`adh bin Jabal said: Is it for God alone, O Prophet of God, or for all of mankind? He said: Rather, for all of mankind.” Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, and Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I took a woman in the garden and took everything from her, except that I did not marry her, so do with me as you wish! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent. When he had gone, he called him and recited to him this verse: ‘Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night,’” the verse. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Nu'man al-Hakam ibn Abdullah al-'Ajli narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, he said: I heard Ibrahim narrating, on the authority of his maternal uncle al-Aswad, on the authority of Abdullah: "A man met a woman in one of the streets of Madinah, and he did something with her that was less than intercourse. So he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, so the verse was revealed: 'Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.'" Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: O Messenger of God, is this specific to us, or is it general for us? He said: Rather, it is general for you." Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, he said, Samak told me, he said, I heard Ibrahim narrating, on the authority of his maternal uncle, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud: “A man said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I met a woman in a courtyard in Medina, and I had intercourse with her in a way that was less than intercourse, something similar.” Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Qatn Amr Ibn Al-Haitham Al-Baghdadi told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of his maternal uncle, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Abu al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: “So-and-so ibn Mu’tab, a man from the Ansar, came and said: ‘O Messenger of God, a woman came to me and I did with her what a man does with his wife, except that I did not have intercourse with her?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not know how to answer him, until this verse was revealed: ‘Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds,’ the verse. So he called him and recited it to him.” Yaqub and Ibn Wakee’ told me, they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, and Humayd ibn Mas’adah told us, he said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, and Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, all of them, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud: “A man did something to a woman, I do not know what it amounted to, but it was less than fornication. So he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, so the verse was revealed: ‘Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds.’ The man said: Is this for me, O Messenger of God? He said: ‘For whoever among my nation takes it, or whoever acts upon it.’” Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakee’ told me: Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Abu Uthman, who said: I was with Salman, and he took a dry branch of a tree and chopped it, and he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever performs ablution and does it well, his sins will fall away like these leaves fall away! Then he said: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night, to the end of the verse. Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said: Abu Usamah and Husayn al-Ja`fi narrated to us, on the authority of Za`idah, he said: `Abd al-Malik ibn `Umair narrated to us, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, on the authority of Mu`adh, he said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of a man who meets a woman whom he does not know, and he does not do anything to his wife except that he does it to him, except that he does not have intercourse with her? So God revealed this verse: ‘Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Perform ablution and then pray. Mu`adh said: I said: O Messenger of God, is it for him specifically, or for the believers in general? He said: Rather, for the believers in general.” Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Abd al-Malik ibn `Umair, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila: “A man had intercourse with a woman, but not sexual intercourse. He came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about that. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited - or it was revealed: ‘Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night,’ the verse. Mu`adh said: O Messenger of God, is it specifically for him, or for all people? He said: It is for all people.” Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Malik Ibn Umair, he said: I heard Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Abi Laila say: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar. Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Shabwayh told me, he said, Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Amr bin Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdullah bin Salim told me, on the authority of Al-Zubaidi, he said, Salim bin Aamer told us: that he heard Abu Umamah say: “A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, establish the limits of God, once or twice. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him, then the prayer was called, and when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished, he said: Where is this one who said: establish the limits of God? He said: I am here! He said: Did you complete the ablution and pray with us just now? He said: Yes! He said: Then you are free from your sin as your mother bore you, so do not do it again! And God then revealed to His Messenger: “Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night,” the verse.” Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, he said, Jarir narrated to me, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Abi Laila, “On the authority of Muadh bin Jabal: that he was sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when a man came and said: O Messenger of God, a man has done to a woman what is not permissible for him, he did not leave anything that a man does to his wife without doing it, except that he did not have intercourse with her? He said: He should perform ablution properly and then pray. Then God revealed this verse: “Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night,” the verse. Muadh said: O Messenger of God, is it for him specifically or for the Muslims in general? He said: Rather, for the Muslims in general.” Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Muhammad bin Muslim narrated to us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Yahya bin Ja’dah: “A man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned a woman while he was sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked his permission for a need, so he gave him permission. He went to look for her but did not find her. The man came wanting to give the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, good report of rain, and he found the woman sitting by a pond. He pushed her chest and sat between her legs, and his penis became like a tuft of hair. He got up regretfully until he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him what he had done. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Seek forgiveness from your Lord and pray four rak’ahs. He said: And he recited to him: ‘Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night,’ the verse.” Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais bin Al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Muhab, on the authority of Musa bin Talha, on the authority of Abu Al-Yusr bin Umar Al-Ansari, he said: A woman came to me to buy dates from me for a dirham, so I said: There are dates in the house better than these! So I entered, and I was drawn to her and kissed her. So I went to Abu Bakr and asked him, and he said: Cover yourself, repent and seek forgiveness from God! So I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Did you replace a man fighting in the way of God with his family for something like this? Until I thought I was among the people of Hell, until I wished I had converted to Islam at that moment! He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lowered his head for a while, then Gabriel came down and said: Where is Abu Al-Yusr? So I came, and he recited to me: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night to A reminder for those who remember. A man said: O Messenger of God, is it for him specifically, or for all people? He said: All people.” Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: A man kissed a woman, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Prophet of God, I am ruined! So God revealed: “Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.” Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, he said: “A man struck a woman on the back of her neck, then he came to Abu Bakr and Umar, may God have mercy on them. Whenever he asked one of them about the expiation for that, he said: ‘Is it a military campaign?’ He said: ‘Yes!’ He said: ‘I do not know!’ Then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about that, and he said: ‘Is it a military campaign?’ He said: ‘Yes!’ He said: ‘I do not know!’” Until God revealed: “Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds.” Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Qays ibn Sa`d, on the authority of `Ata’, regarding the statement of God: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night, “that a woman entered upon a man selling flour, and he kissed her, and he was discouraged. So he went to `Umar and mentioned that to him, and he said: Fear God, and do not be a woman who fights? The man said: She is a woman who fights! So he went to Abu Bakr and said the same as `Umar had said, and they all went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said the same to him, then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent and did not answer them,” so God revealed: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night, the obligatory prayers, “Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.” Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah informed me, saying: A woman came to a man who was selling flour to buy some from him. He entered the house with her, and when he was alone with him, he kissed her. He said: He was disappointed, so he went to Abu Bakr and mentioned that to him, and he said: Be careful, do not be the wife of a man who fights! While they were like that, the following verse was revealed concerning that: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. It was said to Ata’: Is it the obligatory prayer? He said: Yes, it is the obligatory prayer. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah ibn Kathir said: They are the obligatory prayers. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman: A man from the Prophet of Ghannam, a woman entered upon him, so he kissed her and put his hand on her anus. He came to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, then to Umar, may God be pleased with him, then to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this verse was revealed: Establish prayer, until His saying: That is a reminder for those who remember. So the man who kissed the woman did not stop remembering. This is what he said: A reminder for those who remember.
11:115: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And be patient, O Muhammad, with what you receive from the polytheists of your people of harm and dislike for the sake of God, hoping for a great reward from God for that, for God does not waste the reward of the work of one who does good and obeys God and follows His command, and defends Him with it, but rather He provides it for him when he is most in need of it.
11:116: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: “Why were there not among the generations whose story I have told you in these surahs, whom I destroyed for their disobedience to Me and their disbelief in My messengers, “before you those who had a remainder,” meaning: those who had a remainder of understanding and reason, who would consider God’s admonitions and ponder His proofs, and who would know what was for them in believing in God and what was against them in disbelief in Him, who forbade corruption on the earth, meaning: they forbade the people of sin from their sins, and the people of disbelief in God from their disbelief in Him, on His earth, except a few of those We saved from among them, meaning: there were not among the generations before you those who had a remainder who forbade corruption on the earth, except a few, for they used to forbid corruption on the earth, so God saved them from His punishment, when He punished those who persisted in disbelief in God, and they were the followers of the prophets and messengers. And the word little is in the accusative case because his saying, except a little, is an exception that is disconnected from what precedes it, just as he said, except the people of Jonah, when they believed. We have explained that in more than one place, so there is no need to repeat it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: He apologized and said: Why were there not among the generations before you until he reached except a few of those We saved from among them and so they were the ones who were saved when the punishment of God descended. And he recited: And those who did wrong pursued that in which they were luxurious. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: Why were there not among the generations before you those who had a remainder? to his statement: Except a few of those We saved from among them, he said: God considers them insignificant from among every people. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday narrated to us, on the authority of Dawud, he said: Bilal asked me about what al-Hasan said about predestination. He said: I heard al-Hasan say: “It was said, ‘O Noah, disembark with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon the peoples with you. But there are peoples whom We will grant enjoyment, then a painful punishment will touch them from Us.’” He said: God sent Hud to ‘Ad, so God saved Hud and those who believed with him, and those who granted enjoyment perished. God sent Salih to Thamud, so God saved Salih and those who granted enjoyment perished. So I began to ask the peoples about it, and he said: I do not think that he was anything but a good speaker about predestination. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Why were there not among the generations before you those of sound mind who would forbid corruption on the earth, except a few of those We saved from among them? That is, there were no people before you who forbade corruption on the earth, except a few of those We saved from among them. And His statement: And those who did wrong followed that in which they were luxurious, God Almighty says: And those who did wrong followed, meaning themselves, so they disbelieved in God, that in which they were luxurious. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said: And those who did wrong pursued that in which they were given luxury, he said: that in which they were given pleasure. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And those who did wrong pursued that in which they were given luxury, of their worldly life. It is as if these people interpreted the words: “And those who did wrong pursued the thing that their Lord had given them respite of the pleasures and delights of this world, preferring it over the work of the Hereafter and that which would save them from the punishment of God.” Others said: The meaning of this is: And those who did wrong followed the tyranny of the king, and they rebelled against the command of God. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: And those who did wrong pursued that in which they were luxurious, he said: In it is their kingship and their tyranny, and their abandonment of the truth. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar, except that he said: And they abandoned the truth. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same hadith of Muhammad bin Amr, exactly the same. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the statements on this matter is to say: God Almighty informed us: Those who wronged themselves from every nation that came before, and disbelieved in God, followed what they saw of worldly pleasures, so they were arrogant and disbelieved in God, and followed what they saw of worldly pleasures, so they were arrogant about God’s command, and were tyrannical and turned away from His path. This is because the pampered, in the speech of the Arabs, is the one who is pampered and has been nourished by pleasures, and from this is the saying of the rajaz poet: We dedicate the heads of the opulent ones to the Commander of the Faithful, the Eternal And his saying: And they were criminals, means: And they had acquired disbelief in God.
11:117: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And your Lord, O Muhammad, would not have destroyed the towns which He destroyed, the story of which He has told you, unjustly while their people were righteous in their deeds, not evildoers. So His destruction of them, while they were righteous in their deeds and obeyed their Lord, would have been unjust. Rather, He destroyed them because of the disbelief of their people in God, their persistence in their error, their denial of their messengers, and their committing evil deeds. It has been said: The meaning of this is: He would not have destroyed them because of their associating partners with God. This is what He said: in injustice meaning because of their associating partners with God, and its people are righteous, not oppressing one another, but rather they are dealing with justice among themselves, even if they are associating partners with God. He only destroys them if they oppress one another.
11:118: God Almighty says: And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community, but they will not cease to differ.
11:119: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: And if your Lord had willed, O Muhammad, He would have made all people one group, on one religion and one faith, as: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community. He says: He could have made them all Muslims. And His saying: And they will continue to differ, God Almighty says: And people will continue to differ except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the difference that God described people to be in. Some of them said: It is the difference in religions. The interpretation of that according to their doctrine is: People will continue to differ on various religions, between Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians, and so on. And those who said this statement said: God exempted from that those whom He had mercy on, and they are the people of faith. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Talha bin Amr, on the authority of Ata’: And they will not cease to differ, he said: The Jews, Christians, and Magians, and the Hanifis are those upon whom your Lord has had mercy. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Qubaysah told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Talha bin Amr, on the authority of Ata’: And they will not cease to differ, he said: the Jews, Christians, and Magians, except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy, he said: they are the Hanifis. Yaqub bin Ibrahim and Ibn Wakee’ told me, they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Mansur bin Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: I said to Hassan: What about his statement: And they will not cease to differ, except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy? He said: People differ over various religions, except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy, so those upon whom He has mercy do not differ. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Hasan ibn Salih, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: And they will not cease to differ, he said: the people of falsehood, except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy, he said: the people of truth. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And they will not cease to differ, he said: the people of falsehood, except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy, he said: the people of truth. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. He said, Ma'la bin Asad told us, Abdul Aziz told us, on the authority of Mansour bin Abdul Rahman, who said: Al-Hasan was asked about this verse: And they will not cease to differ, except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy. He said: All people differ in their various religions, except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy. So those upon whom He has mercy do not differ. So I said to him: And for that He created them? He said: He created these for His Paradise, and these for His Hellfire, and He created these for His mercy, and He created these for His punishment. He said, Ishaq told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa`d told us, Abu Ja`far told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And they will not cease to differ, he said: the people of falsehood, except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy, he said: the people of truth. He said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And they will not cease to differ, he said: the people of truth and the people of falsehood, except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy, he said: the people of truth. He said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us: Except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy, he said: The people of truth, there is no difference among them. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah: And they will not cease to differ, he said: the Jews and the Christians, except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy, he said: the people of the Qiblah. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Al-Hakam bin Abaan told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And they will not cease to differ, he said: the people of falsehood, except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy, he said: the people of truth. Hanad told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: And they will not cease to differ * Except whom your Lord has mercy upon, he said: They will not cease to differ in desire. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And they will not cease to differ * Except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy, so the people of God’s mercy are people of community, even if their homes and bodies are dispersed. And the people of His disobedience are people of division, even if their homes and bodies are united. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash: And they will not cease to differ * Except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy, he said: Those whom He made to be Muslims. He said, Abdul Aziz told us, Al-Hasan bin Wasil told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And they will not cease to differ, he said: the people of falsehood, except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy. He said, Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And they will not cease to differ, he said: the people of falsehood, except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy, he said: the people of truth. Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: They will continue to differ in terms of provision, as this one is poor and this one is rich. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father: Al-Hasan said: They differed in provision, some of them were made subservient to others. Some of them said: They differ in forgiveness and mercy, or something like that. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct interpretation of this is the statement of the one who said: The meaning of this is that people will continue to differ in their religions and desires, with different religions, sects and desires, except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy, who believe in God and believe in His Messengers, for they do not differ in the oneness of God, and the belief in His Messengers, and what came to them from God. I said: This is more correct in interpreting that, because God Almighty followed that with His saying: “And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: ‘I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together.’” In that is clear evidence that what preceded it of His mentioning the report of the people’s differences is only report of a blameworthy difference that necessitates Hellfire for them. If it had been report of their differences in provision, He would not have followed that with report of their punishment and torment. As for his saying: And for that He created them, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: It means: He created them for the sake of difference. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Mubarak bin Fadala, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And for that He created them, he said: for the difference. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Mansur bin Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: I said to al-Hasan: And for this He created them, so he said: He created these for His Paradise, and He created these for His Hell, and He created these for His mercy, and He created these for His punishment. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Mualla bin Asad told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, on the authority of Mansour bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Al-Hasan, something similar. He said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’: that Al-Hasan said regarding this verse: And for that He created them, he said: He created these for this, and He created these for this. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Hudha bin Khalifa told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: And for that He created them, he said: As for the people of God’s mercy, they do not differ in a way that harms them. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And for this He created them, he said: He created them into two groups, a group that is merciful and does not differ, and a group that is not merciful and differs, and that is His statement: And among them is the wretched and the happy. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Talha bin Amr, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement: And they will not cease to differ, he said: Jews, Christians, and Magians, Except for whom your Lord has mercy, he said: Those whom He made a Muslim, And for that He created them, he said: Believers and disbelievers. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us: And for this He created them, he said: Believers and disbelievers. Yunus told me, he said, Ashhab told us, he said: Malik was asked about the statement of God: And they will not cease to differ * Except whom your Lord has mercy upon, and for that He created them, he said: He created them to be two groups: a group in Paradise, and a group in the Blaze. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And for mercy He created them. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Hasan ibn Salih, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: And for that He created them, he said: for mercy. Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: And for that He created them, he said: for mercy. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa`d told us, he said, Abu Hafs told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, the same, except that he said: He created them for mercy. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And for that He created them, he said: He created them for mercy. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of the one who mentioned it, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: And for that He created them, he said: for mercy. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Al-Hakam bin Abaan told me, on the authority of Ikrimah: And for that He created them, he said: The people of truth and those who follow Him, for His mercy. Saad bin Abdullah told me, he said, Hafs bin Omar told us, he said, Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “And they will not cease to differ * Except whom your Lord has mercy upon. And for that,” he said: He created them for mercy, and did not create them for punishment. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said: And for the difference in misery and happiness He created them, because God, may He be glorified and exalted, mentioned two types of His creation: one of them is the people of difference and falsehood, and the other is the people of truth. Then He followed that with His saying: And for that He created them, so He made His saying: And for that He created them, a description of the two types, so He informed about each group of them that it is facilitated for what it was created for. If someone says: If the interpretation of that is as you mentioned, then it is appropriate that those who differ should not be blamed for their differences, since that is why their Lord created them, and that those who enjoy themselves should be blamed? It was said: The meaning of this is contrary to what you have gone to, and the meaning of the statement is: And people will continue to differ in falsehood in their religions and sects, except for whom your Lord has mercy, so this is for the truth, and for His knowledge, and based on His knowledge that penetrates them before He created them, that there will be among them the believer and the disbeliever, the wretched and the happy, He created them, so the meaning of the lam in His statement: And for that He created them, is in the sense of based, like you saying to a man: I honored you for your righteousness to Me, and I honored you for your righteousness to Me.
