As for his saying: “And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: ‘I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together,’” it is because of his prior knowledge that they deserve to be burned there because of their disbelief in God and their disobedience to His command. His saying: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled, is an oath like the saying of someone who says: I swore to visit you, and it occurred to me that I would come to you. That is why I received it with the lam of the oath. His saying: From Paradise, which is what is hidden from the sight of the children of Adam, and people, meaning: and the children of Adam. It was said that they were called Paradise because they were in Paradise. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Saddī, on the authority of Abu Malik: They were called Paradise because they were in Paradise, and all the angels are Paradise. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, he said, Paradise means the angels. As for the meaning of what Abu Malik said: that Iblis was one of the angels, and the jinn are his offspring, and that the angels are called jinn in his view, this is because I have explained previously in this book of ours.
11:120: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And We relate to you, O Muhammad, of the report of the messengers, who were before you, that by which We strengthen your heart, so do not be alarmed by the denial of those among your people who have denied you, and the rejection of what you have brought them, and do not let your chest be constricted, so that you abandon some of what was revealed to you because they said: Why was a treasure not sent down to him or an angel brought with him? if you know what those of My messengers before you from their nations encountered, such as: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: And We relate to you from the report of the messengers what will strengthen your heart, he said: So that you may know what the messengers before you encountered from their nations. The Arab scholars differed on the reason for the accusative case of Kula. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is in the accusative case, meaning: And We relate to you from the report of the messengers what will strengthen your heart, both, as if the whole is in the accusative case according to him as a source of deficiency, with the interpretation: And We relate to you all of that story. Some Arabists have denied this, saying: This is not permissible. He said: The reason for placing both in the accusative case is deficiency because both is built on addition, whether there is an addition with it or not. He said: He meant: All of it is deficient for you, and he made what we affirm a response to both. I have explained the correct statement in this regard. As for his saying: And the truth has come to you in this, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of it. Some of them said: It means: The truth has come to you in this Surah. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Ja’far, on the authority of Abu Iyas, on the authority of Abu Musa: And the truth has come to you in this, he said: in this surah. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ja’far, on the authority of Abu Iyas Mu’awiyah ibn Qurrah, on the authority of Abu Musa, the same. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Saeed bin Aamer told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And the truth has come to you in this, he said: in this surah. Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Abu Awana, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Amr Al-Anbari, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the truth has come to you in this, he said: in this surah. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Abu Awana, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of a man from Banu Al-Anbar, who said: Ibn Abbas addressed us and said: And the truth has come to you in this, he said: In this surah. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, he said: I heard Ibn Abbas reciting this surah to the people, until he reached: And the truth has come to you in this, he said: In this surah. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Marwan Al-Asghar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: that he read on the pulpit: And the truth has come to you in this, and he said: In this surah. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: And the truth has come to you in this, he said: in this surah. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And it came to you in this surah. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar Al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, who said: This is the surah. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa`id told us, he said, Abu Ja`far al-Razi told us, on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas, the same. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Abu Raja’ told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And the truth has come to you in this, he said: in this surah. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Abaan bin Taghlib, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And the truth has come to you in this, he said: in this surah. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: I heard Al-Hasan Al-Basri say regarding the statement of God: And the truth has come to you in this, he said: He means: in this surah. Others said: The meaning of this is: The truth has come to you in this world. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar and Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, they said, Muhammad bin Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the truth has come to you in this world, he said: in this world. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Qatada: And the truth has come to you in this world, he said: Al-Hasan used to say: in this world. Abu Jaafar said: The most correct of the two interpretations in interpreting this is the statement of the one who said: And the truth has come to you in this surah, because the proof from the people of interpretation has agreed that this is its interpretation. If someone says: Did the truth not come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the surahs of the Qur’an except in this surah? It is said: And did the truth come to you in this surah? He was told: Yes, it has all come to pass. If he said: Then what is the reason for his being specific in this surah with his saying: And the truth has come to you in this? It was said: The meaning of the statement is: And the truth has come to you in this surah, along with what has come to you in the rest of the surahs of the Qur’an - or: to what has come to you of the truth in the rest of the surahs of the Qur’an - not that its meaning is: And the truth has come to you in this surah, without the rest of the surahs of the Qur’an. And His saying: And an admonition, meaning: And there has come to you an admonition that admonishes the ignorant of God, and shows them a lesson from those who disbelieved in Him and denied His messengers. And a reminder for the believers, meaning: And a reminder that reminds the believers of God and His messengers, so that they do not neglect what is due to God upon them.
11:121: God Almighty said: And say to those who do not believe, ‘Work according to your position, for we are working.’
11:122: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And say, O Muhammad, to those who do not believe you and do not acknowledge the Oneness of God, ‘Work according to your position,’ meaning: Despite your weakness and your ability to do what you are doing, we will do what we are doing of the deeds that God has commanded us to do, and await what Satan has promised you, for we are awaiting what God has promised us of war against you and our victory over you, as: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: “And wait, for we are waiting,” he said: He says: Wait for the promises that Satan makes to you based on what he makes attractive to you, for we are waiting.
11:123: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: To God, O Muhammad, is the kingdom of everything that is hidden from you in the heavens and the earth, which you did not see or know. All of that is in His hand and with His knowledge. Nothing of it is hidden from Him. He knows what the polytheists of your people do, and to Him will come the end of their affair, whether they remain in polytheism or abandon it and repent. And to Him will return the whole affair, meaning: To God is the return of every worker and his work, and He will reward all of them for their deeds, as: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And to Him returns the whole matter, he said: So He judges between them with His judgment and justice. Worship Him, meaning: worship your Lord, O Muhammad, and put your trust in Him, meaning: entrust your affair to Him, and trust in Him and in His sufficiency, for He is sufficient for whoever puts his trust in Him. And His statement: And your Lord is not unaware of what you do, God Almighty says: And your Lord, O Muhammad, is not unaware of what these polytheists among your people do, but rather He encompasses it, nothing of it escapes Him, and He is watching them, so do not be saddened by their turning away from you, nor by their denying the truth that you have brought, and proceed with the command of your Lord, for you are in Our sight. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, on the authority of Ja’far bin Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Imran Al-Joni, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rabah, on the authority of Ka’b, who said: The conclusion of the Torah is the conclusion of Hud.
